title: vta-service-v0.57.0
body:
### Added

- **rooms**: Room files — file keys, STREAM sealing and rooms/keys/file-key ([#2017](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2017))

* feat(rooms): file keys, STREAM sealing and blob manifests in vti-rooms

  Adds vti_rooms::files, the construction rooms/_shared/0.1/blobs.schema.json FileManifest specifies (trust-tasks-tf #739): a per-file key, HKDF-SHA256 over the epoch storage key salted with the fileId and bound to the room and epoch; ChaCha20-Poly1305 STREAM segments whose nonce counts and whose associated data carries the final flag, so truncation, reordering and splicing fail to authenticate; one sealed segment per transfer chunk; the blob manifest and its BlobRef (sha2-256 over JCS); Padmé padding; and streaming sealer and opener that refuse a file whose plaintext digest is not the one its author signed. The manifest and digests build without the mls feature so a host can check them; the keyed half is behind mls with the rest of the member half. SealedRoom gains file_key_for_seal and file_key_for_open, walking the epoch chain as open_record does. Test vectors in vti-rooms/tests/fixtures/file-vectors.json.

- **vta**: External accounts — short-lived provider credentials with no inbound surface ([#2016](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2016))

* feat(vta): external-accounts capabilities and keyspaces

  Adds the two capabilities the external/* family (trust-tasks-tf #740) gates on: external-accounts-manage, derived by admin alone, and external-auth-use, derived by every role that holds sign (the account's binding, not the role, bounds a consumer). Both are non-additive members of the non-exhaustive Capability enum.

  Registers two keyspaces: external_accounts (settings, bindings, state) in BACKED_UP, and external_secrets (wrapped provider secrets) in EXCLUDED_FROM_BACKUP, so a portable password-protected backup is never a way to take a provider secret away. DID deletion: an account's binding names its consumer, so external_accounts blocks; external_secrets is unrelated.

  The device-binding Capability registry (device/_shared 0.2) does not list the two yet, so device listings carry them under ext until it does.

- Verify ES256 / ES256K SD-JWT-VCs from did:web and did:webvh issuers ([#1988](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1988)) ([#2010](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2010))

Credentials issued on the swiyu stack and the EUDI profiles could not be
  received or verified: the vault and the VTC verifier accepted only EdDSA,
  the vault only a `did:key` issuer, the shared resolver only a
  `publicKeyMultibase` key, and holder binding only an Ed25519 `cnf.jwk`.

  - `vta_sdk::jws` (new): compact-JWS verification over a resolved key —
    EdDSA, ES256 (P-256) and ES256K (secp256k1). The header's `alg` must be
    the one the resolved key's curve signs with, checked before the
    signature; `crit` is refused. `JwsKey::from_jwk` reads a `cnf.jwk`
    (refusing one that carries `d`), `did_key()` names a P-256 holder
    `did:key:zDn…` and a secp256k1 one `did:key:zQ3s…`.
    `sd_jwt_issuer_method` binds the issuer JWS `kid` to `iss`: a `did:key`
    issuer's own key whatever the fragment, any other DID must name its
    method with a DID-URL `kid` (VTI-CRD-002: the issuer is resolved, not
    guessed).
  - `TrustTaskVmResolver` reads a `publicKeyJwk` method (Ed25519, X25519,
    P-256, secp256k1) and a secp256k1 Multikey; PQC keys stay Multikey-only.
  - `vta-vault`: `receive_sd_jwt_vc` and `stored_claims` take the issuer
    resolver, so a `did:web` / `did:webvh` issuer resolves for
    `assertionMethod`. `receive` with `IssuerKey::None` resolves locally
    (`did:key` / `did:peer`); the VTA's issued-credential path passes its DID
    cache. A credential carrying an IETF `status.status_list` reference is
    stored `Unknown`, not `Valid`: no `statuslist+jwt` resolver exists yet, so
    its status cannot be read (VTI-CRD-012).
  - `vtc-service`: the SD-JWT-VC presentation verifier takes ES256 / ES256K
    issuers and P-256 / secp256k1 `cnf.jwk` holders.

- **vta-sdk**: Wallet sign-in with a trigger link: sign auth/oob grants, enrol UV keys, advertise TrustTaskHTTPS and SignInPortal ([#1997](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1997))

* feat(vta-sdk)!: sign auth/oob/grant for assertionMethod (VTI-KEY-106)

  Adds `auth/oob/grant` to `ATTESTATION_SLUGS`, so `vault/sign-trust-task`
  signs a wallet sign-in grant for `assertionMethod`: the grant ("let this
  browser key act as me at this origin until notAfter") is the approving
  DID's attestation, which the service relies on to open a session, and it
  verifies the grant against `assertionMethod` (sign-in trigger-link
  contract C5, base design §10).

  `auth/oob/identify` stays operational and is signed for `authentication`,
  as the service verifies it; the other `auth/oob` documents are not
  attestations either. Both are pinned in the classifier tests.



### Build & CI

- Trust-tasks-rs 0.28, affinidi-messaging-sdk 0.34 and affinidi-tdk 0.24 ([#2028](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2028))

Moves the workspace to trust-tasks-rs 0.28 (with capability-client, https,
  didcomm, tsp and proof) in lockstep with the Affinidi messaging crates built
  against it (affinidi-tdk-rs #933): affinidi-messaging-sdk 0.34, affinidi-tdk
  0.24, mediator-admin / mediator-tui 0.9 (pnm messaging console) and
  test-mediator 0.20. The lock holds one trust-tasks-rs, one trust-tasks-proof,
  one SDK and one tdk: `MediatorAcl` crosses the SDK's API, so a graph holding
  two trust-tasks-rs does not compile.

  0.28's one break, the rooms 0.1 `NOT_AUTHORIZED` constants withdrawn for the
  standard `permissionDenied` (trust-tasks-tf #743), touches nothing here: the
  room host already answers `permissionDenied`.

  It carries `DeclaredErrorCode::details_schema` / `check_details`
  (trust-tasks-tf #742), so the rooms/keys/file-key handler tests check
  `unknownEpoch` details against the schema the specification declares rather
  than a hand copy, and vta-service's jsonschema dev-dependency, which existed
  only for that copy, is dropped.

  Publishing a vta-sdk on SDK 0.34 / tdk 0.24 is step 2 of the crossing
  affinidi-tdk-rs's workspace-duplicates-allow.txt records; step 3 moves the
  mediator's vta-sdk requirement to it there.

- Trust-tasks-rs 0.27.8, with auth/oob on its generated types ([#2011](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2011))

* build: trust-tasks-rs 0.27.8 — auth/oob, room files and external accounts



### Fixed

- **auth**: Bound wallet sign-in sessions by the grant's notAfter across refresh ([#2026](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2026))

A wallet sign-in (`auth/oob/*`) grant carries `notAfter`, the latest
  moment the member approved the session for, and redeem reports it. The
  member-portal mint clamped only the first window to it — the comment
  "refreshing cannot extend it" was false: `handle_refresh` reset both
  expiries to now + the full TTL on every rotation, so a session approved
  for an hour could be renewed indefinitely. The console session minted by
  wallet sign-in (`mint_admin_cookie_session`, #2014) ignored `notAfter`
  entirely, and reported the refresh deadline as `notAfter`.

- **vta**: Check an extension passkey's rpIdHash against its chrome-extension:// origin ([#2020](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2020))

Chrome requires an extension to pass its bare runtime id as rp.id but
  signs the assertion over SHA-256("chrome-extension://<id>"), so every
  browser-plugin grant was refused with oobUvInvalid ("authenticatorData.rpIdHash
  does not match expected rp_id"). Verify an extension passkey against its
  origin; web passkeys and stored enrolments are unchanged.



### Performance

- **vta-service**: Multi-core REST and direct vsock inbound, failing closed ([#2005](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2005))

* perf(vta-service): serve REST on one worker per CPU

  The REST server ran on its own current-thread tokio runtime, so every REST
  handler shared one thread and the VTA could use at most one CPU however
  many it had. In a Nitro enclave this showed as a 2-vCPU enclave half idle at
  its ceiling (47%/62% per vCPU), with storage replies waiting for that one
  thread to poll them.

  With more than one CPU the REST runtime is now multi-threaded, one worker
  per CPU. With one CPU it stays current-thread: a multi-threaded runtime was
  measurably worse there (1-vCPU enclave at 220 keys/sign per second: 463
  errors against 2).

  Measured alone on c6g.4xlarge with a 2-vCPU enclave, in builds with extra
  timing logging and an audit-key cache not in this series: at 320/s p95
  840 -> 71 ms. With this series as it stands, c6g.4xlarge saturates at about
  345/s with a 2-vCPU enclave and about 380 to 400/s with a 4-vCPU enclave.

  Review note: handlers that interleaved only at await points now also run in
  parallel. Existing non-atomic read-modify-write sequences were already racy
  across await points; this makes those races more likely.

- **vta-service**: Fewer storage reads per keys/sign without widening key custody ([#2001](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2001))

* perf(vta-service): read the caller's ACL entry once per keys/sign

  sign_payload read the caller's ACL entry twice: once for the sign
  capability (gate 0) and again for the allowed-keys filter (gate 4). The
  entry from gate 0 is now passed to gate 4, which reads it itself only when
  gate 0 did not run (protocol-defined signing input). Both gates still run,
  in the same order, and now see the same version of the entry.

  One storage round trip fewer per keys/sign.

title: vta-vault-v0.16.0
body:
### Added

- Read IETF Token Status Lists for SD-JWT VCs, signed by the credential's issuer ([#1988](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1988)) ([#2015](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2015))

An SD-JWT VC from the swiyu stack or an EUDI issuer names its status as
  `status.status_list = { idx, uri }`, a `statuslist+jwt`. The VTC fed that
  reference to the W3C Bitstring fetcher, which could never read it (Unknown at
  every join), and the vault held such credentials Unknown for good. Both now
  read it, through affinidi-status-list 0.1.7's `token` module.

  - `vta_sdk::token_status_list` (new): `verify_status_list_token` and
    `resolve_token_status`. A list decides revocation, so it is trusted only as
    the credential issuer's: the token's `kid` must name one of that issuer's
    `assertionMethod` keys (`sd_jwt_issuer_method`), the signature is checked
    with that key's algorithm (`JwsKey`) before the payload is read, and an
    `iss` naming anyone else is refused. `typ`, `sub` = the referenced `uri`,
    `iat` and `exp` are checked by the TDK, and the list is decompressed under
    a cap. The fetch is SSRF-guarded, takes no redirects and caps the body. A
    separate Status Issuer linked by certificate chain (draft §13.5) is not
    supported; its lists are refused.
  - `vta-vault`: `StatusListResolver::resolve_token_status` (a defaulted method,
    so existing resolvers compile and refuse) is implemented by
    `HttpStatusListResolver`. `refresh_status`, which the present gate runs
    first, takes the Token path when a credential carries `status.status_list`
    and no W3C `credentialStatus`: `INVALID` → `Revoked` (terminal),
    `SUSPENDED` → `Revoked` tagged `tokenStatus:suspended` so a later `VALID`
    restores it, an application-specific or unregistered value → `Unknown`
    (VTI-CRD-012). Receive still stores such a credential `Unknown`: its status
    has not been read until that refresh.
  - `vtc-service`: `StatusListFetcher::check_token_status`, implemented by the
    verifying `HttpStatusListFetcher`. `resolve_presented_status` (join, join
    criteria, invitations) maps `VALID` / `INVALID` / `SUSPENDED` to Valid /
    Revoked / Suspended, and anything unreadable to Unknown for the join policy.
  - `affinidi-status-list` 0.1.3 → 0.1.7. `docs/03-vtc/credentials.md` gains
    *Reading another issuer's status*.

- Verify ES256 / ES256K SD-JWT-VCs from did:web and did:webvh issuers ([#1988](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1988)) ([#2010](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2010))

Credentials issued on the swiyu stack and the EUDI profiles could not be
  received or verified: the vault and the VTC verifier accepted only EdDSA,
  the vault only a `did:key` issuer, the shared resolver only a
  `publicKeyMultibase` key, and holder binding only an Ed25519 `cnf.jwk`.

  - `vta_sdk::jws` (new): compact-JWS verification over a resolved key —
    EdDSA, ES256 (P-256) and ES256K (secp256k1). The header's `alg` must be
    the one the resolved key's curve signs with, checked before the
    signature; `crit` is refused. `JwsKey::from_jwk` reads a `cnf.jwk`
    (refusing one that carries `d`), `did_key()` names a P-256 holder
    `did:key:zDn…` and a secp256k1 one `did:key:zQ3s…`.
    `sd_jwt_issuer_method` binds the issuer JWS `kid` to `iss`: a `did:key`
    issuer's own key whatever the fragment, any other DID must name its
    method with a DID-URL `kid` (VTI-CRD-002: the issuer is resolved, not
    guessed).
  - `TrustTaskVmResolver` reads a `publicKeyJwk` method (Ed25519, X25519,
    P-256, secp256k1) and a secp256k1 Multikey; PQC keys stay Multikey-only.
  - `vta-vault`: `receive_sd_jwt_vc` and `stored_claims` take the issuer
    resolver, so a `did:web` / `did:webvh` issuer resolves for
    `assertionMethod`. `receive` with `IssuerKey::None` resolves locally
    (`did:key` / `did:peer`); the VTA's issued-credential path passes its DID
    cache. A credential carrying an IETF `status.status_list` reference is
    stored `Unknown`, not `Valid`: no `statuslist+jwt` resolver exists yet, so
    its status cannot be read (VTI-CRD-012).
  - `vtc-service`: the SD-JWT-VC presentation verifier takes ES256 / ES256K
    issuers and P-256 / secp256k1 `cnf.jwk` holders.

title: feat(rooms): pnm rooms file put/get, and signed sealed bodies for rooms put/get
body:
A member can now put a file in a sealed room and fetch it from the CLI, end to end (`data-rooms-files.md` P6). `pnm rooms put` and `get` also work on sealed rooms.

**Spec first:** the sealed record body this writes and reads was undefined. It's now `SealedRecordBody` in `rooms/_shared/0.1/room.schema.json`, from trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#747 (merged). No `trust-tasks-rs` bump is needed: no host task carries the body, so there's no generated type for it (like `FileManifest`).

### What's in it
- **`vtc_client::rooms::body`**: `SealedRecordBody`, signed by its author (Data Integrity, `eddsa-jcs-2022` / `ecdsa-jcs-2019`) and naming the room, key and version it was written for. `verify_record_body` is the only way to a `VerifiedRecordBody`. It refuses (never warns) on:
  - an unknown member or a broken bound;
  - a bad or foreign-suite proof;
  - a relocated body;
  - on `attributed`, a signer other than the host-recorded author.
- **`pnm rooms put` on sealed rooms**: reads the tier (`rooms/info`), signs the body, and has the VTA seal it (`rooms/keys/seal`). The VTA signs nothing.
  - Versions come from a room-wide counter, so a put that lands at an unpredicted version is re-sealed and rewritten over exactly what landed (≤ 4 tries), then reported with the `--expected-version` to use.
  - Without a file, `put` and `get` stay on records 0.1, which the VTC serves.
- **`pnm rooms get`**: verifies the body before showing it. It also reads `sealed` as the object hosts actually return; it treated it as a string, so it could open no sealed record.
- **`pnm rooms file put / get`**: sealed and opened locally with one file's key (`rooms/keys/file-key`); the bytes never pass through the VTA. `get` writes nothing unless every check holds:
  - the record's signed body;
  - the blob is the one the author named;
  - each chunk matches the manifest;
  - the plaintext matches the author's digest.

  Untrusted names and text are made inert, and nothing is ever written over an existing file.
- **Clients**:
  - `vtc-client` blob upload/download, `room_info`, `get_record_v2`, `put_sealed_record_with_blobs`, on the generated `trust_tasks_rs` types;
  - `VtaClient::room_seal`;
  - `trust_task_sign::sign_object_for_assertion`.

### Not yet
Files need `rooms/records/put` 0.2, which `room-host` serves and the VTC doesn't yet (next: P5 in `vtc-service`). `put` reads a file whole into memory; streaming can come with the portal work.

### Tests
- `room-host`: the whole file path through the real client against the host served on a socket (upload, put with a signed body, `get` 0.2, verify, download, open).
- The body's refusals (7 tests) and the CLI's text and file-name handling.
- Full CI-equivalent run: 5,624/5,625 workspace tests passed. The exception was `vta-backup`'s `every_backed_up_keyspace_survives_a_round_trip`, which hit the 300 s limit under load and passed alone in 37 s. 2,973/2,973 vtc tests and doctests passed. The fmt and clippy findings that run reported are fixed in this commit.

body:
feat(rooms): pnm rooms file put/get, and signed sealed bodies for rooms put/get (#2037)

A member can now put a file in a sealed room and fetch it from the CLI, end to
end (data-rooms-files.md P6), and `pnm rooms put`/`get` work on sealed rooms.

Sealed record body (vtc_client::rooms::body). This implements
`SealedRecordBody` (rooms/_shared/0.1/room.schema.json,
trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#747): the JSON inside a sealed record. It is
signed by its author with a Data Integrity proof (eddsa-jcs-2022, or
ecdsa-jcs-2019 for P-256) and names the room, key and version it was written
for. `verify_record_body` is the only way to a `VerifiedRecordBody`. It
refuses, rather than warns about, a body that:
- names an unknown member or breaks a bound;
- carries a proof that does not verify for `author` for assertionMethod, or
  uses another suite;
- was signed for another location;
- on attributed, was signed by someone other than the author the host recorded.
There is no generated type for the body, because no host task carries it (the
same as FileManifest).

pnm rooms put on a sealed room:
- reads the tier from `rooms/info`, signs the body as the operator, and seals
  it through the VTA's `rooms/keys/seal`, which seals what it is given and
  signs nothing;
- predicts the version from the room head. The host assigns versions from a
  room-wide counter, so a write that lands at another version is re-sealed at
  the next one and rewritten over exactly what landed, up to 4 times, then
  named with the --expected-version to retry with.
Without a file, `put` and `get` stay on records 0.1, which the VTC host serves.

pnm rooms get:
- verifies the sealed body before showing it;
- reads `sealed` as the object the host returns. It had read it as a bare
  string, so it could open no sealed record.

pnm rooms file put/get. A file is sealed and opened locally with one file's
key from the VTA. `put` seals the file, uploads its ciphertext (begin, the
missing chunks, commit; abort on failure), checks the committed blobRef, then
writes a create-only record (records/put 0.2) whose signed body carries the
FileManifest. `get` writes nothing unless every check holds:
- the body is verified;
- the blob is named on the record and is the one the author named;
- each chunk matches the manifest;
- the plaintext matches the author's digest.
Another member's text has control characters stripped, and a file name keeps
only its last path component, never written over an existing file. Files need
records/put 0.2, which room-host serves and the VTC does not yet.

Client calls:
- vtc-client: begin/upload/commit/abort, get_blob/download_chunk, room_info,
  get_record_v2 and put_sealed_record_with_blobs, on the generated
  trust_tasks_rs types;
- vta-sdk: VtaClient::room_seal, and
  trust_task_sign::sign_object_for_assertion for signing an object that is
  not a Trust Task.

Tests:
- room-host: the whole file path through the real client, against the host
  served on a socket;
- the body's refusals;
- the CLI's text and file-name handling.

title: feat(vta-sdk)!: foreign-protocol DID identities — JWK key slots, an unpublished update key, P-256 slots, and a swiyu-verifier template (#1988)
body:
A VTC that verifies swiyu wallet presentations (OpenID4VP) needs an identity of
its own, shaped by the Swiss Profile Anchor: a did:webvh with one P-256 key
published as a publicKeyJwk (publicKeyMultibase is forbidden), no keyAgreement,
service or @context, the Ed25519 update key kept to the log's updateKeys, and
portable=false. DID templates could express none of that. This adds what they
were missing, and the template.

- `{SLOT}_KEY_JWK`: every key slot now also renders as a JWK object (kty, crv,
  x, y, alg), beside `{SLOT}_KEY_MB`. Either publishes the slot; a JWK
  placeholder for an undeclared slot, or declared as a variable, is refused
  like its multibase twin.
- `KeySlot::publish` (default true; **breaking** — a new public field). Only the
  `signing` slot, the did:webvh update key, may be `publish: false`, and then
  the document must not use it. Its key record is named by its did:key, as the
  log names it, instead of a guessed `#key-0`.
- Templates that declare slots but no `ka` slot get no key-agreement key
  published or recorded.
- Additional signing slots may be P-256 (`derive_p256`'s domain-separated
  derivation).
- `defaults.portable: false` is binding: the VTA mints the DID non-portable
  whatever the caller asked (pnm defaults to true). Only that direction.
- Minted key records are matched to the document by publicKeyJwk as well as
  publicKeyMultibase.
- Built-in `swiyu-verifier` template. Mint it serverless at the swiyu
  identifier-registry slot URL, then upload the log to that slot.

CLAUDE.md: the key policy now allows P-256 / secp256k1 for foreign-protocol
identities, still VTA-minted and custodied, published only in that identity's
own DID. docs/02-vta/did-templates.md documents the JWK placeholder, `publish`,
the binding portable default and the template.

Tests: the swiyu-verifier template minted end to end — the signed log state has
one JsonWebKey2020 P-256 key under authentication and assertionMethod, no
publicKeyMultibase, keyAgreement, service, alsoKnownAs or @context, portable
false, the P-256 and update-key records stored; template validation for JWK
slots and `publish`.

P2 of docs/05-design-notes/oid4vp-wallet-verifier.md.

title: vta-sdk-v0.65.1
body:
### Fixed

- **vta-service**: Omit highWatermark for an unwritten app-state namespace ([#2033](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2033))

`vta/app-state/list` reported the namespace counter as `highWatermark`
  even when nothing had been written, emitting 0. The response schema types
  it as a `Version` (minimum 1), so MockVta's conformance check answered
  `responseSchemaViolation` and every consumer's first sync against an empty
  namespace failed; a production VTA sent the non-conformant reply anyway.

  With no writes there is no watermark, so the member is now absent. It is
  not in `required`, and a consumer keeps the `sinceVersion` it sent, which
  is the same answer.

  Adds a client/server round-trip test covering both list modes on an empty
  namespace and the watermark after the first write.

body:
## 🤖 New release * `vta-sdk`: 0.65.0 -> 0.65.1 (✓ API compatible changes) * `vti-common`: 0.41.0 -> 0.41.1 (✓ API compatible changes) * `cnm-cli`: 0.31.0 -> 0.31.1 * `pnm-cli`: 0.37.0 -> 0.37.1 * `vta-external`: 0.1.0 * `vta-persona`: 0.17.0 -> 0.18.0 * `vta-policy`: 0.12.0 -> 0.13.0 * `vta-vault`: 0.15.0 -> 0.16.0 * `vta-sweepers`: 0.12.0 -> 0.13.0 * `vta-tee`: 0.16.0 -> 0.17.0 * `vta-webvh`: 0.13.0 -> 0.14.0 * `vta-service`: 0.56.0 -> 0.57.0
Changelog

## `vta-sdk`

## [0.65.1](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/compare/vta-sdk-v0.65.0...vta-sdk-v0.65.1) — 2026-10-11 ### Fixed - **vta-service**: Omit highWatermark for an unwritten app-state namespace ([#2033](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2033)) `vta/app-state/list` reported the namespace counter as `highWatermark` even when nothing had been written, emitting 0. The response schema types it as a `Version` (minimum 1), so MockVta's conformance check answered `responseSchemaViolation` and every consumer's first sync against an empty namespace failed; a production VTA sent the non-conformant reply anyway. With no writes there is no watermark, so the member is now absent. It is not in `required`, and a consumer keeps the `sinceVersion` it sent, which is the same answer. Adds a client/server round-trip test covering both list modes on an empty namespace and the watermark after the first write.
## `vti-common`
## [0.41.1](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/compare/vti-common-v0.41.0...vti-common-v0.41.1) — 2026-10-11 ### Added - **vti-common**: Log each TSP reply sent, with its route and timing ([#2032](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2032))
## `vta-external`
## [0.1.0](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/releases/tag/vta-external-v0.1.0) — 2026-10-11 ### Added - **vta**: External accounts — short-lived provider credentials with no inbound surface ([#2016](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2016)) * feat(vta): external-accounts capabilities and keyspaces Adds the two capabilities the external/* family (trust-tasks-tf #740) gates on: external-accounts-manage, derived by admin alone, and external-auth-use, derived by every role that holds sign (the account's binding, not the role, bounds a consumer). Both are non-additive members of the non-exhaustive Capability enum. Registers two keyspaces: external_accounts (settings, bindings, state) in BACKED_UP, and external_secrets (wrapped provider secrets) in EXCLUDED_FROM_BACKUP, so a portable password-protected backup is never a way to take a provider secret away. DID deletion: an account's binding names its consumer, so external_accounts blocks; external_secrets is unrelated. The device-binding Capability registry (device/_shared 0.2) does not list the two yet, so device listings carry them under ext until it does.
## `vta-vault`
## [0.16.0](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/compare/vta-vault-v0.15.0...vta-vault-v0.16.0) — 2026-10-11 ### Added - Read IETF Token Status Lists for SD-JWT VCs, signed by the credential's issuer ([#1988](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1988)) ([#2015](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2015)) An SD-JWT VC from the swiyu stack or an EUDI issuer names its status as `status.status_list = { idx, uri }`, a `statuslist+jwt`. The VTC fed that reference to the W3C Bitstring fetcher, which could never read it (Unknown at every join), and the vault held such credentials Unknown for good. Both now read it, through affinidi-status-list 0.1.7's `token` module. - `vta_sdk::token_status_list` (new): `verify_status_list_token` and `resolve_token_status`. A list decides revocation, so it is trusted only as the credential issuer's: the token's `kid` must name one of that issuer's `assertionMethod` keys (`sd_jwt_issuer_method`), the signature is checked with that key's algorithm (`JwsKey`) before the payload is read, and an `iss` naming anyone else is refused. `typ`, `sub` = the referenced `uri`, `iat` and `exp` are checked by the TDK, and the list is decompressed under a cap. The fetch is SSRF-guarded, takes no redirects and caps the body. A separate Status Issuer linked by certificate chain (draft §13.5) is not supported; its lists are refused. - `vta-vault`: `StatusListResolver::resolve_token_status` (a defaulted method, so existing resolvers compile and refuse) is implemented by `HttpStatusListResolver`. `refresh_status`, which the present gate runs first, takes the Token path when a credential carries `status.status_list` and no W3C `credentialStatus`: `INVALID` → `Revoked` (terminal), `SUSPENDED` → `Revoked` tagged `tokenStatus:suspended` so a later `VALID` restores it, an application-specific or unregistered value → `Unknown` (VTI-CRD-012). Receive still stores such a credential `Unknown`: its status has not been read until that refresh. - `vtc-service`: `StatusListFetcher::check_token_status`, implemented by the verifying `HttpStatusListFetcher`. `resolve_presented_status` (join, join criteria, invitations) maps `VALID` / `INVALID` / `SUSPENDED` to Valid / Revoked / Suspended, and anything unreadable to Unknown for the join policy. - `affinidi-status-list` 0.1.3 → 0.1.7. `docs/03-vtc/credentials.md` gains *Reading another issuer's status*. - Verify ES256 / ES256K SD-JWT-VCs from did:web and did:webvh issuers ([#1988](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1988)) ([#2010](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2010)) Credentials issued on the swiyu stack and the EUDI profiles could not be received or verified: the vault and the VTC verifier accepted only EdDSA, the vault only a `did:key` issuer, the shared resolver only a `publicKeyMultibase` key, and holder binding only an Ed25519 `cnf.jwk`. - `vta_sdk::jws` (new): compact-JWS verification over a resolved key — EdDSA, ES256 (P-256) and ES256K (secp256k1). The header's `alg` must be the one the resolved key's curve signs with, checked before the signature; `crit` is refused. `JwsKey::from_jwk` reads a `cnf.jwk` (refusing one that carries `d`), `did_key()` names a P-256 holder `did:key:zDn…` and a secp256k1 one `did:key:zQ3s…`. `sd_jwt_issuer_method` binds the issuer JWS `kid` to `iss`: a `did:key` issuer's own key whatever the fragment, any other DID must name its method with a DID-URL `kid` (VTI-CRD-002: the issuer is resolved, not guessed). - `TrustTaskVmResolver` reads a `publicKeyJwk` method (Ed25519, X25519, P-256, secp256k1) and a secp256k1 Multikey; PQC keys stay Multikey-only. - `vta-vault`: `receive_sd_jwt_vc` and `stored_claims` take the issuer resolver, so a `did:web` / `did:webvh` issuer resolves for `assertionMethod`. `receive` with `IssuerKey::None` resolves locally (`did:key` / `did:peer`); the VTA's issued-credential path passes its DID cache. A credential carrying an IETF `status.status_list` reference is stored `Unknown`, not `Valid`: no `statuslist+jwt` resolver exists yet, so its status cannot be read (VTI-CRD-012). - `vtc-service`: the SD-JWT-VC presentation verifier takes ES256 / ES256K issuers and P-256 / secp256k1 `cnf.jwk` holders.
## `vta-service`
## [0.57.0](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/compare/vta-service-v0.56.0...vta-service-v0.57.0) — 2026-10-11 ### Added - **rooms**: Room files — file keys, STREAM sealing and rooms/keys/file-key ([#2017](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2017)) * feat(rooms): file keys, STREAM sealing and blob manifests in vti-rooms Adds vti_rooms::files, the construction rooms/_shared/0.1/blobs.schema.json FileManifest specifies (trust-tasks-tf #739): a per-file key, HKDF-SHA256 over the epoch storage key salted with the fileId and bound to the room and epoch; ChaCha20-Poly1305 STREAM segments whose nonce counts and whose associated data carries the final flag, so truncation, reordering and splicing fail to authenticate; one sealed segment per transfer chunk; the blob manifest and its BlobRef (sha2-256 over JCS); Padmé padding; and streaming sealer and opener that refuse a file whose plaintext digest is not the one its author signed. The manifest and digests build without the mls feature so a host can check them; the keyed half is behind mls with the rest of the member half. SealedRoom gains file_key_for_seal and file_key_for_open, walking the epoch chain as open_record does. Test vectors in vti-rooms/tests/fixtures/file-vectors.json. - **vta**: External accounts — short-lived provider credentials with no inbound surface ([#2016](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2016)) * feat(vta): external-accounts capabilities and keyspaces Adds the two capabilities the external/* family (trust-tasks-tf #740) gates on: external-accounts-manage, derived by admin alone, and external-auth-use, derived by every role that holds sign (the account's binding, not the role, bounds a consumer). Both are non-additive members of the non-exhaustive Capability enum. Registers two keyspaces: external_accounts (settings, bindings, state) in BACKED_UP, and external_secrets (wrapped provider secrets) in EXCLUDED_FROM_BACKUP, so a portable password-protected backup is never a way to take a provider secret away. DID deletion: an account's binding names its consumer, so external_accounts blocks; external_secrets is unrelated. The device-binding Capability registry (device/_shared 0.2) does not list the two yet, so device listings carry them under ext until it does. - Verify ES256 / ES256K SD-JWT-VCs from did:web and did:webvh issuers ([#1988](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1988)) ([#2010](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2010)) Credentials issued on the swiyu stack and the EUDI profiles could not be received or verified: the vault and the VTC verifier accepted only EdDSA, the vault only a `did:key` issuer, the shared resolver only a `publicKeyMultibase` key, and holder binding only an Ed25519 `cnf.jwk`. - `vta_sdk::jws` (new): compact-JWS verification over a resolved key — EdDSA, ES256 (P-256) and ES256K (secp256k1). The header's `alg` must be the one the resolved key's curve signs with, checked before the signature; `crit` is refused. `JwsKey::from_jwk` reads a `cnf.jwk` (refusing one that carries `d`), `did_key()` names a P-256 holder `did:key:zDn…` and a secp256k1 one `did:key:zQ3s…`. `sd_jwt_issuer_method` binds the issuer JWS `kid` to `iss`: a `did:key` issuer's own key whatever the fragment, any other DID must name its method with a DID-URL `kid` (VTI-CRD-002: the issuer is resolved, not guessed). - `TrustTaskVmResolver` reads a `publicKeyJwk` method (Ed25519, X25519, P-256, secp256k1) and a secp256k1 Multikey; PQC keys stay Multikey-only. - `vta-vault`: `receive_sd_jwt_vc` and `stored_claims` take the issuer resolver, so a `did:web` / `did:webvh` issuer resolves for `assertionMethod`. `receive` with `IssuerKey::None` resolves locally (`did:key` / `did:peer`); the VTA's issued-credential path passes its DID cache. A credential carrying an IETF `status.status_list` reference is stored `Unknown`, not `Valid`: no `statuslist+jwt` resolver exists yet, so its status cannot be read (VTI-CRD-012). - `vtc-service`: the SD-JWT-VC presentation verifier takes ES256 / ES256K issuers and P-256 / secp256k1 `cnf.jwk` holders. - **vta-sdk**: Wallet sign-in with a trigger link: sign auth/oob grants, enrol UV keys, advertise TrustTaskHTTPS and SignInPortal ([#1997](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1997)) * feat(vta-sdk)!: sign auth/oob/grant for assertionMethod (VTI-KEY-106) Adds `auth/oob/grant` to `ATTESTATION_SLUGS`, so `vault/sign-trust-task` signs a wallet sign-in grant for `assertionMethod`: the grant ("let this browser key act as me at this origin until notAfter") is the approving DID's attestation, which the service relies on to open a session, and it verifies the grant against `assertionMethod` (sign-in trigger-link contract C5, base design §10). `auth/oob/identify` stays operational and is signed for `authentication`, as the service verifies it; the other `auth/oob` documents are not attestations either. Both are pinned in the classifier tests. ### Build & CI - Trust-tasks-rs 0.28, affinidi-messaging-sdk 0.34 and affinidi-tdk 0.24 ([#2028](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2028)) Moves the workspace to trust-tasks-rs 0.28 (with capability-client, https, didcomm, tsp and proof) in lockstep with the Affinidi messaging crates built against it (affinidi-tdk-rs #933): affinidi-messaging-sdk 0.34, affinidi-tdk 0.24, mediator-admin / mediator-tui 0.9 (pnm messaging console) and test-mediator 0.20. The lock holds one trust-tasks-rs, one trust-tasks-proof, one SDK and one tdk: `MediatorAcl` crosses the SDK's API, so a graph holding two trust-tasks-rs does not compile. 0.28's one break, the rooms 0.1 `NOT_AUTHORIZED` constants withdrawn for the standard `permissionDenied` (trust-tasks-tf #743), touches nothing here: the room host already answers `permissionDenied`. It carries `DeclaredErrorCode::details_schema` / `check_details` (trust-tasks-tf #742), so the rooms/keys/file-key handler tests check `unknownEpoch` details against the schema the specification declares rather than a hand copy, and vta-service's jsonschema dev-dependency, which existed only for that copy, is dropped. Publishing a vta-sdk on SDK 0.34 / tdk 0.24 is step 2 of the crossing affinidi-tdk-rs's workspace-duplicates-allow.txt records; step 3 moves the mediator's vta-sdk requirement to it there. - Trust-tasks-rs 0.27.8, with auth/oob on its generated types ([#2011](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2011)) * build: trust-tasks-rs 0.27.8 — auth/oob, room files and external accounts ### Fixed - **auth**: Bound wallet sign-in sessions by the grant's notAfter across refresh ([#2026](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2026)) A wallet sign-in (`auth/oob/*`) grant carries `notAfter`, the latest moment the member approved the session for, and redeem reports it. The member-portal mint clamped only the first window to it — the comment "refreshing cannot extend it" was false: `handle_refresh` reset both expiries to now + the full TTL on every rotation, so a session approved for an hour could be renewed indefinitely. The console session minted by wallet sign-in (`mint_admin_cookie_session`, #2014) ignored `notAfter` entirely, and reported the refresh deadline as `notAfter`. - **vta**: Check an extension passkey's rpIdHash against its chrome-extension:// origin ([#2020](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2020)) Chrome requires an extension to pass its bare runtime id as rp.id but signs the assertion over SHA-256("chrome-extension://"), so every browser-plugin grant was refused with oobUvInvalid ("authenticatorData.rpIdHash does not match expected rp_id"). Verify an extension passkey against its origin; web passkeys and stored enrolments are unchanged. ### Performance - **vta-service**: Multi-core REST and direct vsock inbound, failing closed ([#2005](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2005)) * perf(vta-service): serve REST on one worker per CPU The REST server ran on its own current-thread tokio runtime, so every REST handler shared one thread and the VTA could use at most one CPU however many it had. In a Nitro enclave this showed as a 2-vCPU enclave half idle at its ceiling (47%/62% per vCPU), with storage replies waiting for that one thread to poll them. With more than one CPU the REST runtime is now multi-threaded, one worker per CPU. With one CPU it stays current-thread: a multi-threaded runtime was measurably worse there (1-vCPU enclave at 220 keys/sign per second: 463 errors against 2). Measured alone on c6g.4xlarge with a 2-vCPU enclave, in builds with extra timing logging and an audit-key cache not in this series: at 320/s p95 840 -> 71 ms. With this series as it stands, c6g.4xlarge saturates at about 345/s with a 2-vCPU enclave and about 380 to 400/s with a 4-vCPU enclave. Review note: handlers that interleaved only at await points now also run in parallel. Existing non-atomic read-modify-write sequences were already racy across await points; this makes those races more likely. - **vta-service**: Fewer storage reads per keys/sign without widening key custody ([#2001](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2001)) * perf(vta-service): read the caller's ACL entry once per keys/sign sign_payload read the caller's ACL entry twice: once for the sign capability (gate 0) and again for the allowed-keys filter (gate 4). The entry from gate 0 is now passed to gate 4, which reads it itself only when gate 0 did not run (protocol-defined signing input). Both gates still run, in the same order, and now see the same version of the entry. One storage round trip fewer per keys/sign.

title: trust-tasks-rs-v0.29.0
body:
### Added

- **keys**: Sign-jws and sign-csr — protocol signatures from a VTA-held key ([#749](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/749))

A custodian that hardens keys/sign frames every payload under its own
  opaque signing domain (vti.vta.opaque-signing.v1 || 0x00 || payload), so
  nothing signed there verifies as a protocol signature. That is the point
  of the hardening, and it also means nobody can obtain a usable JWS or a
  certificate request for a custodian-held key. A community server acting
  as an OpenID4VP verifier for swiyu and EUDI wallets needs both: a signed
  request object (typ oauth-authz-req+jwt) and proof-of-possession JWTs,
  and a PKCS#10 request to obtain an EUDI relying-party access certificate.

  Two narrow tasks where the custodian builds the protocol bytes itself, so
  the key stays custodian-held and the custodian signs only what it built:

  - keys/sign-jws/0.1: the producer sends header members and a payload
    (a JSON object, or payloadBase64Url); the custodian sets alg from the
    key type (EdDSA, ES256, ES256K, ML-DSA-44/65), refuses alg, crit, b64,
    jwk, jku and x5u, checks an x5c leaf against the key, serialises both
    halves with RFC 8785 and signs the bare JWS signing input. Audited by a
    digest of the signing input, never the payload.
  - keys/sign-csr/0.1: the producer names the subject as ordered typed
    attributes from a closed set and optional subject alternative names;
    the custodian builds the CertificationRequestInfo from those and the
    key's own public key (P-256 with ecdsa-with-SHA256, or Ed25519) and
    returns the PEM request with the key's multibase public key. No
    extension but subjectAltName is ever requested.

  Registers the signJws and signCsr device capabilities (sign-jws and
  sign-csr in 0.1). A custodian must not require sign for either; one that
  frames keys/sign under its own domain should not accept sign in their
  place, since its sign grant cannot yield a JWS or CSR.

  Bindings regenerated (Rust, TS, Go, Dart); no version bumps.

  Refs OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#1988

The Release PR for every package in this repo. **Merging this is the release.**

| Package | Registry | Version | Bump |
|---|---|---|---|
| `trust-tasks` | crates.io | `0.28.1` → `0.29.0` | breaking |

| `github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/trust-tasks-go` | Go (tag `trust-tasks-go/v0.6.2`) | `0.6.1` → `0.6.2` | patch |
| `trust_tasks` | pub.dev | `0.6.1` → `0.6.2` | patch |

What merging does, per registry (all in `publish.yml`, each keyed on "this
version is not published yet"):

- **crates.io** — `release-plz-release` tags `<crate>-v<version>`, publishes in
  dependency order and creates a GitHub Release per crate. Bump levels come from
  `cargo-semver-checks`.
- **npm** — `publish-npm` publishes with OIDC provenance and tags
  `<prefix>-v<version>`.
- **Go** — `publish-go` builds, vets and tests, then pushes the tag, which *is*
  the publication. **Irreversible**: proxy.golang.org never forgets a tag.
- **pub.dev** — `tag-dart` verifies against the *published* core and pushes the
  tag; `publish-dart.yml` publishes from it.

The npm, Go and Dart bumps are only as accurate as the commit subjects — nothing
checks their APIs the way `cargo-semver-checks` checks the crates. Look for a
missing `!` before merging.

This branch is regenerated from `main` on every push, so do not commit to it —
edits are force-pushed away. See RELEASING.md.

title: feat(keys): sign-jws and sign-csr — protocol signatures from a VTA-held key
body:
A custodian that hardens keys/sign frames every payload under its own
opaque signing domain (vti.vta.opaque-signing.v1 || 0x00 || payload), so
nothing signed there verifies as a protocol signature. That is the point
of the hardening, and it also means nobody can obtain a usable JWS or a
certificate request for a custodian-held key. A community server acting
as an OpenID4VP verifier for swiyu and EUDI wallets needs both: a signed
request object (typ oauth-authz-req+jwt) and proof-of-possession JWTs,
and a PKCS#10 request to obtain an EUDI relying-party access certificate.

Two narrow tasks where the custodian builds the protocol bytes itself, so
the key stays custodian-held and the custodian signs only what it built:

- keys/sign-jws/0.1: the producer sends header members and a payload
  (a JSON object, or payloadBase64Url); the custodian sets alg from the
  key type (EdDSA, ES256, ES256K, ML-DSA-44/65), refuses alg, crit, b64,
  jwk, jku and x5u, checks an x5c leaf against the key, serialises both
  halves with RFC 8785 and signs the bare JWS signing input. Audited by a
  digest of the signing input, never the payload.
- keys/sign-csr/0.1: the producer names the subject as ordered typed
  attributes from a closed set and optional subject alternative names;
  the custodian builds the CertificationRequestInfo from those and the
  key's own public key (P-256 with ecdsa-with-SHA256, or Ed25519) and
  returns the PEM request with the key's multibase public key. No
  extension but subjectAltName is ever requested.

Registers the signJws and signCsr device capabilities (sign-jws and
sign-csr in 0.1). A custodian must not require sign for either; one that
frames keys/sign under its own domain should not accept sign in their
place, since its sign grant cannot yield a JWS or CSR.

title: build(deps): affinidi-messaging-sdk 0.34.1
body:
## What and why

This moves the workspace to `affinidi-messaging-sdk` **0.34.1** (affinidi-tdk-rs #936).

Below 0.34.1, the SDK's websocket watchdog replayed heartbeat ticks it had missed while disconnected. After any disconnection longer than about 40 s, every new mediator socket was closed as `Missed Pong, closing connection` within milliseconds. The VTA or VTC then received nothing until its process was restarted, while HTTP kept answering. This is VTI-70. It was seen on 2026-10-11:
- on two VTAs and a VTC after a host DNS outage, with each new socket closed 23–420 ms after opening, for over an hour;
- on `gt-vta` after its mediator was restarted, where only a VTA restart brought it back.

The cause and fix are explained in affinidi-tdk-rs #936. In short, the timer now uses `MissedTickBehavior::Delay`, and it is re-armed on every connect.

The workspace pin moves from `0.34.0` to `0.34.1` as a **correctness floor**, with a comment. A fresh resolve can't pick a version without the fix. The lockfile changes only `affinidi-messaging-sdk`.

## Requirements

VTI-70 (Keyring).

## Backport

None. The release that needs this is the next one cut from `main`. If a deployed release branch has to recover from mediator restarts without an operator, this is a candidate for a backport, and that's the release manager's call.

## Checklist

- [x] Targets `main`
- [x] No `version =` edits in any crate's `Cargo.toml`. Only the workspace dependency pin moves.
- [x] `cargo fmt` and `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` are clean (`-p vti-common -p vta-service -p vtc-service -p vta-sdk`). `cargo test -p vti-common`: 686 passed.

title: spec(rooms): define the sealed record body, signed by its author and bound to its location
body:
`rooms/records/put` 0.2 relies on "the sealed body the author signed" to detect a substituted blob, and `blobs.schema.json` defines the body's `file` member (`FileManifest`), but the body itself was never defined. So two clients couldn't read each other's records, and no reader could check the signature. I hit this implementing `pnm rooms file put/get` in VTI: the CLI would have had to invent a format the portal and extension then copy.

### What this adds
`SealedRecordBody` in `rooms/_shared/0.1/room.schema.json`, the JSON inside `SealedRecord.ciphertext` on `attributed` and `private` rooms:

| member | |
|---|---|
| `roomId`, `key`, `version` | required: the record's location, signed |
| `author` | required: the writing member or agent |
| `title`, `description`, `body`, `tags` | same constraints as the open tier's `cleartext` |
| `file` | `FileManifest`, when the record carries a file |
| `proof` | required: Data Integrity proof by `author`, `assertionMethod`; writers MUST support `eddsa-jcs-2022`, MAY use `ecdsa-jcs-2019` |

**Readers MUST**, before showing anything or trusting `file`:
1. refuse unknown members;
2. verify the proof against `author`;
3. check the signed location matches where the record was read;
4. on `attributed`, check `author` equals the host-recorded author.

A failing record is refused, not shown with a warning.

### Why the location is signed as well as sealed
The AEAD binds `roomId`/`key`/`version`/epoch against the **host**. But every member can open and re-seal a record. Without the location under the author's signature, a member could copy another member's signed body to a new key or a later version. On a `private` room, where the host records no author, readers would attribute it to the original author.

### Also
- `records/put` 0.2 producer rules 3 and 6 point at the definition.
- `keys/seal` 0.1: the plaintext is a signed `SealedRecordBody`. A key holder seals what it's given and never signs for the writer.

No payload or response schema changes, so no version moves. The definition isn't referenced by any task schema, so codegen output is unchanged (as with `FileManifest`, clients implement it). `npm run validate` passes.

- the open tier's title, description, body and tags;
- an optional `file` (FileManifest);
- `author`;
- a Data Integrity proof by `author` (eddsa-jcs-2022, or ecdsa-jcs-2019 for

Readers MUST verify the proof and MUST refuse a record that fails it, not show
it with a warning.

The body also signs its own location (roomId, key, version). The AEAD binds
those against the host, but any member can open and re-seal a record. Without
the signed location, a member could copy another member's body to a new key
or version, and on a private room, where the host records no author, readers
would attribute it to the original author. On attributed rooms, readers also
check `author` against the author the host recorded.

records/put 0.2 and keys/seal 0.1 point at the definition. keys/seal says a
key holder seals what it is given and never signs for the writer. No payload
or response schema changes, so no version moves and no generated type changes.

* build(bindings): hoist shared definitions reached from shared schemas; regenerate

The TS generator seeded its component registry from payload schemas only, but
it compiles every shared schema whole. A shared definition no payload reaches
can still carry a cross-file $ref, and that $ref then resolved to nothing.
SealedRecordBody, which only clients read, references FileManifest in
blobs.schema.json, so building the bindings failed with "resolves to no known
shared component".

The registry is now also seeded from the _shared and _framework schemas. The
only new hoisted type is FileManifest, which blobs.ts re-exports. Go and Dart
regenerate room.schema.json with SealedRecordBody.

title: fix(vta-service): omit highWatermark for an unwritten app-state namespace
body:
Fixes #2029.

## Problem

`vta/app-state/list/1.0` reported the namespace counter as `highWatermark` even when nothing had been written to the namespace, so it sent `0`. The response schema types `highWatermark` as a `Version`, which has `minimum: 1`. As a result:

- A production VTA sent a reply that did not conform to the schema.
- `MockVta`'s response-conformance check turned that reply into `500 responseSchemaViolation`. Every consumer's first sync against an empty namespace failed. OpenVTC's account-sync e2e test had to write a seed record first to get past it.

## Fix

This is option 1 from the issue. With no writes there is no watermark, so `list` now leaves `highWatermark` out of the reply in both snapshot and change-feed mode. The member is not in `required`. Consumers already handle it being absent: the SDK field is `Option<u64>`, and a consumer keeps the `sinceVersion` it sent, which gives the same result. No schema or trust-tasks-rs change is needed.

`watermarkTooOld` cannot carry a 0. It is raised only when `since < reaped_through`, which means at least one write has happened.

## Changes

- `vta-service/src/operations/app_state.rs`: filter out a zero counter.
- `vta-sdk`: the docs on `AppStateListResponse::high_watermark` and `app_state_changes_since` now say the field is absent until the first write.
- `vta-service/tests/it/client_round_trip.rs`: a new round-trip test runs the real client against MockVta. It lists an empty namespace in both modes, expecting success and no watermark, then checks the watermark is `1` after the first write. Before the fix it failed with the exact error from the issue.

## Testing

- `cargo test -p vta-service --test it app_state`: passes.
- `cargo test -p vta-service --lib app_state`: 50 passed.
- `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --all-targets` on `vta-service` and `vta-sdk`: clean.

## Pre-merge checklist

- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2): no client code touched
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3): n/a
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1): read path only
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4): n/a
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5): n/a
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6): n/a
- [x] New/changed wire types: camelCase, deny_unknown_fields where security-relevant, schema registered, all consumers (incl. JS) updated (R3.*): no type change. An optional member is now omitted in one more case, and the response now conforms to its registered schema. Rust consumers already handle absence. No JS consumer reads `highWatermark`.
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive; fail-closed if enforcement can't start (R5.*): n/a
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified; background-job failures are surfaced (R6.*): n/a
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1): no mutation touched
- [x] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers: none

title: app-state list: highWatermark is 0 on an unwritten namespace, which the response schema forbids (minimum 1)
body:
## Summary

`vta/app-state/list/1.0` returns `highWatermark: 0` for a namespace that has never been written. The published response schema forbids that: `highWatermark` is a `$ref` to `Version`, which has `"minimum": 1`.

## Where

- `vta-service/src/operations/app_state.rs` (`list`): `high_watermark = Some(read_counter(ks, context_id, ns).await?)`. `read_counter` is `0` for a fresh namespace, and the value is emitted unchanged.
- Schema: `https://trusttasks.org/spec/vta/app-state/list/1.0#response`, `highWatermark` → `#/$defs/Version` (`minimum: 1`), in trust-tasks-rs 0.27.7.

## Effect

- **Production:** the reply is sent anyway. Consumers that parse `high_watermark: Option<u64>` read it fine, but the service is sending a non-conformant response.
- **`MockVta` (test-support):** the response-conformance check rejects the reply and the client gets `server error (500): responseSchemaViolation`:

```
RESPONSE-CONFORMANCE VIOLATION  https://trusttasks.org/spec/vta/app-state/list/1.0#response: payload failed schema validation: 0 is less than the minimum of 1
```

So any consumer test that does a first sync against an empty namespace fails. OpenVTC's first-sync e2e (account-state sync, `openvtc-core/tests/vta_sync_e2e.rs`) hit this and works around it by seeding one record before syncing.

## Repro

Against `MockVta::start_provisionable()` (vta-service 0.54.0): create a context, then

```rust
client.app_state_changes_since(ctx, "openvtc", 0, None, true, Some(100), None).await
```

on a namespace with no writes.

## Fix options

Either one works:

1. **Service:** omit `highWatermark` when the counter is 0. The member is not in `required`, and a consumer treats absent as "no change since 0".
2. **Spec:** let `highWatermark` admit 0. The request side already does: `sinceVersion` has `minimum: 0`, and its description says "or 0 for a first full pull". A watermark you can be handed back should be one you can send.

Option 2 seems more coherent, since a consumer stores this value and sends it back as `sinceVersion`.

title: feat(did): pluggable contact DID methods and domain-linked contacts (route B)
body:
Implements the two-route contact rule being written into trustoverip/dtgwg-vti-spec#58, so future DID methods (did:scid, did:webs, ledger DIDs) can be supported by registering a resolver, without touching the sign-in flow.

**No registered method uses route B yet.** Only `did:webvh` and `did:web` are registered, both route A ("host-named"), so behaviour today is unchanged: only those two are accepted, `did:key`/`did:peer` stay `from-not-allowed`, anything else stays `unsupported-vid`.

## What changes

- **Contact-method registry** (`packages/core/src/did/methods.ts`): `ContactMethodRegistry`. Each entry has a kind, a route (`host-named` | `domain-linked`), `listsServices`, and a `resolve` hook that resolves and verifies the document. `did:webvh`/`did:web` use the existing resolution code (webvh egress guard, host rules, `doc.id` check). A method with a route but no resolver is rejected when it is registered. `resolveCommunityDocument` delegates to it and now also returns `route`.
- **Pure policy half in `links`** (layering: `links` can't import `did`): `ContactMethodPolicy` / `ContactMethodTable`, which `parseTriggerLink` (new `contactMethods` option), `allowsContact` and `contactDomainLabel` consult. `CONTACT_METHOD_CAPABILITIES` and `isHostNamedServiceContact` are now derived from the built-in policies. `SIGN_IN_FLOW.allowsContact` is `isServiceContact` (either route). New reason `domain-not-linked` (outcome `invalid`).
- **Route B verifier** (`packages/core/src/vtc/domain-linkage.ts`): checks the portal origin against DIF Well-Known DID Configuration v1.0.
  - The request: GET `<origin>/.well-known/did-configuration.json` with `credentials: "omit"` and `redirect: "error"`, plus a check that the response landed on the same origin. It has a timeout (`withFetchTimeout`) and a 64 KiB streamed body cap.
  - The resource: `@context` must be exact, and `linked_dids` is required.
  - The credential: issuer and `credentialSubject.id` must equal the DID, `origin` must match exactly, it must be valid now (60 s allowance, expiry required), and it must be signed with a key under `assertionMethod` in the already-verified document.
  - Formats: **JWT (EdDSA and ES256)** and **JSON-LD with `eddsa-jcs-2022`**. Both use crypto the package already has (`@noble/curves` ed25519/p256 and the existing Data Integrity verifier). No new dependencies.
- **Flow** (`sign-in-flows.ts`): for a domain-linked contact, the linkage is checked after Continue and before the claim. In the join path (unknown DID hosting service), it is checked before `bindIdentity` records anything. On failure the flow ends with `domain-not-linked` and nothing is sent to the contact's services. The fetch goes through the same injected `fetch` that `sendOob` already uses in the offscreen document. No manifest, permission or host-match changes.
- **UI copy**: a "Meaning" line under Details for `domain-not-linked` and `unsupported-vid`, and a stage label for the linkage check.

## Tests

- `core/tests/did.contact-methods.mjs`: the registry accepts webvh/web; an unregistered method gives `unsupported-vid` and nothing is resolved; key/peer stay `from-not-allowed`; a test-only domain-linked method is registered in a fresh registry.
- `core/tests/vtc.domain-linkage.mjs`: valid EdDSA/ES256/JSON-LD cases. Invalid cases: wrong origin, wrong DID, expired, bad signature, key not under assertionMethod, redirect, oversize, timeout, bad `@context`, and others.
- `extension/tests/sign-in-domain-linked.test.mts`: nothing reaches the portal before Continue; the linkage is fetched after Continue, then the claim; the claim happens only when the linkage is valid; `domain-not-linked` is returned with nothing sent; the join path is covered.
- Existing tests pass unchanged, except one assertion in `links.trigger-link.mjs` that pinned `SIGN_IN_FLOW.allowsContact === isHostNamedServiceContact`. It now checks `isServiceContact` and that it agrees with `isHostNamedServiceContact` for every built-in kind.

`npm run lint`, `npm test` and `npm run build` pass.

Note: like the trust-task POSTs, the linkage GET from the offscreen document needs the portal to allow the extension origin (CORS) unless a host permission is granted.

body:
### Added

- **vta**: External accounts — short-lived provider credentials with no inbound surface ([#2016](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2016))

* feat(vta): external-accounts capabilities and keyspaces

  Adds the two capabilities the external/* family (trust-tasks-tf #740) gates on: external-accounts-manage, derived by admin alone, and external-auth-use, derived by every role that holds sign (the account's binding, not the role, bounds a consumer). Both are non-additive members of the non-exhaustive Capability enum.

  Registers two keyspaces: external_accounts (settings, bindings, state) in BACKED_UP, and external_secrets (wrapped provider secrets) in EXCLUDED_FROM_BACKUP, so a portable password-protected backup is never a way to take a provider secret away. DID deletion: an account's binding names its consumer, so external_accounts blocks; external_secrets is unrelated.

  The device-binding Capability registry (device/_shared 0.2) does not list the two yet, so device listings carry them under ext until it does.

### Added

- **rooms**: Room files on the host — blob store, uploads, downloads and limits ([#2018](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2018))

* feat(common): a BlobStore for room files, with local-directory, S3 and GCS backends

  Room files are a record plus a blob; the blob is the file's ciphertext, held outside the room's keyspaces. vti_common::blob_store is node-neutral, beside backup_transfer, so a standalone room host and a community share one store and one conformance suite (data-rooms-files.md §5.3).

  - BlobStore: put (idempotent on the key), get_range, delete (Deleted | Lapses | Unsupported), health.
  - LocalDirStore: plain files, written via a synced temp file and renamed, owner-only. Always compiled.
  - ObjectStoreBlobs over object_store 0.14: S3-compatible (feature blob-s3) and GCS (feature blob-gcs), credentials from the environment for now. object_store passes cargo deny (advisories, bans, licences, sources).
  - Keys are rooms/<first 32 hex of SHA-256(roomId)>/<blobRef>: the store never learns a room's identifier, and the per-room prefix is what a downscoped credential will name.
  - blob_ref_of_manifest: the BlobRef is the sha2-256 DigestMultibase of the manifest's JCS form, computed by the host.
  - conformance::run, which every backend's own test calls.

title: pnm-cli-v0.37.0
body:
### Added

- **rooms**: Room files — file keys, STREAM sealing and rooms/keys/file-key ([#2017](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2017))

* feat(rooms): file keys, STREAM sealing and blob manifests in vti-rooms

  Adds vti_rooms::files, the construction rooms/_shared/0.1/blobs.schema.json FileManifest specifies (trust-tasks-tf #739): a per-file key, HKDF-SHA256 over the epoch storage key salted with the fileId and bound to the room and epoch; ChaCha20-Poly1305 STREAM segments whose nonce counts and whose associated data carries the final flag, so truncation, reordering and splicing fail to authenticate; one sealed segment per transfer chunk; the blob manifest and its BlobRef (sha2-256 over JCS); Padmé padding; and streaming sealer and opener that refuse a file whose plaintext digest is not the one its author signed. The manifest and digests build without the mls feature so a host can check them; the keyed half is behind mls with the rest of the member half. SealedRoom gains file_key_for_seal and file_key_for_open, walking the epoch chain as open_record does. Test vectors in vti-rooms/tests/fixtures/file-vectors.json.

- **vta**: External accounts — short-lived provider credentials with no inbound surface ([#2016](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2016))

* feat(vta): external-accounts capabilities and keyspaces

  Adds the two capabilities the external/* family (trust-tasks-tf #740) gates on: external-accounts-manage, derived by admin alone, and external-auth-use, derived by every role that holds sign (the account's binding, not the role, bounds a consumer). Both are non-additive members of the non-exhaustive Capability enum.

  Registers two keyspaces: external_accounts (settings, bindings, state) in BACKED_UP, and external_secrets (wrapped provider secrets) in EXCLUDED_FROM_BACKUP, so a portable password-protected backup is never a way to take a provider secret away. DID deletion: an account's binding names its consumer, so external_accounts blocks; external_secrets is unrelated.

  The device-binding Capability registry (device/_shared 0.2) does not list the two yet, so device listings carry them under ext until it does.



### Build & CI

- Trust-tasks-rs 0.28, affinidi-messaging-sdk 0.34 and affinidi-tdk 0.24 ([#2028](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2028))

Moves the workspace to trust-tasks-rs 0.28 (with capability-client, https,
  didcomm, tsp and proof) in lockstep with the Affinidi messaging crates built
  against it (affinidi-tdk-rs #933): affinidi-messaging-sdk 0.34, affinidi-tdk
  0.24, mediator-admin / mediator-tui 0.9 (pnm messaging console) and
  test-mediator 0.20. The lock holds one trust-tasks-rs, one trust-tasks-proof,
  one SDK and one tdk: `MediatorAcl` crosses the SDK's API, so a graph holding
  two trust-tasks-rs does not compile.

  0.28's one break, the rooms 0.1 `NOT_AUTHORIZED` constants withdrawn for the
  standard `permissionDenied` (trust-tasks-tf #743), touches nothing here: the
  room host already answers `permissionDenied`.

  It carries `DeclaredErrorCode::details_schema` / `check_details`
  (trust-tasks-tf #742), so the rooms/keys/file-key handler tests check
  `unknownEpoch` details against the schema the specification declares rather
  than a hand copy, and vta-service's jsonschema dev-dependency, which existed
  only for that copy, is dropped.

  Publishing a vta-sdk on SDK 0.34 / tdk 0.24 is step 2 of the crossing
  affinidi-tdk-rs's workspace-duplicates-allow.txt records; step 3 moves the
  mediator's vta-sdk requirement to it there.

title: fix(oob): only build trigger links for host-named DID contacts (VTI-LNK-102)
body:
## Summary
- `buildTriggerLink` (and so `createSignIn`'s `serviceDid`) previously refused only `did:key` contacts.
- VTI-LNK-102/112 (trustoverip/dtgwg-vti-spec#58, d37a675) require a DID whose method names the host serving its document, can list services, and is verified under VTI-LNK-052 — in practice `did:webvh` and `did:web`.
- Replaces the refusal with a capability allow-list, `CONTACT_METHOD_CAPABILITIES` + `isHostNamedServiceContact`, mirroring the plugin reader (`packages/core/src/links/trigger-link.ts`). A new qualifying method is a one-row addition.
- Refusals throw `TriggerLinkError` (`bad-from`) with a message naming VTI-LNK-102.
- CHANGELOG entry under `## Unreleased`; version not bumped.

## Tests
- did:webvh and did:web accepted; did:peer (numalgo 0 and 2), did:key, did:ion and `did:constructor` refused.
- `npm run lint`, `npm test` (134 passed), `npm run build` all pass.

title: cnm-cli-v0.31.0
body:
### Changed

- **vtc**: Drop vtc-client's unused bearer token and the uncalled persona REST route ([#2023](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2023))

* refactor(vtc-client): keep no bearer token, and say what the VTC's REST surface now is

  Every verb `vtc-client` sends is a signed Trust Task, and the last bearer
  routes it called are gone, but the client still stored the access token
  `connect` obtained and its docs still described verbs "on bearer REST until
  they have a Trust Task".

  - `VtcClient` no longer holds a token. `connect` still runs the
    challenge-response login: it is the up-front access check, so a DID the VTC
    does not know is refused where `cnm` can print the fix rather than on the
    first verb. Its token was read by nothing but `Debug`, which now reports
    whose signing key is held.
  - Docs: the vetting-admin "stays on bearer REST" note,
    `VtcError::NoRestTransport` (now: no REST base and no session to carry a
    Trust Task), `with_key`, and the `self.token` mentions in `git_ns` and
    `rooms`.
  - vtc-service: the surface-task and join-discovery comments no longer say
    those verbs keep a REST route; the persona route's exception rows say what
    is true — `vtc/relationships/persona/0.1` has no upstream specification,
    which is why the spine cannot dispatch it.
  - cnm: the withdrawal hint pointed at `GET /v1/join-requests/<id>/vetting`,
    which is not mounted; it now points at the join request in the console.
  - admin-ui: a comment named `POST /v1/schemas/accepts` for what is
    `vtc/schemas/accepts/register`.

title: vti-rooms-v0.12.0
body:
### Added

- **rooms**: Room files on the host — blob store, uploads, downloads and limits ([#2018](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2018))

* feat(common): a BlobStore for room files, with local-directory, S3 and GCS backends

  Room files are a record plus a blob; the blob is the file's ciphertext, held outside the room's keyspaces. vti_common::blob_store is node-neutral, beside backup_transfer, so a standalone room host and a community share one store and one conformance suite (data-rooms-files.md §5.3).

  - BlobStore: put (idempotent on the key), get_range, delete (Deleted | Lapses | Unsupported), health.
  - LocalDirStore: plain files, written via a synced temp file and renamed, owner-only. Always compiled.
  - ObjectStoreBlobs over object_store 0.14: S3-compatible (feature blob-s3) and GCS (feature blob-gcs), credentials from the environment for now. object_store passes cargo deny (advisories, bans, licences, sources).
  - Keys are rooms/<first 32 hex of SHA-256(roomId)>/<blobRef>: the store never learns a room's identifier, and the per-room prefix is what a downscoped credential will name.
  - blob_ref_of_manifest: the BlobRef is the sha2-256 DigestMultibase of the manifest's JCS form, computed by the host.
  - conformance::run, which every backend's own test calls.

body:
### Added

- **rooms**: Room files on the host — blob store, uploads, downloads and limits ([#2018](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2018))

* feat(common): a BlobStore for room files, with local-directory, S3 and GCS backends
