- **rooms**: Room files — file keys, STREAM sealing and rooms/keys/file-key ([#2017](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2017))

* feat(rooms): file keys, STREAM sealing and blob manifests in vti-rooms

  Adds vti_rooms::files, the construction rooms/_shared/0.1/blobs.schema.json FileManifest specifies (trust-tasks-tf #739): a per-file key, HKDF-SHA256 over the epoch storage key salted with the fileId and bound to the room and epoch; ChaCha20-Poly1305 STREAM segments whose nonce counts and whose associated data carries the final flag, so truncation, reordering and splicing fail to authenticate; one sealed segment per transfer chunk; the blob manifest and its BlobRef (sha2-256 over JCS); Padmé padding; and streaming sealer and opener that refuse a file whose plaintext digest is not the one its author signed. The manifest and digests build without the mls feature so a host can check them; the keyed half is behind mls with the rest of the member half. SealedRoom gains file_key_for_seal and file_key_for_open, walking the epoch chain as open_record does. Test vectors in vti-rooms/tests/fixtures/file-vectors.json.

- **vtc**: Add a member and make an ACL entry a membership, governed by an admission policy ([#2022](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2022))

* feat(vtc): add a member and make an ACL entry a membership, governed by an admission policy

  Add vtc/members/admit/0.1 (admit a DID directly, without a join request)
  and vtc/members/make-membership/0.1 (give an ACL entry with no member
  record - the bootstrap administrator - the member record and membership
  credentials, leaving the entry untouched). Both are decided by a new
  ceremony purpose, admission (vtc.admission): allow admits, deny refuses,
  refer parks the operation in the action list (Act::DirectAdmission) for
  another holder of vtc.members.manage (VTI-APV-015, VTI-APV-017). Roles
  beyond member take vtc.roles.assign and are bounded by the actor's own
  entry (VTI-ACL-071); admin is never seated this way (VTI-APV-018).

  Wire types are local until the specifications are published; the spine
  enforces their document policy through a local SpecPolicy. ACL entries
  gain ext.org.openvtc.membership so the console can offer the action.
  Audited as MemberAdmittedDirectly. The console gains Add a member and
  Make this a membership. Wallet sign-in declines are now logged with their
  reason and request id; the wire answer stays notAuthorized (T15).

- **vta**: External accounts — short-lived provider credentials with no inbound surface ([#2016](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2016))

* feat(vta): external-accounts capabilities and keyspaces

  Adds the two capabilities the external/* family (trust-tasks-tf #740) gates on: external-accounts-manage, derived by admin alone, and external-auth-use, derived by every role that holds sign (the account's binding, not the role, bounds a consumer). Both are non-additive members of the non-exhaustive Capability enum.

  Registers two keyspaces: external_accounts (settings, bindings, state) in BACKED_UP, and external_secrets (wrapped provider secrets) in EXCLUDED_FROM_BACKUP, so a portable password-protected backup is never a way to take a provider secret away. DID deletion: an account's binding names its consumer, so external_accounts blocks; external_secrets is unrelated.

  The device-binding Capability registry (device/_shared 0.2) does not list the two yet, so device listings carry them under ext until it does.

- **vtc**: Wallet sign-in by trigger link on the operator console's login page ([#2014](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2014))

* feat(vtc): wallet sign-in by trigger link on the operator console's login page

  The console's login page (`/admin/`) gets the `auth/oob/*` key-grant
  sign-in the member portal has, and is rebuilt on the community's sign-in
  look, with a way back to the community's home page.

- **vtc**: Member portal, with wallet sign-in by trigger link ([#2007](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2007))

* feat(vtc): a member portal at /members, and a home page that explains the community

  Members could not sign in anywhere: VTC sign-in admitted administrators only,
  and every session it minted read as an admin session. This adds a member
  portal as a separate application from the console, with the separation
  enforced by the daemon rather than by what each page shows.

  Member portal (`crate::member_portal`, `routes::member_portal`):
  - Only an active member signs in — a live ACL entry that is not expired,
    suspended or an `application` entry, plus a member record that has not been
    removed — checked at challenge (VTI-SES-006/007 via the shared handler), at
    authentication, on every refresh and on every request (VTI-SES-020..022).
  - Sign-in by the browser wallet (SIOPv2 at `<origin>/v1/member/wallet`) or a
    portal passkey only. A passkey is added from the portal after a wallet
    sign-in; adding or removing one requires a wallet-proven session (`amr`
    contains `did`). Audited as the new `MemberPasskeyChanged` event.
  - Tokens carry audience `VTC-member` (`JwtKeys::for_audience`), so console
    extractors refuse them and the portal refuses console tokens.
  - Sessions and passkeys live in their own keyspaces (`member_sessions`,
    `member_passkeys`, excluded from backup), so a member who is also an
    administrator cannot redeem a portal refresh token or passkey at the console.
  - Cookies `vtc_member_session` / `vtc_member_refresh` are `Path=/v1/member`;
    `vtc_member_csrf` is the portal's own double-submit value, and the CSRF gate
    picks the cookie pair by path.
  - The portal is its own Vite bundle (`vite.members.config.ts`), baked by
    build.rs into `$OUT_DIR/member-ui-dist` and served at `/members/`; it loads
    no console code. In subdomain mode it is served on the API host.
  - The sign-in page carries manual install steps for the VTA Wallet extension
    (OpenVTC/vta-browser-plugin).

  Default landing page: rebuilt around a visitor who does not know what a VTC
  is — "Get started" at openvtc.net, member sign-in, capability cards (git
  across GitHub, Forgejo/Codeberg and Gitea, verifiable data rooms, access
  management, credentials, recognition), a quieter operator-console link, and
  the existing status panel. Fixes hidden status rows rendering empty.

  The step-up passkey route test now compares an unrouted response with the
  website fallback byte for byte; its old "no 'credentials' in the body" check
  tripped on the new landing page copy.

- **vta-sdk**: Wallet sign-in with a trigger link: sign auth/oob grants, enrol UV keys, advertise TrustTaskHTTPS and SignInPortal ([#1997](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1997))

* feat(vta-sdk)!: sign auth/oob/grant for assertionMethod (VTI-KEY-106)

  Adds `auth/oob/grant` to `ATTESTATION_SLUGS`, so `vault/sign-trust-task`
  signs a wallet sign-in grant for `assertionMethod`: the grant ("let this
  browser key act as me at this origin until notAfter") is the approving
  DID's attestation, which the service relies on to open a session, and it
  verifies the grant against `assertionMethod` (sign-in trigger-link
  contract C5, base design §10).

  `auth/oob/identify` stays operational and is signed for `authentication`,
  as the service verifies it; the other `auth/oob` documents are not
  attestations either. Both are pinned in the classifier tests.



### Fixed

- **auth**: Bound wallet sign-in sessions by the grant's notAfter across refresh ([#2026](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2026))

A wallet sign-in (`auth/oob/*`) grant carries `notAfter`, the latest
  moment the member approved the session for, and redeem reports it. The
  member-portal mint clamped only the first window to it — the comment
  "refreshing cannot extend it" was false: `handle_refresh` reset both
  expiries to now + the full TTL on every rotation, so a session approved
  for an hour could be renewed indefinitely. The console session minted by
  wallet sign-in (`mint_admin_cookie_session`, #2014) ignored `notAfter`
  entirely, and reported the refresh deadline as `notAfter`.

- **vti-common**: Pooled enclave storage with atomic multi-step operations ([#1999](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1999))

* fix(vti-common): pool the enclave's vsock storage connections

  Inside a Nitro enclave every storage operation went through one vsock
  connection behind one mutex held for the whole round trip, so all storage
  I/O in the VTA ran strictly one operation at a time. Throughput of anything
  that touches storage was capped by the round-trip time, whatever the
  enclave's vCPU count: a keys/sign costs about ten round trips, and load
  tests saw the same ceiling (about 85 signs/s) with one and with two enclave
  vCPUs, with neither the enclave nor the parent CPU saturated.

  VsockStore now keeps a bounded pool of connections (up to 8). A request
  owns a connection for one complete round trip and returns it only after a
  full response; the parent's storage proxy already serves each connection in
  its own task, so independent operations now run in parallel. Each
  operation is still a single request, and the multi-step operations (swap,
  take_raw, move_if_unchanged) are no less atomic than before: the old lock
  was released between their steps too.

  This also fixes a latent correctness bug. The old code kept the shared
  connection after a cancelled request: if a request future was dropped
  after writing its request but before reading the response (a request
  timeout, a client disconnect), the next caller read the previous caller's
  response. A pooled connection that fails or is cancelled mid-round-trip is
  dropped instead of reused.

  The pool is transport-agnostic and compiled under `test` as well as
  `vsock-store`, so its tests run on every platform, not only Linux.



### Performance

- **audit**: Cache the active audit key per keyspace, failing closed ([#2004](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2004))

Every audited operation read the active audit key from storage twice: the
  `audit_key:active` marker, then the key it names. #1951 measured removing
  both reads at roughly +13-25% keys/sign throughput in a Nitro Enclave.

  Per-keyspace write tracking in the store (store/generation.rs), shared by
  every handle for a keyspace name:

  - A write begins before its request leaves (generation bumped, counted in
    flight) and ends when it completes or is dropped (bumped again).
  - A write that ends without a reply after its frame had completely left
    the enclave - transport failure, or its future dropped - marks the
    keyspace unknown: the parent may still apply it. A write that ends before
    its frame left (no connection, pool closed, write error) cannot have been
    applied, so it marks nothing. The pool reports which via a `sent` flag set
    in round_trip once the whole frame is written (request_tracked /
    request_once_tracked).
  - The unknown mark clears when a write that began after it completes, or
    after UNKNOWN_SETTLE (30 s) - longer than any plausible late apply of an
    abandoned frame; without it one timed-out write would switch the
    audit_key cache off until the next rotation.
  - Readers take a ticket before reading: none while a write is in flight or
    unknown, and a fresh read is cached only if its ticket is still current.
  - Vsock: both pool paths are tracked - `send` (request_tracked: plain ops,
    fallbacks, the restore's plain insert) and `send_atomic`
    (request_once_tracked: OP_TAKE, OP_INSERT_IF_ABSENT, OP_SWAP_IF_ABSENT,
    OP_MOVE_IF_EQUAL, the restore). Anything not a known read-only opcode is a
    write.
  - Local: each write's guard runs inside the blocking closure that writes, so
    its outcome is always known (a panic excepted).

- **vta-service**: Multi-core REST and direct vsock inbound, failing closed ([#2005](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2005))

* perf(vta-service): serve REST on one worker per CPU

  The REST server ran on its own current-thread tokio runtime, so every REST
  handler shared one thread and the VTA could use at most one CPU however
  many it had. In a Nitro enclave this showed as a 2-vCPU enclave half idle at
  its ceiling (47%/62% per vCPU), with storage replies waiting for that one
  thread to poll them.

  With more than one CPU the REST runtime is now multi-threaded, one worker
  per CPU. With one CPU it stays current-thread: a multi-threaded runtime was
  measurably worse there (1-vCPU enclave at 220 keys/sign per second: 463
  errors against 2).

  Measured alone on c6g.4xlarge with a 2-vCPU enclave, in builds with extra
  timing logging and an audit-key cache not in this series: at 320/s p95
  840 -> 71 ms. With this series as it stands, c6g.4xlarge saturates at about
  345/s with a 2-vCPU enclave and about 380 to 400/s with a 4-vCPU enclave.

  Review note: handlers that interleaved only at await points now also run in
  parallel. Existing non-atomic read-modify-write sequences were already racy
  across await points; this makes those races more likely.

- **storage**: Atomic take / insert-if-absent / swap / compare-and-move in the parent proxy ([#2003](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2003))

* perf(enclave-proxy): atomic take / insert-if-absent / swap / compare-and-move

  The enclave store's claims and moves were sequences of single operations
  over vsock: two round trips for a take or an insert-if-absent, three for a
  swap, four for a compare-and-move. The proxy now serves each as one
  operation (OP_TAKE, OP_INSERT_IF_ABSENT, OP_SWAP_IF_ABSENT,
  OP_MOVE_IF_EQUAL), advertised by OP_HELLO, under a per-keyspace lock held
  across its fjall steps. A plain mutex rather than fjall's transactional
  database: the critical sections are a few fjall calls with no await, and
  switching the database type would touch every operation.

  None needs plaintext. Values are ciphertext bound to (keyspace, key);
  OP_MOVE_IF_EQUAL compares the stored ciphertext with bytes the enclave has
  just read and compared in plaintext itself.

  Each reply frame now goes out in one write (it was two packets). A DID-log
  write through any of the new operations still lands on disk.

title: vta-sdk-v0.65.0
body:
### Added

- **rooms**: Room files — file keys, STREAM sealing and rooms/keys/file-key ([#2017](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2017))

* feat(rooms): file keys, STREAM sealing and blob manifests in vti-rooms

  Adds vti_rooms::files, the construction rooms/_shared/0.1/blobs.schema.json FileManifest specifies (trust-tasks-tf #739): a per-file key, HKDF-SHA256 over the epoch storage key salted with the fileId and bound to the room and epoch; ChaCha20-Poly1305 STREAM segments whose nonce counts and whose associated data carries the final flag, so truncation, reordering and splicing fail to authenticate; one sealed segment per transfer chunk; the blob manifest and its BlobRef (sha2-256 over JCS); Padmé padding; and streaming sealer and opener that refuse a file whose plaintext digest is not the one its author signed. The manifest and digests build without the mls feature so a host can check them; the keyed half is behind mls with the rest of the member half. SealedRoom gains file_key_for_seal and file_key_for_open, walking the epoch chain as open_record does. Test vectors in vti-rooms/tests/fixtures/file-vectors.json.

- P-256 and secp256k1 members — Trust Task proofs, rotation and OID4VCI key binding ([#1988](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1988)) ([#2021](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2021))

#2010 accepted P-256 and secp256k1 for credentials others issue. A member
  holding such a key — a secure-enclave or EUDI-wallet key, `did:key:zDn…` /
  `did:key:zQ3s…` — still could not sign as one: the SDK signed Trust Tasks
  Ed25519 only, and the VTC's hex holder signatures and OID4VCI key-binding
  proof read every key as Ed25519. Every one of these now goes through
  `vta_sdk::jws::JwsKey`, so the key decides the algorithm and nothing in the
  request can choose one.

  - Trust Task proofs: the shared verifier already accepted `ecdsa-jcs-2019`
    (P-256) once phase 1 taught the VM resolver P-256 keys; a test now holds
    it. `trust_task_sign` signs `ecdsa-jcs-2019` for a P-256 holder — a private
    multibase with the `p256-priv` prefix, or a bare one beside a
    `did:key:zDn…`. The Trust Tasks framework has every consumer SHOULD-verify
    that suite, for hardware-backed signers. There is no secp256k1 Data
    Integrity suite, so a secp256k1 key signs no Trust Task.
  - `vtc/members/rotate`: the old and new signatures (hex, 64 bytes) may be
    EdDSA, ES256 or ES256K by the key that made them; ECDSA is `r || s` over
    the SHA-256 of the canonical bytes, as JWS encodes it. The `did:webvh` path
    resolves `#key-0` through `TrustTaskVmResolver` (bound to authentication,
    VTI-KEY-022, with the cached-document refresh, VTI-KEY-134) instead of
    reading Ed25519 bytes off the document. Join's REST holder binding shares
    the same verifier.
  - OID4VCI key-binding proof: `EdDSA`, `ES256` or `ES256K`, whichever the
    `kid`'s key signs; a header naming another is refused before the
    signature. `DidVmResolver::resolve_verifying_key` (Ed25519) becomes
    `resolve_jws_key`.
  - `vta_sdk::jws`: `JwsKey::from_did_key`, and `verify_signature` is public
    for signatures that are not a JWS.

  What the workspace mints, and every key `sealed_transfer` seals to, stays
  Ed25519 / X25519: the VTA's sealed credential delivery (`seal_issued_credential`)
  still needs an Ed25519 `did:key` holder, and a sign-in `sessionKey` is still
  Ed25519. Accepting more algorithms widens what VTI-KEY-013 (retirable
  algorithms) would have to retire; that requirement is already an open
  divergence in the specification's register.

- **vta**: External accounts — short-lived provider credentials with no inbound surface ([#2016](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2016))

* feat(vta): external-accounts capabilities and keyspaces

  Adds the two capabilities the external/* family (trust-tasks-tf #740) gates on: external-accounts-manage, derived by admin alone, and external-auth-use, derived by every role that holds sign (the account's binding, not the role, bounds a consumer). Both are non-additive members of the non-exhaustive Capability enum.

  Registers two keyspaces: external_accounts (settings, bindings, state) in BACKED_UP, and external_secrets (wrapped provider secrets) in EXCLUDED_FROM_BACKUP, so a portable password-protected backup is never a way to take a provider secret away. DID deletion: an account's binding names its consumer, so external_accounts blocks; external_secrets is unrelated.

  The device-binding Capability registry (device/_shared 0.2) does not list the two yet, so device listings carry them under ext until it does.

- Read IETF Token Status Lists for SD-JWT VCs, signed by the credential's issuer ([#1988](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1988)) ([#2015](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2015))

An SD-JWT VC from the swiyu stack or an EUDI issuer names its status as
  `status.status_list = { idx, uri }`, a `statuslist+jwt`. The VTC fed that
  reference to the W3C Bitstring fetcher, which could never read it (Unknown at
  every join), and the vault held such credentials Unknown for good. Both now
  read it, through affinidi-status-list 0.1.7's `token` module.

  - `vta_sdk::token_status_list` (new): `verify_status_list_token` and
    `resolve_token_status`. A list decides revocation, so it is trusted only as
    the credential issuer's: the token's `kid` must name one of that issuer's
    `assertionMethod` keys (`sd_jwt_issuer_method`), the signature is checked
    with that key's algorithm (`JwsKey`) before the payload is read, and an
    `iss` naming anyone else is refused. `typ`, `sub` = the referenced `uri`,
    `iat` and `exp` are checked by the TDK, and the list is decompressed under
    a cap. The fetch is SSRF-guarded, takes no redirects and caps the body. A
    separate Status Issuer linked by certificate chain (draft §13.5) is not
    supported; its lists are refused.
  - `vta-vault`: `StatusListResolver::resolve_token_status` (a defaulted method,
    so existing resolvers compile and refuse) is implemented by
    `HttpStatusListResolver`. `refresh_status`, which the present gate runs
    first, takes the Token path when a credential carries `status.status_list`
    and no W3C `credentialStatus`: `INVALID` → `Revoked` (terminal),
    `SUSPENDED` → `Revoked` tagged `tokenStatus:suspended` so a later `VALID`
    restores it, an application-specific or unregistered value → `Unknown`
    (VTI-CRD-012). Receive still stores such a credential `Unknown`: its status
    has not been read until that refresh.
  - `vtc-service`: `StatusListFetcher::check_token_status`, implemented by the
    verifying `HttpStatusListFetcher`. `resolve_presented_status` (join, join
    criteria, invitations) maps `VALID` / `INVALID` / `SUSPENDED` to Valid /
    Revoked / Suspended, and anything unreadable to Unknown for the join policy.
  - `affinidi-status-list` 0.1.3 → 0.1.7. `docs/03-vtc/credentials.md` gains
    *Reading another issuer's status*.

- Verify ES256 / ES256K SD-JWT-VCs from did:web and did:webvh issuers ([#1988](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1988)) ([#2010](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2010))

Credentials issued on the swiyu stack and the EUDI profiles could not be
  received or verified: the vault and the VTC verifier accepted only EdDSA,
  the vault only a `did:key` issuer, the shared resolver only a
  `publicKeyMultibase` key, and holder binding only an Ed25519 `cnf.jwk`.

  - `vta_sdk::jws` (new): compact-JWS verification over a resolved key —
    EdDSA, ES256 (P-256) and ES256K (secp256k1). The header's `alg` must be
    the one the resolved key's curve signs with, checked before the
    signature; `crit` is refused. `JwsKey::from_jwk` reads a `cnf.jwk`
    (refusing one that carries `d`), `did_key()` names a P-256 holder
    `did:key:zDn…` and a secp256k1 one `did:key:zQ3s…`.
    `sd_jwt_issuer_method` binds the issuer JWS `kid` to `iss`: a `did:key`
    issuer's own key whatever the fragment, any other DID must name its
    method with a DID-URL `kid` (VTI-CRD-002: the issuer is resolved, not
    guessed).
  - `TrustTaskVmResolver` reads a `publicKeyJwk` method (Ed25519, X25519,
    P-256, secp256k1) and a secp256k1 Multikey; PQC keys stay Multikey-only.
  - `vta-vault`: `receive_sd_jwt_vc` and `stored_claims` take the issuer
    resolver, so a `did:web` / `did:webvh` issuer resolves for
    `assertionMethod`. `receive` with `IssuerKey::None` resolves locally
    (`did:key` / `did:peer`); the VTA's issued-credential path passes its DID
    cache. A credential carrying an IETF `status.status_list` reference is
    stored `Unknown`, not `Valid`: no `statuslist+jwt` resolver exists yet, so
    its status cannot be read (VTI-CRD-012).
  - `vtc-service`: the SD-JWT-VC presentation verifier takes ES256 / ES256K
    issuers and P-256 / secp256k1 `cnf.jwk` holders.

- **vtc**: Member portal, with wallet sign-in by trigger link ([#2007](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2007))

* feat(vtc): a member portal at /members, and a home page that explains the community

  Members could not sign in anywhere: VTC sign-in admitted administrators only,
  and every session it minted read as an admin session. This adds a member
  portal as a separate application from the console, with the separation
  enforced by the daemon rather than by what each page shows.

  Member portal (`crate::member_portal`, `routes::member_portal`):
  - Only an active member signs in — a live ACL entry that is not expired,
    suspended or an `application` entry, plus a member record that has not been
    removed — checked at challenge (VTI-SES-006/007 via the shared handler), at
    authentication, on every refresh and on every request (VTI-SES-020..022).
  - Sign-in by the browser wallet (SIOPv2 at `<origin>/v1/member/wallet`) or a
    portal passkey only. A passkey is added from the portal after a wallet
    sign-in; adding or removing one requires a wallet-proven session (`amr`
    contains `did`). Audited as the new `MemberPasskeyChanged` event.
  - Tokens carry audience `VTC-member` (`JwtKeys::for_audience`), so console
    extractors refuse them and the portal refuses console tokens.
  - Sessions and passkeys live in their own keyspaces (`member_sessions`,
    `member_passkeys`, excluded from backup), so a member who is also an
    administrator cannot redeem a portal refresh token or passkey at the console.
  - Cookies `vtc_member_session` / `vtc_member_refresh` are `Path=/v1/member`;
    `vtc_member_csrf` is the portal's own double-submit value, and the CSRF gate
    picks the cookie pair by path.
  - The portal is its own Vite bundle (`vite.members.config.ts`), baked by
    build.rs into `$OUT_DIR/member-ui-dist` and served at `/members/`; it loads
    no console code. In subdomain mode it is served on the API host.
  - The sign-in page carries manual install steps for the VTA Wallet extension
    (OpenVTC/vta-browser-plugin).

  Default landing page: rebuilt around a visitor who does not know what a VTC
  is — "Get started" at openvtc.net, member sign-in, capability cards (git
  across GitHub, Forgejo/Codeberg and Gitea, verifiable data rooms, access
  management, credentials, recognition), a quieter operator-console link, and
  the existing status panel. Fixes hidden status rows rendering empty.

  The step-up passkey route test now compares an unrouted response with the
  website fallback byte for byte; its old "no 'credentials' in the body" check
  tripped on the new landing page copy.

- **vta-sdk**: Wallet sign-in with a trigger link: sign auth/oob grants, enrol UV keys, advertise TrustTaskHTTPS and SignInPortal ([#1997](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1997))

* feat(vta-sdk)!: sign auth/oob/grant for assertionMethod (VTI-KEY-106)

  Adds `auth/oob/grant` to `ATTESTATION_SLUGS`, so `vault/sign-trust-task`
  signs a wallet sign-in grant for `assertionMethod`: the grant ("let this
  browser key act as me at this origin until notAfter") is the approving
  DID's attestation, which the service relies on to open a session, and it
  verifies the grant against `assertionMethod` (sign-in trigger-link
  contract C5, base design §10).

  `auth/oob/identify` stays operational and is signed for `authentication`,
  as the service verifies it; the other `auth/oob` documents are not
  attestations either. Both are pinned in the classifier tests.



### Build & CI

- Trust-tasks-rs 0.27.8, with auth/oob on its generated types ([#2011](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2011))

* build: trust-tasks-rs 0.27.8 — auth/oob, room files and external accounts

title: fix(links): align the trigger-link parser with VTI-LNK spec d37a675
body:
Aligns `packages/core/src/links/trigger-link.ts` with the updated trigger-links chapter, trustoverip/dtgwg-vti-spec#58 at d37a675 (`spec/07a-links.md`). The spec is authoritative; every change here makes the reader refuse more.

## Changes

1. **Contact allow-list (VTI-LNK-102 / 112).** `SIGN_IN_FLOW.allowsContact` used to accept `did:peer` (except numalgo 0). It is now `isHostNamedServiceContact`, a capability-style allow-list driven by `CONTACT_METHOD_CAPABILITIES`. That table lists, per method, whether it names its document's host, whether it can list services, and whether it is verified under 052. Only `did:webvh` and `did:web` have all three. Any other contact gets `from-not-allowed`. A new qualifying method needs only one new row. This reader does not implement `vta-claim`, so its flow stays `unknown-flow`. A reader that adds it should reuse the same predicate (noted on `READER_FLOWS`).
2. **Non-DID `_from` (VTI-LNK-020 step 6 / 031).** A value that is neither a DID nor an agent name is now `unsupported-vid` (outcome `update`), whether or not it has a `scheme:` prefix. That covers a bare KERI identifier, a bare domain, or `DID:web:…`. `bad-from` is now kept for two cases only: an empty value, and a value that starts with `did:` but is not valid DID syntax. The `/@` test still runs before the DID-syntax test.
3. **Empty path segments (VTI-LNK-040).** `/vti//flow/sign-in/0.1` is now `bad-type`.
4. **Absolute `_type` (VTI-LNK-040).** The absolute form is now checked as written, before percent-decoding. It must:
   - start with lowercase `https://`
   - have a lowercase host that passes the host rules (060), with no userinfo and no port
   - have a path that meets every path-form constraint (shared `isFlowPath`)

   A fully percent-encoded `https%3A%2F%2F…` used to pass because it was decoded first. It is now `bad-type`. The `wrong-host` check (043) still compares the path without its version, so `https://flows.example.org/vti/flow/sign-in/0.9` is `wrong-host`.

## Tests

`packages/core/tests/links.trigger-link.mjs` adds the chapter's example rows that touch these rules as vectors:
- `/vti//flow`, `https://LINK.…`, `:443`, `flows.example.org/…/0.9`
- `did:web:example.com/@alice`, `did:web:example.com/alice`, the KERI identifier, empty `_from`
- `did:peer:2…` (and `did:peer:0…`)

It also adds edge cases for the absolute form (scheme case, userinfo, port, IP/localhost, trailing dot, percent-encoding in host or path, query, dot segments, whole-value encoding) and checks that a `did:web` contact is accepted. `nonsense` moved from the `bad-from` list to `unsupported-vid`, which the spec now requires.

Existing valid links still pass: the `did:webvh` contact with `_type=/vti/flow/sign-in/0.1`, the absolute same-host form, the alias scheme, and the upper-cased authority. Callers (`sign-in-flows.ts`, `background.ts` `handleTriggerLink`, `trigger-link-click.ts`) only branch on `ok`, `outcome === "pass-on"` and `flow.spec.name`. None of these changes produces `pass-on`, so click routing is unchanged and the new refusals reach the existing `invalid`/`update` messages.

## Backwards compatibility

**`did:peer` contacts are no longer accepted for `sign-in`** (they get `from-not-allowed`), as VTI-LNK-102 now requires. No known producer emits one:
- the VTC portal (`vtc-service` `oob.ts`) uses the VTC's own DID
- `rp-sdk-js` `buildTriggerLink` uses the configured `serviceDid`
- the did-hosting UI (`oob-sign-in.ts`) uses the control service DID

All three are `did:webvh` in deployment. No test fixture or source in those repos builds a `did:peer` `_from`. Their producer-side guards refuse only `did:key`, though, so they could be tightened to match. That is follow-up work in those repos.

No manifest, permission or dependency changes.

`npm run lint`, `npm run build` and `npm test` pass from the root.

title: feat(sign-in): offer to use an unknown DID hosting service, and name the DID it has not listed
body:
## What

Trigger-link sign-in (`auth/oob`) from a site the wallet doesn't know used to stop at "Not one of your communities". This PR adds the join step that contract C3 step 2 promised but never had. It covers DID hosting, and it says plainly what is still missing for VTCs.

**Unknown site.** The wallet first resolves and verifies the site's DID document and runs the page-origin-vs-portal check (`wrong-origin`), the same as on the normal path, before it offers anything. Nothing goes to the site's Trust-Task endpoint until the person agrees. Declining or closing the window sends nothing. The only request made beforehand is the read of the public DID document.

- **DID hosting.** The verified document has a `WebVHHosting` service, matched on `type`.
  - The wallet asks "Use \<host> to host your DIDs?", names the verified origin and lists the DIDs the agent hosts (`vta/webvh/list`, across contexts). With several DIDs, the person picks one.
  - Yes records the service with the vault entry the legacy first-use prompt has always created. `bindProfile` is now shared by `proxyLogin`, `walletProfile`, `login` and this flow. The entry is `didSelfIssued`, its targets are `webOrigin` = portal origin and `did` = the service DID, and it sits in the chosen DID's context with its one derivable signing key.
  - The window then goes straight to the normal confirm → claim → … for the same link. The website doesn't need a second click.
- **Anything else, including a VTC.** The screen stays "Not one of your communities" and now shows the verified sign-in page. The wallet has no VTC join path to hand off to. `@openvtc/pnm-core/vtc` has the `vtc/join-requests/*` client calls, but no surface runs them. VTC DID documents (`vtc-host.json`) don't advertise a join page the wallet could link to.

**Not on the access list.** A DID hosting service can answer `auth/oob:notAuthorized` at `prove`, either just after a join or for an entry that already existed. The wallet then shows "\<host> hasn't added you yet. Send this DID to its operator:" with the DID and a Copy button. The service is unchanged (see below).

**Fixed on the way.** The services send family-qualified codes (C9), such as `auth/oob/claim:alreadyClaimed` and `auth/oob:requestExpired`. The flow compared them against bare names, so neither code ever got its own message. Codes are now matched on the name after the colon.

## Why no server change

`affinidi-webvh-service` #253 returns the one `notAuthorized` for an ACL miss, a bad proof and a replay. The ACL check also runs *before* proof verification. A distinct "not on the list" code would let anyone who can open a sign-in request find out whether a DID is on the operator's ACL without proving control of it. The VTC makes the same choice for the same reason (T15). Reading the code as "not listed" is safe here because the proof came from the member's own VTA and the wallet checked it (`assertSignedAsSent`) before sending. This applies only when the verified document is DID hosting. A VTC's `notAuthorized` keeps the generic message.

Every DID hosting document that advertises `SignInPortal` also advertises `WebVHHosting`: the daemon `setup.rs` and `setup_recipe/apply.rs` add both.

## Compatibility

- No manifest change: no new permissions or host matches.
- No new dependencies.
- Stored data is unchanged, and the entry shape is the legacy one.
- `login`, `proxyLogin` and `walletProfile` behave as before. Their binding logic moved into `bindProfile`, and the behaviour is identical.
- No VTA change is needed.

## Tests

- `sign-in-flows.test.mts`:
  - unknown DID hosting → join → confirm → claim/prove as the chosen DID;
  - Not now / closing sends zero requests to the site and records nothing;
  - wrong origin on an unknown site (DID hosting and VTC) is still refused before any offer;
  - `notAuthorized` → DID shown, for a new entry and for an existing one;
  - a VTC's `notAuthorized` stays generic;
  - an unknown VTC → not-member, with no offer;
  - joining with a DID that wasn't offered is refused;
  - a failed vault write ends the flow and sends nothing;
  - family-qualified codes.
- `sign-in-view.render.test.mts`: the offer screen, picking a DID and going on to confirm, Not now, an agent with no DIDs, VTC not-member, and the not-listed screen with Copy.
- `first-use-profile.test.mts`: `bindProfile`.

`npm run lint`, `npm test` and `npm run build` pass.

## Docs

- README sign-in section.
- `design-docs/sign-in-trigger-link-contract.md`: C3 steps 2–4 and a new C10. `design-docs` is not a git repo, so that file was edited in place.
- `design-docs/sign-in-plugin-test-runbook.md` §9.

## Pre-merge checklist

```
- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2) — no new network clients; uses the existing VTA session and DID resolver
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3)
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1) — the vault entry is the remote effect; a retry after it finds the entry and takes the known path
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4) — no retries added
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5) — n/a
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6) — n/a
- [x] New/changed wire types: camelCase, deny_unknown_fields where security-relevant, schema registered, all consumers (incl. JS) updated (R3.*) — internal bridge types only; refusal codes matched on stable codes (R3.7)
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive; fail-closed if enforcement can't start (R5.*) — an unrecognised document is "not a member"; nothing is offered
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified; background-job failures are surfaced (R6.*) — the offer names only the verified origin; the failure log carries no DID
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1)
- [x] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers — none
```

title: feat(sign-in): offer to use an unknown DID hosting service, and name the DID it has not listed (#315)
body:
feat(sign-in): offer to use an unknown DID hosting service, and name the DID it has not listed (#315)

A trigger link from a site the wallet did not know dead-ended on "Not one
of your communities". The flow now resolves and verifies the site's DID
document and holds the page-origin-vs-portal check before offering
anything, and still sends nothing to the site until the person agrees.

- A verified document with a `WebVHHosting` service is a DID hosting
  service: "Use <host> to host your DIDs?" with the agent's DIDs to pick
  from. Yes records it with the legacy first-use vault entry
  (`bindProfile`, now shared with proxyLogin/walletProfile/login: a
  didSelfIssued entry targeting the portal origin and the service DID),
  then continues straight to the normal confirm for the same link.
- Anything else (a VTC) stays "Not one of your communities", now with
  its verified sign-in page. No VTC join path exists in the wallet.
- A DID hosting service answering `auth/oob:notAuthorized` at prove shows
  "<host> hasn't added you yet. Send this DID to its operator:" with the
  DID and a Copy button, for a new or an existing entry.
- Refusal codes are matched on their stable name after the family
  prefix, so the services' `auth/oob/claim:alreadyClaimed` and
  `auth/oob:requestExpired` get their own messages again.

No new permissions, host matches or dependencies; stored data and the
legacy login paths are unchanged.

title: trust-tasks-rs-v0.28.1
body:
### Added

- **vtc**: Wallet presentation sessions for a join — start and status ([#745](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/745))

A VTC is becoming an OpenID4VP 1.0 verifier so that a swiyu or EUDI wallet
  can present an SD-JWT VC as evidence for a community join. Such a wallet has
  no DID agent: it cannot sign a Trust Task or receive a pushed document, and
  speaks only OpenID4VP over HTTPS.

  vtc/join-requests/wallet-session/start/0.1 lets the applicant, who does sign
  Trust Tasks, begin that exchange on the wallet's behalf. It opens a
  short-lived session bound to the proof signer, to one criterion version
  (named by the manifest's requirementsDigest, as submit/0.3 names it) and
  optionally to an existing join request, and returns the wallet invocation
  URI, the prefixed client_id the key-binding JWT will name, and the
  criterion's published DCQL query unchanged. The wallet-facing request_uri
  (signed JAR, RFC 9101) and response_uri (direct_post.jwt) are OpenID4VP's
  wire and outside the task.

  vtc/join-requests/wallet-session/status/0.1 lets the applicant read the
  outcome: the session state, and once presented, whether the query was
  satisfied, the holder key and which credentials were presented — never
  claim values — or, when refused, why. Only the applicant who began the
  session can read it.

  The wallet's presentation becomes evidence on the applicant's join, never
  the applicant's identity: the holder key is recorded beside the applicant
  DID, not instead of it.

  Companion specification change: trustoverip/dtgwg-vti-spec#60
  (foreign-protocol interfaces, VTI-OPS-095–099; VTI-CRD-024/025).
  Tracking: OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#1988.

| `trust_tasks` | pub.dev | `0.6.0` → `0.6.1` | patch |

What merging does, per registry (all in `publish.yml`, each keyed on "this
version is not published yet"):

- **crates.io** — `release-plz-release` tags `<crate>-v<version>`, publishes in
  dependency order and creates a GitHub Release per crate. Bump levels come from
  `cargo-semver-checks`.
- **npm** — `publish-npm` publishes with OIDC provenance and tags
  `<prefix>-v<version>`.
- **Go** — `publish-go` builds, vets and tests, then pushes the tag, which *is*
  the publication. **Irreversible**: proxy.golang.org never forgets a tag.
- **pub.dev** — `tag-dart` verifies against the *published* core and pushes the
  tag; `publish-dart.yml` publishes from it.

The npm, Go and Dart bumps are only as accurate as the commit subjects — nothing
checks their APIs the way `cargo-semver-checks` checks the crates. Look for a
missing `!` before merging.

This branch is regenerated from `main` on every push, so do not commit to it —
edits are force-pushed away. See RELEASING.md.

title: feat(vti-common): log each TSP reply sent, with its route and timing
body:
## What and why

`vti_common::tsp_route::send_reply` was silent when a send succeeded, so an agent's log couldn't say whether it replied at all.

In a field incident (`gt-vta` behind `fpdev-mediator`), every request from a browser wallet timed out. The VTA logged `TSP trust-task dispatched … status=200 OK` for each one and nothing after it. That fits a reply sent and then lost just as well as a reply never sent. The wallet has since gained its own evidence (vta-browser-plugin #314: a TSP timeout now says whether any frame reached its socket), but the agent side still had no record.

Each reply the mediator accepts now logs one INFO line:
- the peer;
- the mediator it went through (`via`), plus the peer's own mediator (`to_mediator`) when the reply is nested;
- the size;
- the elapsed time, including the peer-mediator lookup, which can take up to 10 s.

"Sent" means the mediator accepted it, not that the peer received it, and the doc comment says so. Failures stay with the caller, which already reports them once per peer (`uncollected.observe_send`).

This covers both the VTA (`vta-service/src/messaging/tsp_transport.rs`) and the VTC (`vtc-service/src/messaging.rs`), which both reply through this function.

## Requirements

None.

## Backport

None.

## Checklist

- [x] Targets `main`
- [x] No `version =` edits in any `Cargo.toml`
- [x] `cargo fmt` and `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` are clean (`-p vti-common -p vta-service -p vtc-service`). `cargo test -p vti-common`: 686 passed. No new test: the change adds a log line and doesn't alter behaviour.

Changelog

## `vta-sdk`

## [0.65.0](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/compare/vta-sdk-v0.64.2...vta-sdk-v0.65.0) — 2026-10-11 ### Added - **rooms**: Room files — file keys, STREAM sealing and rooms/keys/file-key ([#2017](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2017)) * feat(rooms): file keys, STREAM sealing and blob manifests in vti-rooms Adds vti_rooms::files, the construction rooms/_shared/0.1/blobs.schema.json FileManifest specifies (trust-tasks-tf #739): a per-file key, HKDF-SHA256 over the epoch storage key salted with the fileId and bound to the room and epoch; ChaCha20-Poly1305 STREAM segments whose nonce counts and whose associated data carries the final flag, so truncation, reordering and splicing fail to authenticate; one sealed segment per transfer chunk; the blob manifest and its BlobRef (sha2-256 over JCS); Padmé padding; and streaming sealer and opener that refuse a file whose plaintext digest is not the one its author signed. The manifest and digests build without the mls feature so a host can check them; the keyed half is behind mls with the rest of the member half. SealedRoom gains file_key_for_seal and file_key_for_open, walking the epoch chain as open_record does. Test vectors in vti-rooms/tests/fixtures/file-vectors.json. - P-256 and secp256k1 members — Trust Task proofs, rotation and OID4VCI key binding ([#1988](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1988)) ([#2021](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2021)) #2010 accepted P-256 and secp256k1 for credentials others issue. A member holding such a key — a secure-enclave or EUDI-wallet key, `did:key:zDn…` / `did:key:zQ3s…` — still could not sign as one: the SDK signed Trust Tasks Ed25519 only, and the VTC's hex holder signatures and OID4VCI key-binding proof read every key as Ed25519. Every one of these now goes through `vta_sdk::jws::JwsKey`, so the key decides the algorithm and nothing in the request can choose one. - Trust Task proofs: the shared verifier already accepted `ecdsa-jcs-2019` (P-256) once phase 1 taught the VM resolver P-256 keys; a test now holds it. `trust_task_sign` signs `ecdsa-jcs-2019` for a P-256 holder — a private multibase with the `p256-priv` prefix, or a bare one beside a `did:key:zDn…`. The Trust Tasks framework has every consumer SHOULD-verify that suite, for hardware-backed signers. There is no secp256k1 Data Integrity suite, so a secp256k1 key signs no Trust Task. - `vtc/members/rotate`: the old and new signatures (hex, 64 bytes) may be EdDSA, ES256 or ES256K by the key that made them; ECDSA is `r || s` over the SHA-256 of the canonical bytes, as JWS encodes it. The `did:webvh` path resolves `#key-0` through `TrustTaskVmResolver` (bound to authentication, VTI-KEY-022, with the cached-document refresh, VTI-KEY-134) instead of reading Ed25519 bytes off the document. Join's REST holder binding shares the same verifier. - OID4VCI key-binding proof: `EdDSA`, `ES256` or `ES256K`, whichever the `kid`'s key signs; a header naming another is refused before the signature. `DidVmResolver::resolve_verifying_key` (Ed25519) becomes `resolve_jws_key`. - `vta_sdk::jws`: `JwsKey::from_did_key`, and `verify_signature` is public for signatures that are not a JWS. What the workspace mints, and every key `sealed_transfer` seals to, stays Ed25519 / X25519: the VTA's sealed credential delivery (`seal_issued_credential`) still needs an Ed25519 `did:key` holder, and a sign-in `sessionKey` is still Ed25519. Accepting more algorithms widens what VTI-KEY-013 (retirable algorithms) would have to retire; that requirement is already an open divergence in the specification's register. - **vta**: External accounts — short-lived provider credentials with no inbound surface ([#2016](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2016)) * feat(vta): external-accounts capabilities and keyspaces Adds the two capabilities the external/* family (trust-tasks-tf #740) gates on: external-accounts-manage, derived by admin alone, and external-auth-use, derived by every role that holds sign (the account's binding, not the role, bounds a consumer). Both are non-additive members of the non-exhaustive Capability enum. Registers two keyspaces: external_accounts (settings, bindings, state) in BACKED_UP, and external_secrets (wrapped provider secrets) in EXCLUDED_FROM_BACKUP, so a portable password-protected backup is never a way to take a provider secret away. DID deletion: an account's binding names its consumer, so external_accounts blocks; external_secrets is unrelated. The device-binding Capability registry (device/_shared 0.2) does not list the two yet, so device listings carry them under ext until it does. - Read IETF Token Status Lists for SD-JWT VCs, signed by the credential's issuer ([#1988](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1988)) ([#2015](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2015)) An SD-JWT VC from the swiyu stack or an EUDI issuer names its status as `status.status_list = { idx, uri }`, a `statuslist+jwt`. The VTC fed that reference to the W3C Bitstring fetcher, which could never read it (Unknown at every join), and the vault held such credentials Unknown for good. Both now read it, through affinidi-status-list 0.1.7's `token` module. - `vta_sdk::token_status_list` (new): `verify_status_list_token` and `resolve_token_status`. A list decides revocation, so it is trusted only as the credential issuer's: the token's `kid` must name one of that issuer's `assertionMethod` keys (`sd_jwt_issuer_method`), the signature is checked with that key's algorithm (`JwsKey`) before the payload is read, and an `iss` naming anyone else is refused. `typ`, `sub` = the referenced `uri`, `iat` and `exp` are checked by the TDK, and the list is decompressed under a cap. The fetch is SSRF-guarded, takes no redirects and caps the body. A separate Status Issuer linked by certificate chain (draft §13.5) is not supported; its lists are refused. - `vta-vault`: `StatusListResolver::resolve_token_status` (a defaulted method, so existing resolvers compile and refuse) is implemented by `HttpStatusListResolver`. `refresh_status`, which the present gate runs first, takes the Token path when a credential carries `status.status_list` and no W3C `credentialStatus`: `INVALID` → `Revoked` (terminal), `SUSPENDED` → `Revoked` tagged `tokenStatus:suspended` so a later `VALID` restores it, an application-specific or unregistered value → `Unknown` (VTI-CRD-012). Receive still stores such a credential `Unknown`: its status has not been read until that refresh. - `vtc-service`: `StatusListFetcher::check_token_status`, implemented by the verifying `HttpStatusListFetcher`. `resolve_presented_status` (join, join criteria, invitations) maps `VALID` / `INVALID` / `SUSPENDED` to Valid / Revoked / Suspended, and anything unreadable to Unknown for the join policy. - `affinidi-status-list` 0.1.3 → 0.1.7. `docs/03-vtc/credentials.md` gains *Reading another issuer's status*. - Verify ES256 / ES256K SD-JWT-VCs from did:web and did:webvh issuers ([#1988](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1988)) ([#2010](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2010)) Credentials issued on the swiyu stack and the EUDI profiles could not be received or verified: the vault and the VTC verifier accepted only EdDSA, the vault only a `did:key` issuer, the shared resolver only a `publicKeyMultibase` key, and holder binding only an Ed25519 `cnf.jwk`. - `vta_sdk::jws` (new): compact-JWS verification over a resolved key — EdDSA, ES256 (P-256) and ES256K (secp256k1). The header's `alg` must be the one the resolved key's curve signs with, checked before the signature; `crit` is refused. `JwsKey::from_jwk` reads a `cnf.jwk` (refusing one that carries `d`), `did_key()` names a P-256 holder `did:key:zDn…` and a secp256k1 one `did:key:zQ3s…`. `sd_jwt_issuer_method` binds the issuer JWS `kid` to `iss`: a `did:key` issuer's own key whatever the fragment, any other DID must name its method with a DID-URL `kid` (VTI-CRD-002: the issuer is resolved, not guessed). - `TrustTaskVmResolver` reads a `publicKeyJwk` method (Ed25519, X25519, P-256, secp256k1) and a secp256k1 Multikey; PQC keys stay Multikey-only. - `vta-vault`: `receive_sd_jwt_vc` and `stored_claims` take the issuer resolver, so a `did:web` / `did:webvh` issuer resolves for `assertionMethod`. `receive` with `IssuerKey::None` resolves locally (`did:key` / `did:peer`); the VTA's issued-credential path passes its DID cache. A credential carrying an IETF `status.status_list` reference is stored `Unknown`, not `Valid`: no `statuslist+jwt` resolver exists yet, so its status cannot be read (VTI-CRD-012). - `vtc-service`: the SD-JWT-VC presentation verifier takes ES256 / ES256K issuers and P-256 / secp256k1 `cnf.jwk` holders. - **vtc**: Member portal, with wallet sign-in by trigger link ([#2007](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2007)) * feat(vtc): a member portal at /members, and a home page that explains the community Members could not sign in anywhere: VTC sign-in admitted administrators only, and every session it minted read as an admin session. This adds a member portal as a separate application from the console, with the separation enforced by the daemon rather than by what each page shows. Member portal (`crate::member_portal`, `routes::member_portal`): - Only an active member signs in — a live ACL entry that is not expired, suspended or an `application` entry, plus a member record that has not been removed — checked at challenge (VTI-SES-006/007 via the shared handler), at authentication, on every refresh and on every request (VTI-SES-020..022). - Sign-in by the browser wallet (SIOPv2 at `/v1/member/wallet`) or a portal passkey only. A passkey is added from the portal after a wallet sign-in; adding or removing one requires a wallet-proven session (`amr` contains `did`). Audited as the new `MemberPasskeyChanged` event. - Tokens carry audience `VTC-member` (`JwtKeys::for_audience`), so console extractors refuse them and the portal refuses console tokens. - Sessions and passkeys live in their own keyspaces (`member_sessions`, `member_passkeys`, excluded from backup), so a member who is also an administrator cannot redeem a portal refresh token or passkey at the console. - Cookies `vtc_member_session` / `vtc_member_refresh` are `Path=/v1/member`; `vtc_member_csrf` is the portal's own double-submit value, and the CSRF gate picks the cookie pair by path. - The portal is its own Vite bundle (`vite.members.config.ts`), baked by build.rs into `$OUT_DIR/member-ui-dist` and served at `/members/`; it loads no console code. ## [0.16.0](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/compare/vta-vault-v0.15.0...vta-vault-v0.16.0) — 2026-10-11 ### Added - Read IETF Token Status Lists for SD-JWT VCs, signed by the credential's issuer ([#1988](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1988)) ([#2015](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2015)) An SD-JWT VC from the swiyu stack or an EUDI issuer names its status as `status.status_list = { idx, uri }`, a `statuslist+jwt`. The VTC fed that reference to the W3C Bitstring fetcher, which could never read it (Unknown at every join), and the vault held such credentials Unknown for good. Both now read it, through affinidi-status-list 0.1.7's `token` module. - `vta_sdk::token_status_list` (new): `verify_status_list_token` and `resolve_token_status`. A list decides revocation, so it is trusted only as the credential issuer's: the token's `kid` must name one of that issuer's `assertionMethod` keys (`sd_jwt_issuer_method`), the signature is checked with that key's algorithm (`JwsKey`) before the payload is read, and an `iss` naming anyone else is refused. `typ`, `sub` = the referenced `uri`, `iat` and `exp` are checked by the TDK, and the list is decompressed under a cap. The fetch is SSRF-guarded, takes no redirects and caps the body. A separate Status Issuer linked by certificate chain (draft §13.5) is not supported; its lists are refused. - `vta-vault`: `StatusListResolver::resolve_token_status` (a defaulted method, so existing resolvers compile and refuse) is implemented by `HttpStatusListResolver`. `refresh_status`, which the present gate runs first, takes the Token path when a credential carries `status.status_list` and no W3C `credentialStatus`: `INVALID` → `Revoked` (terminal), `SUSPENDED` → `Revoked` tagged `tokenStatus:suspended` so a later `VALID` restores it, an application-specific or unregistered value → `Unknown` (VTI-CRD-012). Receive still stores such a credential `Unknown`: its status has not been read until that refresh. - `vtc-service`: `StatusListFetcher::check_token_status`, implemented by the verifying `HttpStatusListFetcher`. `resolve_presented_status` (join, join criteria, invitations) maps `VALID` / `INVALID` / `SUSPENDED` to Valid / Revoked / Suspended, and anything unreadable to Unknown for the join policy. - `affinidi-status-list` 0.1.3 → 0.1.7. `docs/03-vtc/credentials.md` gains *Reading another issuer's status*. - Verify ES256 / ES256K SD-JWT-VCs from did:web and did:webvh issuers ([#1988](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1988)) ([#2010](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2010)) Credentials issued on the swiyu stack and the EUDI profiles could not be received or verified: the vault and the VTC verifier accepted only EdDSA, the vault only a `did:key` issuer, the shared resolver only a `publicKeyMultibase` key, and holder binding only an Ed25519 `cnf.jwk`. - `vta_sdk::jws` (new): compact-JWS verification over a resolved key — EdDSA, ES256 (P-256) and ES256K (secp256k1). The header's `alg` must be the one the resolved key's curve signs with, checked before the signature; `crit` is refused. `JwsKey::from_jwk` reads a `cnf.jwk` (refusing one that carries `d`), `did_key()` names a P-256 holder `did:key:zDn…` and a secp256k1 one `did:key:zQ3s…`. `sd_jwt_issuer_method` binds the issuer JWS `kid` to `iss`: a `did:key` issuer's own key whatever the fragment, any other DID must name its method with a DID-URL `kid` (VTI-CRD-002: the issuer is resolved, not guessed). - `TrustTaskVmResolver` reads a `publicKeyJwk` method (Ed25519, X25519, P-256, secp256k1) and a secp256k1 Multikey; PQC keys stay Multikey-only. - `vta-vault`: `receive_sd_jwt_vc` and `stored_claims` take the issuer resolver, so a `did:web` / `did:webvh` issuer resolves for `assertionMethod`. `receive` with `IssuerKey::None` resolves locally (`did:key` / `did:peer`); the VTA's issued-credential path passes its DID cache. A credential carrying an IETF `status.status_list` reference is stored `Unknown`, not `Valid`: no `statuslist+jwt` resolver exists yet, so its status cannot be read (VTI-CRD-012). - `vtc-service`: the SD-JWT-VC presentation verifier takes ES256 / ES256K issuers and P-256 / secp256k1 `cnf.jwk` holders.
## `vta-service`
## [0.57.0](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/compare/vta-service-v0.56.0...vta-service-v0.57.0) — 2026-10-11 ### Added - **rooms**: Room files — file keys, STREAM sealing and rooms/keys/file-key ([#2017](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2017)) * feat(rooms): file keys, STREAM sealing and blob manifests in vti-rooms Adds vti_rooms::files, the construction rooms/_shared/0.1/blobs.schema.json FileManifest specifies (trust-tasks-tf #739): a per-file key, HKDF-SHA256 over the epoch storage key salted with the fileId and bound to the room and epoch; ChaCha20-Poly1305 STREAM segments whose nonce counts and whose associated data carries the final flag, so truncation, reordering and splicing fail to authenticate; one sealed segment per transfer chunk; the blob manifest and its BlobRef (sha2-256 over JCS); Padmé padding; and streaming sealer and opener that refuse a file whose plaintext digest is not the one its author signed. The manifest and digests build without the mls feature so a host can check them; the keyed half is behind mls with the rest of the member half. SealedRoom gains file_key_for_seal and file_key_for_open, walking the epoch chain as open_record does. Test vectors in vti-rooms/tests/fixtures/file-vectors.json. - **vta**: External accounts — short-lived provider credentials with no inbound surface ([#2016](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2016)) * feat(vta): external-accounts capabilities and keyspaces Adds the two capabilities the external/* family (trust-tasks-tf #740) gates on: external-accounts-manage, derived by admin alone, and external-auth-use, derived by every role that holds sign (the account's binding, not the role, bounds a consumer). Both are non-additive members of the non-exhaustive Capability enum. Registers two keyspaces: external_accounts (settings, bindings, state) in BACKED_UP, and external_secrets (wrapped provider secrets) in EXCLUDED_FROM_BACKUP, so a portable password-protected backup is never a way to take a provider secret away. DID deletion: an account's binding names its consumer, so external_accounts blocks; external_secrets is unrelated. The device-binding Capability registry (device/_shared 0.2) does not list the two yet, so device listings carry them under ext until it does. - Verify ES256 / ES256K SD-JWT-VCs from did:web and did:webvh issuers ([#1988](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1988)) ([#2010](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2010)) Credentials issued on the swiyu stack and the EUDI profiles could not be received or verified: the vault and the VTC verifier accepted only EdDSA, the vault only a `did:key` issuer, the shared resolver only a `publicKeyMultibase` key, and holder binding only an Ed25519 `cnf.jwk`. - `vta_sdk::jws` (new): compact-JWS verification over a resolved key — EdDSA, ES256 (P-256) and ES256K (secp256k1). The header's `alg` must be the one the resolved key's curve signs with, checked before the signature; `crit` is refused. `JwsKey::from_jwk` reads a `cnf.jwk` (refusing one that carries `d`), `did_key()` names a P-256 holder `did:key:zDn…` and a secp256k1 one `did:key:zQ3s…`. `sd_jwt_issuer_method` binds the issuer JWS `kid` to `iss`: a `did:key` issuer's own key whatever the fragment, any other DID must name its method with a DID-URL `kid` (VTI-CRD-002: the issuer is resolved, not guessed). - `TrustTaskVmResolver` reads a `publicKeyJwk` method (Ed25519, X25519, P-256, secp256k1) and a secp256k1 Multikey; PQC keys stay Multikey-only. - `vta-vault`: `receive_sd_jwt_vc` and `stored_claims` take the issuer resolver, so a `did:web` / `did:webvh` issuer resolves for `assertionMethod`. `receive` with `IssuerKey::None` resolves locally (`did:key` / `did:peer`); the VTA's issued-credential path passes its DID cache. A credential carrying an IETF `status.status_list` reference is stored `Unknown`, not `Valid`: no `statuslist+jwt` resolver exists yet, so its status cannot be read (VTI-CRD-012). - `vtc-service`: the SD-JWT-VC presentation verifier takes ES256 / ES256K issuers and P-256 / secp256k1 `cnf.jwk` holders. - **vta-sdk**: Wallet sign-in with a trigger link: sign auth/oob grants, enrol UV keys, advertise TrustTaskHTTPS and SignInPortal ([#1997](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1997)) * feat(vta-sdk)!: sign auth/oob/grant for assertionMethod (VTI-KEY-106) Adds `auth/oob/grant` to `ATTESTATION_SLUGS`, so `vault/sign-trust-task` signs a wallet sign-in grant for `assertionMethod`: the grant ("let this browser key act as me at this origin until notAfter") is the approving DID's attestation, which the service relies on to open a session, and it verifies the grant against `assertionMethod` (sign-in trigger-link contract C5, base design §10). `auth/oob/identify` stays operational and is signed for `authentication`, as the service verifies it; the other `auth/oob` documents are not attestations either. Both are pinned in the classifier tests. ### Build & CI - Trust-tasks-rs 0.28, affinidi-messaging-sdk 0.34 and affinidi-tdk 0.24 ([#2028](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2028)) Moves the workspace to trust-tasks-rs 0.28 (with capability-client, https, didcomm, tsp and proof) in lockstep with the Affinidi messaging crates built against it (affinidi-tdk-rs #933): affinidi-messaging-sdk 0.34, affinidi-tdk 0.24, mediator-admin / mediator-tui 0.9 (pnm messaging console) and test-mediator 0.20. The lock holds one trust-tasks-rs, one trust-tasks-proof, one SDK and one tdk: `MediatorAcl` crosses the SDK's API, so a graph holding two trust-tasks-rs does not compile. 0.28's one break, the rooms 0.1 `NOT_AUTHORIZED` constants withdrawn for the standard `permissionDenied` (trust-tasks-tf #743), touches nothing here: the room host already answers `permissionDenied`. It carries `DeclaredErrorCode::details_schema` / `check_details` (trust-tasks-tf #742), so the rooms/keys/file-key handler tests check `unknownEpoch` details against the schema the specification declares rather than a hand copy, and vta-service's jsonschema dev-dependency, which existed only for that copy, is dropped. Publishing a vta-sdk on SDK 0.34 / tdk 0.24 is step 2 of the crossing affinidi-tdk-rs's workspace-duplicates-allow.txt records; step 3 moves the mediator's vta-sdk requirement to it there. - Trust-tasks-rs 0.27.8, with auth/oob on its generated types ([#2011](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2011)) * build: trust-tasks-rs 0.27.8 — auth/oob, room files and external accounts ### Fixed - **auth**: Bound wallet sign-in sessions by the grant's notAfter across refresh ([#2026](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2026)) A wallet sign-in (`auth/oob/*`) grant carries `notAfter`, the latest moment the member approved the session for, and redeem reports it. The member-portal mint clamped only the first window to it — the comment "refreshing cannot extend it" was false: `handle_refresh` reset both expiries to now + the full TTL on every rotation, so a session approved for an hour could be renewed indefinitely. The console session minted by wallet sign-in (`mint_admin_cookie_session`, #2014) ignored `notAfter` entirely, and reported the refresh deadline as `notAfter`. - **vta**: Check an extension passkey's rpIdHash against its chrome-extension:// origin ([#2020](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2020)) Chrome requires an extension to pass its bare runtime id as rp.id but signs the assertion over SHA-256("chrome-extension://"), so every browser-plugin grant was refused with oobUvInvalid ("authenticatorData.rpIdHash does not match expected rp_id"). Verify an extension passkey against its origin; web passkeys and stored enrolments are unchanged. ### Performance - **vta-service**: Multi-core REST and direct vsock inbound, failing closed ([#2005](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2005)) * perf(vta-service): serve REST on one worker per CPU The REST server ran on its own current-thread tokio runtime, so every REST handler shared one thread and the VTA could use at most one CPU however many it had. In a Nitro enclave this showed as a 2-vCPU enclave half idle at its ceiling (47%/62% per vCPU), with storage replies waiting for that one thread to poll them. With more than one CPU the REST runtime is now multi-threaded, one worker per CPU. With one CPU it stays current-thread: a multi-threaded runtime was measurably worse there (1-vCPU enclave at 220 keys/sign per second: 463 errors against 2). title: feat(vtc): wallet presentation sessions for a join — start and status
body:
A VTC is becoming an OpenID4VP 1.0 verifier so that a swiyu or EUDI wallet
can present an SD-JWT VC as evidence for a community join. Such a wallet has
no DID agent: it cannot sign a Trust Task or receive a pushed document, and
speaks only OpenID4VP over HTTPS.

vtc/join-requests/wallet-session/start/0.1 lets the applicant, who does sign
Trust Tasks, begin that exchange on the wallet's behalf. It opens a
short-lived session bound to the proof signer, to one criterion version
(named by the manifest's requirementsDigest, as submit/0.3 names it) and
optionally to an existing join request, and returns the wallet invocation
URI, the prefixed client_id the key-binding JWT will name, and the
criterion's published DCQL query unchanged. The wallet-facing request_uri
(signed JAR, RFC 9101) and response_uri (direct_post.jwt) are OpenID4VP's
wire and outside the task.

vtc/join-requests/wallet-session/status/0.1 lets the applicant read the
outcome: the session state, and once presented, whether the query was
satisfied, the holder key and which credentials were presented — never
claim values — or, when refused, why. Only the applicant who began the
session can read it.

The wallet's presentation becomes evidence on the applicant's join, never
the applicant's identity: the holder key is recorded beside the applicant
DID, not instead of it.

Companion specification change: trustoverip/dtgwg-vti-spec#60
(foreign-protocol interfaces, VTI-OPS-095–099; VTI-CRD-024/025).
Tracking: OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#1988.

body:
A proposed change to #58, opened against `feat/trigger-links` so that whether to take it stays your call. The reasoning, and the points where the text could be more precise, are in the comment on #58.

The change keeps the trigger-link format protocol-neutral, and makes the Trust Task first request VTI's adoption of it:
- **Design principles** at the top of the chapter, citing the Abstract and Layering.
- **The chapter split in two:** "The trigger-link format" and "VTI's use of trigger links".
- **VTI-LNK-054 made general.** Each flow states its first request, sent after approval, over the transport chosen under 053, and with the handle.
- **New VTI-LNK-057.** VTI's registry flows use the Trust Task first request. VTI-LNK-113 now points at 057.
- **VTI-LNK-055 made protocol-neutral.**
- **"Anyone may define a flow"**, and the shared host described as a convenience.
- **A note proposing** that the format later moves to its own component spec, deferred until it has settled.

No VTI flow, outcome or requirement number changes.

title: feat(sync): keep account state at the VTA so every device sees it
body:
## Why

A user reported: archive a VTC on one machine, open the same context on another, and the archive isn't there. None of OpenVTC's own state reached the VTA. The VTA held keys, DIDs and credentials, but flags, relationships, contacts and the rest lived only in each machine's local config.

The VTA's app-state store (`vta/app-state/*`, VTI #1029) was what `docs/design/vta-authoritative-state.md` step 5 was blocked on. It has shipped, and vta-sdk 0.63.3 (already pinned) has the client. This PR is the writer.

## What

**`openvtc_core::vta_sync`** stores one record per item (D8a) in namespace `openvtc` of the account's top context:

| Synced | Stays local |
|---|---|
| personas, memberships (incl. archived/favourite/acknowledged), relationships, contacts, positive agent names, TSP rows, VRCs, VTA-managed key refs, vetting state | tasks, activity log, kept inbound messages, replay records, **locally-held keys**, **hidden-vetting engine** (secrets) |

- **Sync cycle:** pull the change feed since the watermark, falling back to a snapshot on `watermarkTooOld`. Merge each record three-way against its last agreed version (stored in `ProtectedConfig.vta_sync`), then push with `expectedVersion`. A lost race returns the winner's value, which is merged and pushed again.
- **Conflicts:** different fields edited on two devices both survive. The same field edited on both takes the VTA's value and is reported in the activity log.
- **At load:** runs in `load_step2` before persona hydration, so a persona, relationship or key ref created elsewhere comes up straight away. 20 s budget; it never fails the load.
- **At runtime:** after each save and every 60 s, spawned off the loop. Results are merged back on the loop, which stays the single mutator. Backoff via `vta_sync_driver`.
- **Next launch:** persona, relationship, key, TSP and vetting changes from another device are held and applied then (they need hydration).
- **Unknown records:** records from a newer build (envelope `schemaVersion`) are held, not applied. A record over the size cap is reported once and not offered again until it changes.

`docs/design/vta-authoritative-state.md` records what was built. **Deviation from D8c/D14:** a same-field conflict resolves to the VTA's value with a log line. The design proposed an acknowledge-and-continue step. `expectedVersion` is still on every write, so nothing is overwritten unseen.

## Behaviour changes to note

- A State-A account (context, no persona) now opens a VTA session at load so it can pull. If the VTA is unreachable it still loads, just without the sync. Accounts with personas fail to load when the VTA is unreachable, as before.
- **First sync on a device with history:** there is no base to compare against, so a field that differs takes the VTA's value. Whichever device syncs first sets the shared state.
- The recovery screen's gaps list now says that synced copies come back on first launch.

## Tests

- Unit: merge rules, plus two-device scenarios against an in-memory store with the VTA's version, conflict and tombstone semantics:
  - archive propagates to a running device
  - concurrent edits to different fields merge
  - a same-field edit is reported
  - a new persona waits for the next launch
  - deletion, and snapshot fallback after tombstones are reaped
  - an Imported key never leaves the device
  - too-large, unsupported VTA, newer-format record
- Driver: cycle spacing, timer, backoff, disable.
- E2E (`openvtc-core/tests/vta_sync_e2e.rs`, `#[ignore]`d like the other MockVta tests): a real in-process VTA, archive on A then open on B, plus concurrent field edits. It works around **VTI #2029** (`highWatermark: 0` on an unwritten namespace fails MockVta's response-conformance check) by seeding the namespace first.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check` are clean.
- Known failure: `vetting_actions::tests::no_ticket_is_issued_for_requests_that_cannot_be_attested` depends on the clock and fails identically on `main`. It is unrelated to this PR.

## Pre-merge checklist

- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2). Every call goes through vta-sdk's Trust-Task dispatch with the app-state timeout; the load-time sync also has a 20 s overall budget.
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3). The network half runs on owned data; the merge happens on the loop.
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1). Local edits are saved first by design (write-behind, D8c). Base versions advance only on a confirmed `written`, so an interrupted push is retried and converges through `expectedVersion`.
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4). Pages are capped at 500, load rounds at 3, and runtime backoff runs 30 s to 10 min. Writes always carry `expectedVersion`, so a replay conflicts instead of double-writing.
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5). A transient error backs off and retries; unsupported or refused disables sync for the session.
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6). A remote delete is sent only for a record whose local removal has been saved, conditional on the base version.
- [x] New/changed wire types (R3.*). No new wire types; this uses the published `vta/app-state/*` 1.0 via the SDK. Checked against the real service with MockVta, which surfaced VTI #2029.
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive; fail-closed if enforcement can't start (R5.*). Without a VTA or the store, nothing syncs and local behaviour is unchanged.
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified; background-job failures are surfaced (R6.*). "Applied N changes" counts only applied merges. Errors are distinguished: unreachable, refused, VTA without the store, contract mismatch (R6.4).
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1). A crash before save loses only bookkeeping; the next sync re-pulls, and since merging identical values is a no-op it converges.
- [x] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers. None from the guide. The design-doc deviation (D8c/D14 conflict handling) is described above.

title: A foreign-protocol interface serves an exchange a task began, and is a binding rather than a parallel interface (VTI-OPS-095 – 099, VTI-CRD-024 – 025)
body:
Some counterparties cannot meet a node on the task surface. A credential wallet that speaks OpenID4VP signs no operation document and receives no message a node sends. VTI-OPS-002 left only two options: refuse them, or open a second way in.

**Operations (`08-operations.md`, new section *Foreign-protocol interfaces*)**
- **VTI-OPS-095** defines a foreign-protocol interface: an endpoint whose wire an external protocol fixes, for a counterparty that cannot produce an operation document. One that meets 096–099 is not a parallel interface under VTI-OPS-002.
- **VTI-OPS-096:** it serves an exchange a catalogue task began, begins no operation of its own, and is reachable only within that exchange.
- **VTI-OPS-097:** it confers no authority. What arrives is evidence, and the decision is taken under the beginning task's authority.
- **VTI-OPS-098:** the exchange is single-use and expires, and the interface meets its own protocol's security requirements in full.
- **VTI-OPS-099:** the outcome is readable through a task, and each interface is documented with the task it serves.

**Credentials (`09-credentials.md`, *Presentation*)**
- **VTI-CRD-024:** a presentation that arrives this way names the verifier's identifier in that protocol as its audience (for OpenID4VP, the client identifier, prefix included), and commits to the beginning task's challenge.
- **VTI-CRD-025:** the holder of a presented credential and the party who began the exchange are kept apart unless the protocol binds them. Anyone who can see a cross-device code can answer it.

Motivation: OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#1988. The design is at `docs/05-design-notes/oid4vp-wallet-verifier.md` in that repository (merged in #2031).

A foreign-protocol interface serves an exchange a task began, and is a binding rather than a parallel interface (VTI-OPS-095 – 099, VTI-CRD-024 – 025) (#60)

Some counterparties cannot meet a node on the task surface: a credential wallet that speaks OpenID4VP signs no operation document and receives no message a node sends. VTI-OPS-002 left only refusing them or opening a second way in.

VTI-OPS-095 – 099 define a foreign-protocol interface: an endpoint whose wire an external protocol fixes, serving an exchange a catalogue task began. It begins no operation, confers no authority (what arrives is evidence for the task that began the exchange), is single-use and expiring, meets its own protocol's security requirements in full, and its outcome is readable through a task. VTI-CRD-024 fixes the audience and challenge of a presentation that arrives that way (for OpenID4VP, the verifier's client identifier, prefix included, and the beginning task's challenge).
