title: feat(diagnostics): a real round trip per transport in the self-test; say when no reply frame arrived
body:
## Why

In the `gt-vta` incident, the connection self-test passed every check while every request to the agent timed out. Each check was about reachability (DID resolves, origin allowed, socket open), and none waited for an answer. When requests did time out, the TSP error didn't say whether anything had arrived at all, so "the reply never came" had to be inferred from screenshots that happened to log no inbound frames.

## Change

- **A round trip per transport in the self-test.** It sends one timed `auth/whoami` over each advertised transport (TSP, DIDComm, REST). Each goes over a session built with only that transport, so the report says which path answers rather than which one the session picked.
  - An agent's **refusal counts as an answer**, because the path worked both ways. The refusal is shown as the next thing to fix (e.g. "DID not in ACL").
  - Probes ignore the REST cooldown from #309, since the point is to ask the path live traffic is avoiding.
  - A 12 s budget per probe, and they run one after another, because they share the warm socket.
  - `probeRoundTrip` lives in `core/src/vta/round-trip.ts` and is wallet-safe: `auth/whoami` is not one of the banned admin URIs. `round-trip-check.ts` holds the wording.
- **A TSP timeout says whether any frame reached the socket.** Zero frames means the reply was lost before the wallet, at the agent's send or at the mediator. A declined frame keeps its existing "last inbound frame declined: …" reason. Both put `framesSeen` in `details`.

## Tests

- `core/tests/tsp.timeout-diagnosis.mjs`: no frames vs a declined frame.
- `core/tests/vta.round-trip.mjs`: an answer, a refusal-as-answer, a local failure, and an uncoded throw.
- `extension/tests/round-trip-check.test.mts`: the check wording.
- Core 878, extension 998; lint and build clean.

## Pre-merge checklist

- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2): the probe has its own 12 s budget
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3)
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1): read-only probe
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4): no retry
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5): unchanged
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6): unchanged
- [x] New/changed wire types (R3.*): none; `auth/whoami/0.1` as declared
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive (R5.*): n/a
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified (R6.*): this is that
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1): no mutations
- [x] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers: none

body:
Design note for #1988 item 4: `docs/05-design-notes/oid4vp-wallet-verifier.md`.

- **Verification only.** Issuance into wallets is deferred.
- **One OID4VP 1.0 verifier core in the TDK**, with two verifier identities: a swiyu-profile `did:webvh` (`decentralized_identifier:`) and an EUDI X.509 access certificate (`x509_hash:`). Both are P-256 and VTA-held.
- **A wallet credential is evidence on a join** (Option A). The applicant keeps their OpenVTC/VTA DID and starts a presentation session with a signed Trust Task; the wallet presents into it. There are no wallet-only members.
- **Each VTC operator registers its own verifier identity** with swiyu or an EUDI registrar.
- **Spec work comes first (P0):** VTI-OPS-002 and foreign-protocol bindings in dtgwg-vti-spec, and the session Trust Tasks in dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf.
- **Also covered:** the requirements met (VTI-CRD-020…023, -002, -010…014, VTI-KEY-080/-013), the risks (cross-device relay, per-operator registration, moving profiles), and a P0–P5 plan.

body:
This PR moves the workspace to `trust-tasks-rs` 0.28 together with the Affinidi messaging crates built against it (affinidi-tdk-rs #933).

### Dependencies
| Crate | Version |
|---|---|
| `trust-tasks-rs`, `-capability-client`, `-https`, `-didcomm`, `-tsp`, `-proof` | 0.27 → 0.28 |
| `affinidi-messaging-sdk` | 0.33.2 → 0.34.0 |
| `affinidi-tdk` | 0.23 → 0.24 |
| `affinidi-messaging-mediator-admin` / `-tui` (pnm messaging console) | 0.8 → 0.9 |
| `affinidi-messaging-test-mediator` (dev, four crates) | 0.18 → 0.20 |

The lockfile holds one copy each of `trust-tasks-rs`, `trust-tasks-proof`, the SDK and tdk. That matters because `MediatorAcl` crosses the SDK's API: a graph holding two `trust-tasks-rs` versions fails with "expected `MediatorAcl`, found a different `MediatorAcl`". That failure is why this had to wait for #933.

### What 0.28 brings
- **The one breaking change:** the rooms 0.1 `NOT_AUTHORIZED` constants are withdrawn in favour of the standard `permissionDenied` (trust-tasks-tf #743). Nothing here uses them, and the room host already answers `permissionDenied`.
- **`DeclaredErrorCode::details_schema` / `check_details`** (trust-tasks-tf #742): the `rooms/keys/file-key` handler tests now check `unknownEpoch` details against the schema the spec declares, carried by the generated code. The hand copy is gone, and so is `vta-service`'s `jsonschema` dev-dependency, which existed only for it.

### Follow-up
Once a `vta-sdk` on SDK 0.34 / tdk 0.24 is published, affinidi-tdk-rs moves its mediator's `vta-sdk` requirement to it and deletes the two `workspace-duplicates-allow.txt` entries #933 added.

- **vtc nextest:** 2960 passed.

title: fix(tsp): share one relationship store across the offscreen document's TSP channels
body:
## Problem

The offscreen document builds a `TspChannel` per request and passed no `relationships` store, so each channel got an empty one. As a result:
- Every TSP request re-invited the VTA and waited up to 5 s for an accept before sending.
- Concurrent requests each sent an invite. Once the VTA had accepted the first and was `Bidirectional`, it refused the second's accept: `could not send a TSP relationship accept ... SendAccept in state Bidirectional`, seen in `gt-vta`'s logs.

## Change

- One `MemoryRelationshipStore` for the offscreen document's lifetime, keyed on the (holder, VTA) pair.
- A request now sees the relationship an earlier one formed, or the invite one already has outstanding.
- It stays in memory, so a teardown still leads to a fresh invite.
- A timed-out send still clears the record (`forgetOnFailure`), so a VTA that forgot the wallet is re-invited.

## Tests

`tsp.relationship.mjs`:
- channels sharing a store send one invite between them;
- the control: a channel with its own store invites again.

Full suites pass; lint clean.

## Pre-merge checklist

- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2)
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3)
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1)
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4)
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5): unchanged
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6): unchanged
- [x] New/changed wire types: camelCase, deny_unknown_fields where security-relevant, schema registered, all consumers (incl. JS) updated (R3.*)
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive; fail-closed if enforcement can't start (R5.*)
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified (R6.*)
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1)
- [x] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers: none

title: fix(rest): get the VTA bearer with pre-session Trust Tasks; the /auth/ routes are gone
body:
## Problem

vti #1858 (1 Oct, `VTI-Eucalyptus`) deleted `POST /auth/challenge` and the authcrypted `POST /auth/`, and moved pre-session auth onto `/trust-tasks`. The wallet still used the old routes. Every REST request to a VTA on that release therefore failed its sign-in: `POST /auth/challenge` → `405 Allow: GET,HEAD`, seen against `vta-gt.firstperson.dev`. That includes the REST fallback from #309, which made the fallback a dead end.

## Change

- `getVtaBearer` (`vta/auth.ts`) posts two Trust Tasks to `/trust-tasks` with no bearer, mirroring `vta-sdk/src/auth_light.rs`:
  - `auth/challenge/0.1`, carrying `payload.subject`. The VTA's handler requires it, though the spec makes it optional.
  - a holder-signed `auth/authenticate/0.2`, whose proof is the sign-in.
- Signing goes through `signOutboundTask`, like every channel. Replies are read with `decodeTrustTaskHttpReply`: signed by the VTA, threaded to the request, body before status (R3.7).
- `decodeTrustTaskHttpReply` / `decodeTrustTaskHttpAck` move to `vta/http-reply.ts` (re-exported from `rest-channel.ts`), so `auth.ts` doesn't import the channel that imports it.
- The bearer cache honours the token's `expiresIn`.
- Per CLAUDE.md, there is no fallback to the old routes; the VTA has removed them.
- CLAUDE.md's "not signed" section and the stale comments in `auth-tasks.ts`, `rest-channel.ts`, `vault/*` and `onboarding/swap.ts` are updated.

## Tests

- `vta.rest-net-policy.mjs` and `vta.rest-redirect.mjs` now run against a fake VTA that signs its replies. All the net-policy, redirect and blocked-endpoint guarantees still hold.
- New tests:
  - the two documents are sent, the challenge names the subject, and the authenticate proof verifies as the holder;
  - an unsigned reply is refused, so a token can't be planted;
  - a `trust-task-error` refusal surfaces its code.
- Live check: the challenge document sent to `vta-gt.firstperson.dev` gets a `200`, threaded and signed by the VTA. The authenticate step is not checked live, because it needs a DID on the VTA's access list.
- Core 870, extension 993; lint and build clean.

## Pre-merge checklist

- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2)
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3)
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1)
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4)
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5): unchanged
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6): unchanged
- [x] New/changed wire types: camelCase, deny_unknown_fields where security-relevant, schema registered, all consumers (incl. JS) updated (R3.*)
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive; fail-closed if enforcement can't start (R5.*)
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified (R6.*)
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1)

title: feat(vtc): local GeoIP for the wallet sign-in requester location
body:
## Summary

Wallet sign-in (`auth/oob`) shows the approver where the request came from as `requester.location`. Until now `oob::locate` was a stub, so every location was `"unknown"`, which the wallet shows as a warning. This PR implements the lookup against a **local `.mmdb` database only, with no third-party call** (base design §12.6).

- New `vtc_service::geoip::GeoIp`, carried on `AppState` as `state.geoip`. It replaces the `oob::locate` stub, and `handle_request` in `oob_tasks.rs` is the only caller.
- Reads **DB-IP "IP to City Lite"** (recommended) and **MaxMind GeoLite2 City**. Both use the GeoIP2 `City` record shape.
- Output is `"City, CC"` (English city name, ISO country code). When the record has no city it is the English country name, and otherwise `None`, which shows as `"unknown"`. The result is capped at the schema's `maxLength` of 128 characters and control characters are stripped.
- Addresses that are not public are never looked up: private, loopback, link-local, CGNAT `100.64/10`, unique-local `fc00::/7`, documentation (v4, `2001:db8::/32`, `3fff::/20`), benchmarking, multicast, reserved, and `0/8`. IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses are converted to IPv4 first.
- **Hot reload:** once a minute a background task (stopped by the shutdown signal) checks the file's mtime and size. When either changes it re-reads the file in `spawn_blocking` and swaps it in behind `RwLock<Option<Arc<Reader>>>`. A lookup clones the `Arc` and releases the lock, and lookups never do IO. If the new file can't be read, the VTC keeps the database it already has and logs one warning, not one a minute.

Checked against the real `dbip-city-lite-2026-10.mmdb` locally. Results: `8.8.8.8` gives "Mountain View, US", `1.1.1.1` gives "Sydney, AU", and an IPv6 Google address gives "Frankfurt am Main, DE".

## Config

```toml
[geoip]
database = "/var/lib/vtc/geoip/dbip-city-lite.mmdb"
```

- Env override: `VTC_GEOIP_DATABASE`. An empty value turns it off.
- Backwards compatible. When the key is absent behaviour is unchanged, and an unset value is not serialised back on `save`.
- A configured file that is missing or invalid logs a **warning at startup and the VTC starts anyway**, with every location `"unknown"`. This is a deliberate exception to the repo's fail-closed config validation: location is advisory and sign-in works without it. A database replaced later is still picked up without a restart.

## Privacy

- An IP address is never logged or stored by this code. Warnings name the database path and the error only, and a test asserts that no address appears in the logs.
- Only the coarse result goes into the request record and the `MemberWalletSignIn` / `AdminWalletSignIn` audit rows, as before.

## Licence notes

- Adds **`maxminddb` 0.32.0** (published 2026-09-12, not yanked) as a workspace dependency, with `default-features = false` so there is no `mmap` and no `unsafe`. **Its licence is ISC, not MIT/Apache-2.0** as the task brief assumed. ISC is already on `deny.toml`'s allow-list, and `cargo deny check` passes. Its transitive deps (`ipnetwork` 0.21, `memchr`, `serde`, `thiserror`) were already in the tree, so the lockfile adds only the one package.
- DB-IP Lite data is CC BY 4.0. The docs give the required attribution ("IP Geolocation by DB-IP", linking https://db-ip.com) and suggest places an operator could show it. No UI is added.
- No database or fixture file is vendored.

## Tests

`geoip::tests` (9 tests) builds its test databases with a minimal MMDB writer inside the test code. That covers the IPv6 tree with 24-bit records, the data section and the metadata, so no fixture file or writer dependency is needed. Cases covered:
- unset path gives `None`
- non-public ranges give `None`, using a database that answers for every IPv4 address
- a known address gives `"Vienna, AT"`, including its IPv4-mapped form
- a country-only record gives `"Sweden"`
- a replaced file is reloaded
- a bad replacement keeps the old database, with one warning
- a bad or missing file at startup gives `None` plus a warning, and the database is picked up once a good file appears
- addresses never appear in logs
- the 128-character cap and stripping of control characters

There is also a config parse test for `[geoip] database`.

Local runs:
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: passes
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passes
- `cargo deny check`: passes
- `cargo nextest run -p vtc-service`: passes. The 12 admin-UI embed tests that fail under `VTC_SKIP_ADMIN_UI_BUILD=1` were re-run with the UI built, and all 22 selected tests passed.
- `vta-sdk/tests/secret_debug_census.rs`: not relevant, since no secret-bearing types were added.

## Docs

New `docs/03-vtc/geoip.md` covers:
- what is shown
- DB-IP City Lite download (`dbip-city-lite-YYYY-MM.mmdb.gz`, then gunzip)
- `[geoip] database` and `VTC_GEOIP_DATABASE`
- a monthly cron job that does an atomic `mv`
- the CC BY 4.0 attribution and where it could be shown
- the MaxMind GeoLite2 alternative

It is linked from `docs/README.md` and from the member-portal section of `website-and-admin.md`.

Diff kept to the GeoIP concern. In `oob.rs` it only removes the stub after `same_network`, separated from #2024's hunk by unchanged lines.

title: fix(auth)!: bound wallet sign-in sessions by the grant's notAfter across refresh
body:
## Summary

A wallet sign-in's grant `notAfter` now bounds the whole session, not just its first window, for both the member portal and the operator console. Refresh rotation stays inside it, and once it has passed, refresh is refused and the user signs in again.

## Cause

- **Member portal** (`trust_tasks::oob_tasks::mint_session`): the first access and refresh expiries were clamped to the grant's `notAfter`, and a comment said "refreshing cannot extend it". It could. `vti_common::auth::handlers::handle_refresh` set the new expiries to now + the full TTL on every rotation, and kept nothing that recorded the grant's end. A session approved for one hour could be renewed for as long as the member stayed active.
- **Console** (`routes::auth::mint_admin_cookie_session`, used by wallet sign-in since #2014): `notAfter` was ignored completely. The redeem reported the 24h refresh deadline as `notAfter`.
- Both cookie-refresh routes set the refresh and CSRF cookie `Max-Age` from the configured TTL, not from the token's actual remaining life.

## Fix

- `Session` gains `not_after: Option<u64>`, an absolute end. There are helpers `clamp_to_end` and `past_end`.
- `handle_refresh`:
  - refuses a refresh once `now >= not_after` (`RefreshTokenExpired`);
  - clamps the rotated refresh expiry, and the access-token TTL (so the JWT `exp` too), to the end;
  - carries the end forward to the rotated session;
  - reports `refreshExpiresIn` as the time actually left.
- The lost-response retry path (`replay_rotation`) follows the same rules.
- New `mint_session_tokens_until(.., not_after)` mints both tokens to end by a given instant. `mint_session_tokens` delegates to it with `None` and behaves as before.
- Wallet sign-in stores the grant's `notAfter` as the session's end on both audiences. `mint_admin_cookie_session` takes a `not_after` (`None` for passkey). Redeem's `notAfter` is now the session's true end.
- `/v1/member/auth/refresh` and the console's cookie `/v1/auth/refresh` size their cookies from `refresh_expires_in`.
- The doc comment and `docs/03-vtc/website-and-admin.md` now state the guarantee.

## Compatibility

- `not_after` is `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]`:
  - a stored session written before this change loads as unbounded and keeps sliding exactly as before;
  - unbounded rows serialise byte-identically.
- Passkey and SIOPv2 sessions are unchanged. I looked for an existing absolute session-lifetime setting to combine with, and there isn't one: `AuthConfig` has only the access/refresh TTLs, the idle timeout and the reuse grace.
- **Breaking for `vti-common`** (hence `!`): `Session` is a public struct and now has a new field. Every in-workspace struct literal is updated.
- No new dependencies. No version edits.

## Tests

- `vti-common` unit tests:
  - `session.rs`: an old row without the field loads as unbounded and re-serialises without it; clamping and end semantics.
  - `refresh.rs`: rotations never pass the end, and the end is carried forward; a refresh at or past the end is refused without raising a reuse alert; a grace-window retry cannot outlive the end; an unbounded session still slides by the full TTL.
- `vtc-service/tests/it/member_portal_oob.rs` (end-to-end through `/v1/trust-tasks` and the cookie refresh routes):
  - `a_member_session_is_bounded_by_the_grants_not_after_across_refreshes`: redeem `notAfter` equals the stored end, and three successive refreshes keep the stored deadline, `expiresAt` and every cookie inside it.
  - `a_member_refresh_near_the_end_is_clamped_to_it`: the access cookie, refresh cookie and JWT `exp` are all at or before `notAfter`.
  - `a_member_refresh_after_the_end_is_refused`: returns 401 and sets no session cookie.
  - `a_console_session_is_bounded_by_the_grants_not_after` and `a_console_refresh_near_the_end_is_clamped_to_it`: the same checks for the console audience, including refusal past the end.
  - `a_session_stored_before_not_after_existed_still_refreshes`: a raw pre-change row refreshes and slides by the full TTL.
  - The suite has no clock injection. Like the existing `age` helper, "after the end" is simulated by ageing the stored record.

  - `cargo fmt --all -- --check`

title: fix(auth)!: bound wallet sign-in sessions by the grant's notAfter across refresh (#2026)
body:
fix(auth)!: bound wallet sign-in sessions by the grant's notAfter across refresh (#2026)

A wallet sign-in (`auth/oob/*`) grant carries `notAfter`, the latest
moment the member approved the session for, and redeem reports it. The
member-portal mint clamped only the first window to it — the comment
"refreshing cannot extend it" was false: `handle_refresh` reset both
expiries to now + the full TTL on every rotation, so a session approved
for an hour could be renewed indefinitely. The console session minted by
wallet sign-in (`mint_admin_cookie_session`, #2014) ignored `notAfter`
entirely, and reported the refresh deadline as `notAfter`.

`vti_common::auth::session::Session` gains `not_after: Option<u64>`, an
absolute end. `handle_refresh` refuses a refresh once it is reached
(`RefreshTokenExpired`), clamps the rotated refresh expiry and the
access-token TTL (so the JWT `exp` too) to it, carries it forward, and
reports `refreshExpiresIn` as the time actually left. The lost-response
retry path is bounded the same way. New `mint_session_tokens_until`
mints both tokens to end by a given instant; `mint_session_tokens` is
unchanged.

The member and console wallet sign-ins store the grant's `notAfter` as
the session's end, so redeem's `notAfter` is the session's true end.
The member and console cookie refreshes size the refresh and CSRF
cookies from the rotated token's remaining life instead of the
configured TTL.

Compatibility: the field is `#[serde(default)]` and skipped when `None`,
so stored rows without it load as unbounded and keep sliding, and
unbounded rows serialise byte-identically. Passkey and SIOPv2 sessions
are unchanged; there is no existing absolute-lifetime setting to combine
with. Breaking for `vti-common`: `Session` is a public struct with a new
field.

title: fix(diagnostics): log every failed offscreen request; wait for the lens to load in its test
body:
## Why

While diagnosing a user whose requests to `gt-vta` time out over TSP, the offscreen console showed only `[pnm mediator] dropped session … — reply timeout`. It didn't say which request timed out, and it didn't include the TSP channel's `last inbound frame declined: …` reason. That reason is what tells "the reply never arrived" apart from "it arrived and the wallet refused it", and it only reached the caller, which drew it in a console banner.

## Change

- **Every failed offscreen reply is logged** (`request-failure-log.ts`). The listener wraps Chrome's `sendResponse` once, so all 33 handlers are covered, including any added later. Each line has the handler, agent, task type, elapsed time, error, code and details:
  ```
  [pnm request] offscreen/request-task failed after 30.0s { error, vtaDid, task, code, details }
  ```
  The request payload is never logged, only the task type.
- **The Mediator Lens render test no longer races.** It used to wait a fixed two rounds before asserting, which wasn't always enough on Node 26 in CI ("Reading where this DID's mail goes…", seen on #309). It now keeps waiting while anything is still loading, up to 50 rounds.

## Tests

`tests/request-failure-log.test.mts` covers:
- the fields that are logged;
- that the payload is never logged;
- that details are kept;
- that only failures are logged;
- that malformed input still logs;
- that Chrome's callback is called only inside the wrapper.

Extension 993 pass; build clean.

## Pre-merge checklist

- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2): none
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3)
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1): none
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4): none
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5): unchanged
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6): unchanged
- [x] New/changed wire types (R3.*): none
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive (R5.*): n/a
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified; background-job failures are surfaced (R6.*): this is that
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1): no mutations
- [x] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers: none

title: feat(transport): fall back to REST when an agent stops replying through its mediator, and say so
body:
## Problem

A user's wallet connected to `fpdev-mediator` without trouble (`101`, handshake done), and every request to `gt-vta` waited 30 s and failed. The VTA logs show it received the TSP requests and replied, but no reply reached the wallet. The agent's REST endpoint was healthy the whole time. `buildVtaSession` skips a mediator channel only when it cannot *connect*. This one connected fine, so TSP stayed first and the console could not load.

## Change

- **Fallback (`mediator-fallback.ts`).** A reply timeout on an (agent, relay) pair takes that pair's TSP and DIDComm channels out of the selection for 5 minutes, and only when REST is available. Without REST, skipping them would turn a slow failure into a certain one. After the cooldown the mediator is tried again. The request that timed out still fails, because it may have been applied (R1.4). Only later requests use REST.
- **Health.** The skipped channels are recorded `down` with a new code, `mediator/no-reply`, so `activeTransport` and the Transports pane say "REST".
- **Alert.**
  - A browser notification, at most one per agent per 30 minutes.
  - A polling banner in the console.
  - Both say approval requests from that agent may not be arriving, since they travel through the same mediator (R7.2).
- **Notifications go through the background (`RUNTIME_NOTIFY`).** An offscreen document gets only `chrome.runtime`, so `chrome.notifications` is undefined there. The existing "Approval was not accepted" notice called it from the offscreen document and so never appeared. Both notices now go through the background, which accepts the message only from extension pages (`isExtensionPageSender`). A test fails if `offscreen.ts` calls `chrome.notifications` again.

## Tests

`tests/mediator-fallback.test.mts` covers:
- the cooldown and recovery;
- keying on the pair;
- extending the cooldown on a repeat timeout;
- the notification limit;
- the agent label;
- `sittingOutTransports` matching on the code;
- the offscreen guard.

Extension 987 pass, core 867 pass; lint and build are clean.

## Pre-merge checklist

- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2): no new clients
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3)
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1): the fallback state is an in-memory cache; losing it costs one more timeout
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4): the timed-out request is not resent
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5): inbox sessions are untouched
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6): inbound path unchanged
- [x] New/changed wire types (R3.*): none; the new diagnosis code is matched on the code, not the text (R3.7)
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive (R5.*): n/a
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified (R6.*): "no reply" is what was observed; the text does not guess at a cause
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1)
- [x] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers: none

title: feat(admin-ui): console redesign phase 3 — dashboard, Actions, Members, ACL, ⌘K palette and theme switcher
body:
## Summary

Phase 3 of the operator-console redesign (after #2012, #2013, #2014, #2022): the screen-level work — the dashboard as "what needs me" plus health, the Actions inbox, Members and Access control — and the ⌘K command palette, following the approved proposal's mockups. Also a Match system / Light / Dark theme switcher on the console, the member portal and the community home page, and a `Switch` component for on/off settings. No new dependencies, no API changes, routes unchanged.

Seven commits, each focused: Switch → theme switcher → palette → dashboard → Actions → Members + ACL → docs.

## What changed, per screen

**Dashboard (Overview)**
- A greeting under an Overview breadcrumb, with **Invite a member** as the primary action for a viewer holding `vtc.invitations.manage`.
- Tiles for Members, Join requests, Awaiting a vetting decision, **Waiting for you** (new) and Withdrawn statements, plus single-admin mode when on. Each links to its screen and stays capability-gated as before. A tile needing attention gets a warning rail, so the state doesn't depend on the colour of small text.
- **Waiting for you**: the first five actions from the Actions screen's signed read, each linking to `?action=`. A summary only shows once it has been re-derived and verified (`lib/action-summary.ts`). A refused summary says so and the VTC's text never appears.
- **Service health**: daemon, VTA, mediator, trust registry, this browser's signing key (read from the shell's cached status, not fetched again), build and hidden-vetting support. One row each, with a dot plus a word for screen readers.
- Transport advertisement and Identity stay below as the detail.

**Actions**
- Each card is an inbox row:
  - A chip row first: Critical, Landed now, Consent waived, Cooling off, Queue, and **Summary verified**.
  - Then the verified summary, then one meta line: requester · relative time (full time on hover) · match code.
  - Then the facts.
- Approve/Decline, Acknowledge, Cancel and Land now sit in a right-hand column. On a narrow screen they move under the facts.
- No card content was removed. Tabs, `?action=` detail and every decision path are unchanged.

**Members**
- Page header with count and Add a member, a toolbar on the page (search, role, and a new **Personhood** filter), and the table in an edge-to-edge card.
- One **Member** column shows the name over the DID (abbreviated, with the full DID on hover, copy and QR as before), sortable by name. Personhood shows as a Verified / Not yet chip.
- Accepts `?q=` and `?add=1` (used by the palette). Each is applied once, then dropped from the URL.

**Access control**
- **Add entry** moves into the page header, with the entry count beside the title. A client-side search (DID, label, role) sits next to the role filter.
- One **Entry** column shows the label (still edited in place, and now with an accessible name) over the DID and the "you" chip.
- The session-timeout setting moves below the list and the invites.
- Accepts `?add=1` and `?invite=1`.

**Command palette (⌘K / Ctrl+K, or "Jump to…" in the top bar)**
- **Screens:** every screen the viewer can see. Plugins come from the `registerPlugin` registry, so third-party plugins and plugins without a `group` are listed too, under their nav heading.
- **Actions:**
  - review waiting actions
  - add or invite a member
  - decide join requests
  - add an ACL entry
  - invite an administrator
  - renew the signing key
  - theme light / dark / system
  - reload plugins
  - sign out

  Each action is offered only when the screen it needs is visible.
- A query is also offered as a member search, and a DID opens that member.
- Built from scratch:
  - A labelled modal dialog. The page behind it is `inert` and focus is trapped on the input.
  - The input is an ARIA combobox controlling a grouped listbox, with `aria-activedescendant`.
  - Keys: Up/Down, Home/End, Enter. Escape or a click outside closes it and returns focus to where it was.
  - A live region announces the result count.
- Ranking lives in `lib/commands.ts` (pure, unit-tested).

**Theme switcher**
- An ARIA radio group (roving tabindex, arrow keys).
- Console: stays in the account menu. Member portal and console sign-in page: added to the shared top bar.
- Home page: a static twin, `website-default/theme.js`. It loads undeferred in `<head>`, so a pinned theme is applied before first paint under `default-src 'self'`, and it stays hidden without JS.
- All three use the existing `vtc-admin-theme` key, so one choice applies everywhere and an earlier choice carries over. Tabs stay in sync via `storage` events. "Match system" stores nothing and follows `prefers-color-scheme`.

**Switch**
- A native checkbox with `role="switch"` under a drawn track. The off track meets 3:1 in both themes.
- Used for on/off settings: automatic vetter naming, the five criterion-editor switches, join discovery, "Show system events" and ACL "May approve others' actions".
- Multi-select lists and consent ticks stay checkboxes.

## Deviations from the proposal

- The dashboard mockup's **Administrators** tile ("3 · 2 approvals needed") is replaced by **Waiting for you**: no read the dashboard already makes gives an administrator count. The **Withdrawn statements** tile is kept.
- The Members mockup's **Last seen** column and **Active ▾** status filter are not included. The member listing has no last-seen data (adding it would be an API change), and it holds only current members (departed ones are in *Removed members*). A **Personhood** filter is added instead.
- The proposal's palette also "jumps to any member or DID". Here it offers a member search for any query and opens a DID typed in full. It does not search members inline, which would need a members read the viewer may not be allowed to make.
- "Split `styles.css` per plugin" (also listed under P3) was already done in #2013. The palette and list-screen styles went into `shell.css` / `components.css`, and screen-specific ones into `styles/plugins/*`.
- The proposal says nothing about toggle switches. The Switch is used where a control is a single on/off setting (listed above).

## Compatibility

- Routes under `/admin` are unchanged. New query strings are optional and applied once.
- Plugin API unchanged: no new manifest fields, and every registered plugin shows up in the palette with no field of its own.
- No API or wire changes. `wire:check` is clean.
- The stored theme key (`vtc-admin-theme`) and the collapsed-sidebar setting carry over.
- One Rust change: a test in `website/default_site.rs` pinning that `theme.js` is embedded, loaded in `<head>`, and shares the console's key.

## Test plan

- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit -p .`
- [x] `npx vitest run`: 85 files, 984 tests. New:
  - `Switch.test.tsx`
  - `ThemeSwitcher.test.tsx`
  - `CommandPalette.test.tsx`
  - `AppCommandPalette.test.tsx`
  - `lib/commands.test.ts`
  - `formatRelative`
  - dashboard / Actions / Members / ACL layout tests
  - portal theme test
- [x] `npm run wire:check`, `npm run build`, `npm run build:members`
- [x] `cargo build -p vtc-service` (embedded UI), `cargo test -p vtc-service --lib website::default_site`, `cargo fmt --check`
- [ ] Manual look in both themes at desktop and phone widths (no screenshots attached: producing them needs a signed-in console against a running VTC)

Existing tests changed only where markup legitimately changed:
- the theme buttons are now `radio`
- Members' first column is Member (name over DID)
- the dashboard's hidden-vetting tile is now a health row, and its read check ignores the shared name-book read
- the ACL label input now has an accessible name
- the ACL approve toggle is a switch
- `list-limits` lists the dashboard's `limit: 5` read

Docs: `docs/03-vtc/website-and-admin.md` (theme, dashboard, palette, portal) and a line in `admin-ui-plugins.md`. The full design-language pass is phase 4.

title: fix(mediator): retire a replaced warm session instead of closing it under in-flight requests
body:
## Problem

A user's console showed `contexts/list/1.0 failed: mediator-transport: not connected`, alongside an `Uncaught (in promise) Error: mediator-transport: WebSocket closed` in `offscreen.html`. The self-test passed, reloading did not help, and their clock is not skewed.

Two defects on our side turn a dropped mediator socket into those errors:

1. **`getWarmSession` closed a connection other requests were still using.** When a cached connection failed `isReusable`, it was `close()`d immediately. A concurrent request already holding it then sent into `ws === null` → `not connected`.
2. **An orphaned reply waiter.** `MediatorSessionBridge.sendAndAwaitReply` registers the waiter, then sends. If the send threw, the waiter was never awaited, and its later rejection (timeout or socket close) surfaced as an uncaught promise.

## Fix

- `retireConnection` (`warm-session-health.ts`): a socket that is no longer open is closed at once, since nothing on it can succeed. An open one is closed after `RETIRE_GRACE_MS` (35 s, longer than the 30 s reply wait). The replacement re-attaches the inbox handlers. A message delivered on both sockets during the grace is the same message id: `putPendingInbound` is idempotent by id, and dedup prevents a second prompt.
- The bridge observes the waiter when the send throws. The same change in vti-didcomm-js: OpenVTC/vti-didcomm-js#29.

These do not explain *why* the user's socket drops; that still needs their WebSocket close code. They stop a drop from breaking concurrent requests and from producing an uncaught rejection.

## Tests

- `core/tests/vta.bridge-peer.mjs`: no `unhandledRejection` when the send throws.
- `extension/tests/warm-session-health.test.mts`: an open connection is closed only after the grace, a closed one at once, and the grace outlasts the reply wait.
- core 867 pass / 2 skipped; extension 979 pass.

## Pre-merge checklist

- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2): no new clients
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3)
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1)
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4): no retry added
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5): a deliberate close still does not fire `onClose`; the replacement session carries the inbox
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6): inbound path unchanged
- [x] New/changed wire types (R3.*): none
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive (R5.*): n/a
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified (R6.*)
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1): a pending retire timer dies with the document, which closes the socket anyway
- [x] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers: none

title: fix(mediator): retire a replaced warm session instead of closing it under in-flight requests (#308)
body:
fix(mediator): retire a replaced warm session instead of closing it under in-flight requests (#308)

getWarmSession closed a cached connection the moment isReusable said no,
while a concurrent request could still be sending on it or awaiting its
reply. That request failed with "mediator-transport: not connected" — a
user's console could not list contexts. An open connection is now closed
after a 35 s grace (longer than the 30 s reply wait); a closed one at once.

MediatorSessionBridge also observes its reply waiter when the send throws,
so the waiter's later rejection is not an uncaught promise in the offscreen
document. The same fix lands in vti-didcomm-js (OpenVTC/vti-didcomm-js#29).

title: fix(vtc): sign wallet sign-in respond and cancel replies; mixed-family networks are unknown
body:
## Problem
A wallet sign-in completes. The member portal and the operator console both log in. But the browser plugin's window ends with **Sign-in stopped** and `auth/oob/reply-invalid` at the respond step, refused by the wallet itself.

The plugin's `sendOob` requires every reply from the community to be signed for `assertionMethod` by a key in the community's verified DID document. The VTC signed only the step 1 (claim) and step 2 (prove) replies. `respond` and `cancel` went out through the unsigned `success_response`.

Separately, the plugin warned "This request did not come from the network this browser is on" for a sign-in started and approved on the same machine. `same_network` compared an IPv4 address with an IPv6 /64 as unequal. A dual-stack machine can reach the VTC over different families from the page and from the extension.

## Fix
- **`respond` and `cancel` replies** are signed with `attested()`, the same as steps 1 and 2. The payloads are unchanged.
- **`same_network`** returns `"unknown"` when the two addresses are of different families. The wallet shows a softer note for that.

## Compatibility
- Additive: a client that ignores `proof` sees the same documents.
- The starter's `redeem` is unchanged.

## Tests
- `member_portal_oob` asserts that the respond and cancel replies verify as the VTC's attestation.
- The unit test covers both mixed-family directions.
- `cargo clippy -p vtc-service --all-targets -D warnings`; `cargo nextest` on the oob, wallet and `same_network` tests: all pass.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: refactor(vtc)!: drop vtc-client's unused bearer token and the uncalled persona REST route
body:
Every verb `vtc-client` sends is a signed Trust Task, and the last bearer
routes it called are gone, but the client still stored the access token
`connect` obtained and its docs still described verbs "on bearer REST until
they have a Trust Task".

- `VtcClient` no longer holds a token. `connect` still runs the
  challenge-response login: it is the up-front access check, so a DID the VTC
  does not know is refused where `cnm` can print the fix rather than on the
  first verb. Its token was read by nothing but `Debug`, which now reports
  whose signing key is held.
- Docs: the vetting-admin "stays on bearer REST" note,
  `VtcError::NoRestTransport` (now: no REST base and no session to carry a
  Trust Task), `with_key`, and the `self.token` mentions in `git_ns` and
  `rooms`.
- vtc-service: the surface-task and join-discovery comments no longer say
  those verbs keep a REST route; the persona route's exception rows say what
  is true — `vtc/relationships/persona/0.1` has no upstream specification,
  which is why the spine cannot dispatch it.
- cnm: the withdrawal hint pointed at `GET /v1/join-requests/<id>/vetting`,
  which is not mounted; it now points at the join request in the console.
- admin-ui: a comment named `POST /v1/schemas/accepts` for what is
  `vtc/schemas/accepts/register`.

## Persona annotation route removed

`POST` / `DELETE /v1/relationships/{id}/persona` (#1074, issue #1067) attached
a member's self-issued persona credential (VPC) to one of their relationship
edges. It was the one VTC verb still bearer REST with no Trust Task, and:

- no caller — nothing in this repository, `openvtc` or the browser plugin
  mints a VPC or calls the route;
- no specification — `vtc/relationships/persona/0.1` was never published in
  dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf, though the REST exception rows said it was;
- no settled binding — how a VPC binds to an edge is
  trustoverip/dtgwg-cred-spec#9, still open; the route's request-level binding
  was a stand-in.

Specifying it now would standardise a binding the credentials group has not
agreed, for a feature nobody uses. So the route, its two handlers, the VPC
shape check and the authorization-envelope helpers only it used are gone,
with its integration tests. Stored edges keep their optional `persona` field,
so existing rows decode and the console still groups edges by persona.
`docs/05-design-notes/vpc-persona-annotation.md` is marked parked and says
how to revive it: settle #9, a client that mints VPCs, a spec upstream, then
serve it on the spine. `admin-ui/openapi.json` and `wire.ts` are regenerated.

title: feat(rooms)!: room files on the host — blob store, uploads, downloads and limits (#2018)
body:
feat(rooms)!: room files on the host — blob store, uploads, downloads and limits (#2018)

* feat(common): a BlobStore for room files, with local-directory, S3 and GCS backends

Room files are a record plus a blob; the blob is the file's ciphertext, held outside the room's keyspaces. vti_common::blob_store is node-neutral, beside backup_transfer, so a standalone room host and a community share one store and one conformance suite (data-rooms-files.md §5.3).

- BlobStore: put (idempotent on the key), get_range, delete (Deleted | Lapses | Unsupported), health.
- LocalDirStore: plain files, written via a synced temp file and renamed, owner-only. Always compiled.
- ObjectStoreBlobs over object_store 0.14: S3-compatible (feature blob-s3) and GCS (feature blob-gcs), credentials from the environment for now. object_store passes cargo deny (advisories, bans, licences, sources).
- Keys are rooms/<first 32 hex of SHA-256(roomId)>/<blobRef>: the store never learns a room's identifier, and the per-room prefix is what a downscoped credential will name.
- blob_ref_of_manifest: the BlobRef is the sha2-256 DigestMultibase of the manifest's JCS form, computed by the host.
- conformance::run, which every backend's own test calls.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(common): LocalDirStore can be built without awaiting, and creates its root on first use

A host that opens its state synchronously (room-host's open_state) can now construct the store; the root directory, like every level below it, is created owner-only on the first put or health probe.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(rooms)!: a verified chain names the member its authority descends from

VerifiedChain gains `member`: the subject of the chain's root, the party the room granted to, on the tiers that disclose it (None on private). AuthorizedAction::member() exposes it.

The leaf's subject is who may act, often an agent a member attenuated a chain to. A host charging storage to a member needs the member, or a member could multiply an allowance by minting agents (rooms/blobs/upload/begin: usage is charged to the subject at the root of the presented chain). The DTG verifier already compared the membership credential against the root's subject; it now returns it.

Breaking: a new public field on VerifiedChain, which implementations of ChainVerifier construct.
Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(rooms): room files on the host side — blob index, uploads, downloads, limits, usage and collection

vti_rooms::blobs::BlobHost holds everything a host stores about a room file's ciphertext, shared by room-host and (next) vtc-service as storage and authz already are:

- uploads staged through vti_common::backup_transfer's chunked slots; resume is begin with the same opener, room and manifest;
- the manifest checked for what its schema cannot state, and named by the host-computed BlobRef;
- limits at member, room, storage and host scope, checked and reserved atomically under one lock, refused naming the narrowest scope with its numbers; no member limits on private rooms; usage charged to the chain's member;
- commit stores durably in the BlobStore before recording, converts the reservation, is idempotent, and never stores or charges a blob already committed in the room;
- downloads bound to their opener, each chunk checked against its committed digest before it is served;
- per-record blob references: a write that drops a blob or a retraction releases it, the last release orphans it and credits the room and member at once, and re-referencing an uncollected orphan restores it;
- a collection pass deleting orphans and never-referenced commits past the grace window, and giving back reservations of expired uploads.

Known limit: the store has no multi-key transactions, so a crash between two writes of one step can leave a counter off by one blob.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(room-host): serve room files — rooms/blobs/*, rooms/records/put 0.2 and rooms/info

room-host now stores files in data rooms, over the same dispatch, on every carrier:

- rooms/blobs/upload/{begin,chunk,commit,abort}, rooms/blobs/{get,chunk}, rooms/records/put/0.2 and rooms/info/0.1, each parsed with its generated payload type and answered through its generated response type, refusing with the codes each specification declares;
- room-chain authorization as for records; the transfer tasks are authorized by owning the transfer, notFound to anybody else;
- a 0.1 put and a retraction release the blobs a record named;
- one storage config: a local directory (--blob-dir, default <data-dir>/blobs), limits from the command line (--room-max-*, --member-max-*, --max-file-bytes, --storage-capacity-bytes, --files-disabled), and a collection task (--orphan-grace-hours, --blob-sweep-interval-secs).

Tests cover the whole life of a file (interrupted upload resumed, committed, downloaded byte-identical, named, retracted, collected), rewrites that release and restore a file, deduplication, refusals at member, room, storage and host scope, two racing reservations, transfers answering only their opener, chunk and whole-digest mismatches, abort, a blob from another room, and an abandoned commit.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(common)!: chunked import slots on explicit terms — idle window and lifetime

TransferTerms names how long an import slot lives idle and in all. initiate_import_with takes them; initiate_import_for keeps TransferTerms::backup() (five minutes idle, an hour in all), so backup and website uploads are unchanged. TransferTerms::room_file() is fifteen minutes idle and a day in all, the floors rooms/blobs/upload/begin sets so a 1 GiB file over a slow link can finish.

Breaking: ChunkPlan gains the public field idle_ttl_secs (absent, and so the default, on every backup and website plan).
Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(rooms): align room files with the revised specs — alreadyCommitted, tooManyUploads, revived orphans checked, day-long slots

Follows trust-tasks-tf #739 as revised:
- begin on a BlobRef already committed in this room answers with an uploadId, missing [] and alreadyCommitted, reserving nothing; its commit returns the existing blob and charges nothing. Another room's copy is never reported.
- the per-opener cap on open uploads is BlobError::TooManyUploads { max_open }, retryable.
- upload slots use TransferTerms::room_file(): never expiring sooner than 15 minutes after the last accepted chunk, extending to a day in all. Download handles take the same floors.
- maxFileBytes refusals name the scope the smallest applicable limit was set at, the narrower on a tie; counts and totals the narrowest scope exceeded.
- record writes go through prepare_record / RecordBlobs::apply, which hold the lock across the write. Re-referencing an uncollected orphan charges it again, to the writer's member, and refuses with LimitExceeded when the member's or room's counts and totals would not hold it. record_blobs serves the 0.2 reads; release_record serves retraction.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(room-host): serve records get/list 0.2 with blobs, refuse with permissionDenied, and bound documents by type

- rooms/records/get/0.2 and list/0.2 echo the blobs each record names (absent when none, after a retraction, and on 0.1 writes), answered through their generated response types.
- room-chain refusals in the room-file tasks are the standard permissionDenied; the task-specific notAuthorized codes are gone from the specifications.
- begin answers alreadyCommitted and tooManyUploads (details.maxOpen); records/put 0.2 answers limitExceeded when reviving an orphan would not fit.
- every carrier's dispatch refuses a document larger than its specification's maxDocumentBytes with malformedRequest; tasks that declare no bound keep the transport limit, so the chunk documents are admitted at their bound and nothing else is.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(room-host): records get/list 0.2 read a record and its blobs atomically

A 0.2 read now takes BlobHost::read_snapshot, the lock every record write holds across the record write and its blob references, before reading the record (or the page) and the blobs it names. A concurrent put therefore cannot pair one version's record with another's blobs. A curation now holds the lock across the write too (prepare_release replaces release_record), so a read never sees a retracted record that still names the blobs the retraction released.

Test: writes flip a record between two files while get and list 0.2 run beside them on a multi-threaded runtime; every read pairs a title with the blob from the same write.
Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

title: trust-tasks-rs-v0.28.0
body:
### Added

- **rs**: Declared error codes carry their detailsSchema, and a titled variant no longer generates doctests ([#742](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/742))

Two trust-tasks-codegen defects found while implementing rooms/keys/file-key
  and external/* against the generated types.

  DeclaredErrorCode gains `details_schema: Option<&'static str>`: the JSON
  Schema a specification declares for an error's `details` (SPEC §7.3 item 9),
  or None. A `$ref` into a shared schema file is resolved and carried inline,
  with the same resolver PAYLOAD_SCHEMA uses, so the text compiles with no base
  URI. With the `validate` feature, `DeclaredErrorCode::check_details` checks a
  `details` value against it. An emitter previously had to hand-copy the schema
  to test what it sends, and the copy drifted silently when the specification
  changed. The struct is #[non_exhaustive], so adding the field is not breaking.

  check-bindings now compares each code's details_schema with the front matter
  (shared-file refs inlined, as the registry publishes them), refuses Some where
  none is declared and None where one is, and compiles every one with ajv: all
  195 agree.

  The doc fix: typify documents an enum variant as "{title}\n\n{description}",
  so a titled inline oneOf branch got a two-paragraph doc that no schema
  contained. Printed as /**…*/ with its first line flush against the opener,
  rustdoc read the second paragraph as an indented code block and compiled it as
  a doctest; titling the AccountSettings branches of external/_shared broke 77.
  The description-only pre-pass could not see text typify assembles itself, so
  it is replaced by a pass over every #[doc] attribute typify emits, which starts
  a multi-paragraph doc on its own line. Verified by titling those branches: 77
  failures before, none after. The regenerated tree differs only in the doc-
  embedded schemas, which no longer carry the stray leading "\n" the old pass
  wrote into `description`.



### Specifications

- **rooms**: An unauthorized room request is refused with the standard permissionDenied ([#743](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/743))

Thirteen rooms specifications (create, epoch/{commits,mint,prune},
  keys/open, keys/present 0.1 and 0.2, owner/{claim,transfer},
  records/{curate,get,list,put} 0.1) declared a task-specific
  `<slug>:notAuthorized` for a failure the framework already names: an
  authorization refusal is the standard `permissionDenied` (SPEC §7.2, §8.3).
  The extended code shadowed it, so a consumer switching on
  `permissionDenied` never matched it, and a party that did not recognise it
  degraded it to `taskFailed` (§8.5), a worse signal than the code it
  duplicated. The later rooms specifications (records/put 0.2 onward) already
  use the standard code, as the reference room host does for every version.

  Each withdrawn declaration's condition is kept as one sentence at the end of
  the specification's Conformance section, naming `permissionDenied`. Same
  correction as `vta/app-state:permissionDenied` in 0.11.3.

  Breaking for trust-tasks-rs: the thirteen `error_codes::NOT_AUTHORIZED`
  constants are removed from the generated rooms modules. A consumer emitting
  one should emit `StandardCode::PermissionDenied` instead.

title: feat(rooms): room files — file keys, STREAM sealing and rooms/keys/file-key
body:
First of two stacked PRs for room files (`docs/05-design-notes/data-rooms-files.md`), against the `rooms/*` file specifications (dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#739, trust-tasks-rs 0.27.8 via #2011). This PR covers the client-side cryptography and the VTA's key task. The host side is in the stacked PR.

### What's here
- **`vti-rooms::files`:**
  - the per-file key: `HKDF-SHA256(storage_key(E), salt = fileId, info = "openvtc/room/file/v1" || roomId || u64be(E))`;
  - STREAM ChaCha20-Poly1305 sealing, with nonce `u32be(0) || u64be(i)` and the final flag bound in the AAD;
  - Padmé padding;
  - `BlobManifest` / `FileManifest`, with `BlobRef` as the digest of the JCS-canonical manifest.
- **Reader checks:** a reader checks the blob against the file manifest and requires a verified final segment.
- **`vti-rooms-wasm`:** the same seal and open for the browser.
- **VTA `rooms/keys/file-key`:** returns one file's key to the member's own client.
  - It answers `noGroup` for a room the VTA holds no group for.
  - It answers `unknownEpoch` with `heldEpoch` for an epoch it doesn't hold.
- **`pnm rooms file seal` / `open`.**

### Checks
The same checks were run on the stacked branch, which includes these commits:
- **Workspace nextest:** 5569 tests. The only non-pass was the backup keyspace round trip timing out under contention; it passed in 30 s on its own.
- **vtc nextest:** 2929 passed.
- **Doctests, clippy (`-D warnings`) and fmt:** clean.

feat(rooms): room files — file keys, STREAM sealing and rooms/keys/file-key (#2017)

* feat(rooms): file keys, STREAM sealing and blob manifests in vti-rooms

Adds vti_rooms::files, the construction rooms/_shared/0.1/blobs.schema.json FileManifest specifies (trust-tasks-tf #739): a per-file key, HKDF-SHA256 over the epoch storage key salted with the fileId and bound to the room and epoch; ChaCha20-Poly1305 STREAM segments whose nonce counts and whose associated data carries the final flag, so truncation, reordering and splicing fail to authenticate; one sealed segment per transfer chunk; the blob manifest and its BlobRef (sha2-256 over JCS); Padmé padding; and streaming sealer and opener that refuse a file whose plaintext digest is not the one its author signed. The manifest and digests build without the mls feature so a host can check them; the keyed half is behind mls with the rest of the member half. SealedRoom gains file_key_for_seal and file_key_for_open, walking the epoch chain as open_record does. Test vectors in vti-rooms/tests/fixtures/file-vectors.json.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(rooms): seal and open room files in the browser (vti-rooms-wasm)

FileSealer and FileOpener stream a file through vti_rooms::files a piece at a time. From a RoomMember the file key is derived inside the module and never crosses into JavaScript; FileSealer.withKey / FileOpener.withKey take a key released by the member's VTA (rooms/keys/file-key/0.1) and are for the wallet extension's own context only, never a web page (data-rooms-files.md §4.1). An opener's output is not a received file until finish() has checked the author's digest.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(vta): rooms/keys/file-key — one file's key for the member's own client

Serves rooms/keys/file-key/0.1 (trust-tasks-tf #739). The one rooms/keys task that releases a key: a file can be a gigabyte and its bytes must not pass through the VTA, so the member's client gets that file's key and encrypts or decrypts itself. What crosses opens one file — it is derived per file from the epoch storage key, which never leaves. Gated on roomOpen for both purposes, as seal and open are. Seal derives under the current epoch and refuses a caller-chosen one; open walks the epoch chain as rooms/keys/open does, and refuses an unreachable epoch with the declared unknownEpoch code saying notDelivered or beyondChain (with the earliest epoch). Audited with room, fileId, purpose and epoch, never the key. ReadOnly in vta_sdk::retry_safety, Sensitive in the vta-mcp guard, and VtaClient::room_file_key.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(pnm): rooms file seal and open, with one file's key from the VTA

pnm rooms file seal writes a file's sealed chunks, its blob manifest (what a host checks) and its file manifest (the sealed record body's file member), sealing under a key from rooms/keys/file-key; pnm rooms file open checks the chunks against the blob manifest, the blob manifest against the blobRef its author signed, and the plaintext against the author's digest, and writes nothing on a mismatch. Uploading is rooms/blobs/upload/* once hosts serve it. vti-rooms gains a files feature — the file key and STREAM sealing without OpenMLS, for a party handed one file's key — which mls implies.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(rooms): readers check the blob against the file manifest; a verified finish; heldEpoch

Aligns with the revised FileManifest reading rules and rooms/keys/file-key (trust-tasks-tf #739). FileManifest::check_blob runs before any byte is opened: the blob is the one the author's blobRef names, chunkSize is segmentSize + 16, chunkCount is max(1, ceil(paddedLength / segmentSize)), and the blob's size fits; StreamOpener and open_file now take the blob manifest so the check cannot be skipped. The wasm FileOpener takes the blob manifest the host served, and its finish reports { verified, size, digest } with a verified getter that stays false until the digest has checked, so the extension releases plaintext only then. An out-of-range manifest epoch is refused, never truncated. file-key's notDelivered refusal carries heldEpoch.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(vta): file-key answers noGroup for a room it holds no group for

rooms/keys/file-key/0.1 now declares rooms/keys/file-key:noGroup (trust-tasks-tf #739): the framework defines no standard not-found code, so the oracle that holds no group for the room refuses with the declared code rather than taskFailed with a reason. rooms/keys/open is unchanged. Handler-level tests check the noGroup and unknownEpoch refusals carry their declared codes, that unknownEpoch's details (notDelivered with heldEpoch, beyondChain with earliestEpoch) validate against the declared detailsSchema, that a held room releases a sealing key under its current epoch, and that epoch misuse and an out-of-range epoch are malformedRequest.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

body:
The Release PR for every package in this repo. **Merging this is the release.**

| Package | Registry | Version | Bump |
|---|---|---|---|
| `trust-tasks` | crates.io | `0.27.8` → `0.28.0` | breaking |
| `trust-tasks-capability-client` | crates.io | `0.27.8` → `0.28.0` | breaking |
| `trust-tasks-didcomm` | crates.io | `0.27.8` → `0.28.0` | breaking |
| `trust-tasks-didcomm-v1` | crates.io | `0.27.8` → `0.28.0` | breaking |
| `trust-tasks-https` | crates.io | `0.27.8` → `0.28.0` | breaking |
| `trust-tasks-proof` | crates.io | `0.27.8` → `0.28.0` | breaking |
| `trust-tasks-rs` | crates.io | `0.27.8` → `0.28.0` | breaking |
| `trust-tasks-tsp` | crates.io | `0.27.8` → `0.28.0` | breaking |
| `@openvtc/trust-tasks` | npm | `0.23.9` → `0.24.0` | breaking |
| `github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/trust-tasks-go` | Go (tag `trust-tasks-go/v0.6.0`) | `0.5.9` → `0.6.0` | breaking |
| `trust_tasks` | pub.dev | `0.5.9` → `0.6.0` | breaking |

What merging does, per registry (all in `publish.yml`, each keyed on "this
version is not published yet"):

- **crates.io** — `release-plz-release` tags `<crate>-v<version>`, publishes in
  dependency order and creates a GitHub Release per crate. Bump levels come from
  `cargo-semver-checks`.
- **npm** — `publish-npm` publishes with OIDC provenance and tags
  `<prefix>-v<version>`.
- **Go** — `publish-go` builds, vets and tests, then pushes the tag, which *is*
  the publication. **Irreversible**: proxy.golang.org never forgets a tag.
- **pub.dev** — `tag-dart` verifies against the *published* core and pushes the
  tag; `publish-dart.yml` publishes from it.

The npm, Go and Dart bumps are only as accurate as the commit subjects — nothing
checks their APIs the way `cargo-semver-checks` checks the crates. Look for a
missing `!` before merging.

This branch is regenerated from `main` on every push, so do not commit to it —
edits are force-pushed away. See RELEASING.md.

title: feat: P-256 and secp256k1 members — Trust Task proofs, rotation and OID4VCI key binding (#1988)
body:
#2010 accepted P-256 and secp256k1 for credentials others issue. A member
holding such a key — a secure-enclave or EUDI-wallet key, `did:key:zDn…` /
`did:key:zQ3s…` — still could not sign as one: the SDK signed Trust Tasks
Ed25519 only, and the VTC's hex holder signatures and OID4VCI key-binding
proof read every key as Ed25519. Every one of these now goes through
`vta_sdk::jws::JwsKey`, so the key decides the algorithm and nothing in the
request can choose one.

- Trust Task proofs: the shared verifier already accepted `ecdsa-jcs-2019`
  (P-256) once phase 1 taught the VM resolver P-256 keys; a test now holds
  it. `trust_task_sign` signs `ecdsa-jcs-2019` for a P-256 holder — a private
  multibase with the `p256-priv` prefix, or a bare one beside a
  `did:key:zDn…`. The Trust Tasks framework has every consumer SHOULD-verify
  that suite, for hardware-backed signers. There is no secp256k1 Data
  Integrity suite, so a secp256k1 key signs no Trust Task.
- `vtc/members/rotate`: the old and new signatures (hex, 64 bytes) may be
  EdDSA, ES256 or ES256K by the key that made them; ECDSA is `r || s` over
  the SHA-256 of the canonical bytes, as JWS encodes it. The `did:webvh` path
  resolves `#key-0` through `TrustTaskVmResolver` (bound to authentication,
  VTI-KEY-022, with the cached-document refresh, VTI-KEY-134) instead of
  reading Ed25519 bytes off the document. Join's REST holder binding shares
  the same verifier.
- OID4VCI key-binding proof: `EdDSA`, `ES256` or `ES256K`, whichever the
  `kid`'s key signs; a header naming another is refused before the
  signature. `DidVmResolver::resolve_verifying_key` (Ed25519) becomes
  `resolve_jws_key`.
- `vta_sdk::jws`: `JwsKey::from_did_key`, and `verify_signature` is public
  for signatures that are not a JWS.

What the workspace mints, and every key `sealed_transfer` seals to, stays
Ed25519 / X25519: the VTA's sealed credential delivery (`seal_issued_credential`)
still needs an Ed25519 `did:key` holder, and a sign-in `sessionKey` is still
Ed25519. Accepting more algorithms widens what VTI-KEY-013 (retirable
algorithms) would have to retire; that requirement is already an open
divergence in the specification's register.

Tests: a P-256 member rotates onto a `zDn…` key and then signs a Trust Task
the VTC accepts as from that DID; ES256 and ES256K holder signatures; an
ES256 OID4VCI proof issues to a P-256 holder, and one claiming `EdDSA` is
refused; `from_did_key` round-trips each curve.

title: spec(rooms)!: an unauthorized room request is refused with the standard permissionDenied
body:
Thirteen rooms specifications declared a task-specific `<slug>:notAuthorized` for a failure the framework already names. An authorization refusal is the standard `permissionDenied` (SPEC §7.2, §8.3).

**Specs changed:**
- `rooms/create` 0.1
- `rooms/epoch/{commits,mint,prune}` 0.1
- `rooms/keys/open` 0.1
- `rooms/keys/present` 0.1 and 0.2
- `rooms/owner/{claim,transfer}` 0.1
- `rooms/records/{curate,get,list,put}` 0.1

**Why it matters:**
- A consumer switching on `permissionDenied` never matched the extended code.
- A party that did not recognise it degraded it to `taskFailed` (§8.5), a worse signal than the standard code it duplicated.
- The later rooms specs (`records/put` 0.2 onward) already use the standard code, and the reference room host answers `permissionDenied` for every version. The 0.1 specs were the odd ones out.

This is the same correction as `vta/app-state:permissionDenied` in 0.11.3.

### Changes
- **Errors:** each `notAuthorized` declaration is withdrawn. Its condition is kept as one sentence at the end of the spec's Conformance section, naming `permissionDenied`.
- **Bindings:** regenerated. Only the Rust modules change, because the other three bindings don't carry error codes.

### Breaking for trust-tasks-rs
The 13 `error_codes::NOT_AUTHORIZED` constants are removed from the generated rooms modules. Emit `StandardCode::PermissionDenied` instead. verifiable-trust-infrastructure doesn't reference any of them.

### Checks
- **`npm run validate`:** 739 specs, no errors.
- **`npm run check-bindings`:** all four languages agree; 1670 error codes (13 fewer).
- **`cargo test -p trust-tasks-rs --all-features`:** passes.

title: ci: split Mobile build into iOS and Android legs, and start it in tier 1
body:
Mobile build was the last job to finish on every run that had it. On the
last main push it took 49 of the run's 53 minutes, with every other job done
by minute 17; on a PR that touched the lockfile, 36 of 42. One macOS job built
all five targets in turn, and started only after Clippy.

- Two matrix legs: `ios` on macOS (two targets, needs Xcode) and `android` on
  Linux (three ABIs through cargo-ndk; the Linux image ships the NDK). Each
  leg generates the UniFFI bindings from its own host build, so each stands
  alone, as `build-mobile.sh ios|android` already does.
- Tier 1 instead of tier 2: it needs tier 0 and `affects`, not Clippy. As the
  critical path, waiting for Clippy put Clippy's minutes on the whole run. A
  formatting slip or a stale lockfile still stops it before it starts.

The gate is unchanged: on a pull request it runs only for vta-mobile-core's
own sources or a global file.

Test (workspace) is left package-complete on purpose. Running only the
changed crates and their dependents with `-p` would change feature
unification, which is what made a per-crate run compile 306 tests where the
workspace run compiles 742 (CLAUDE.md, "Running the tests: green and wrong").
It takes 9-14 minutes and is not the critical path; Test (VTC, vetting-pcs)
is longer.
