title: perf(vta-service): multi-core REST and direct vsock inbound, failing closed (#2005)
body:
perf(vta-service): multi-core REST and direct vsock inbound, failing closed (#2005)

* perf(vta-service): serve REST on one worker per CPU

The REST server ran on its own current-thread tokio runtime, so every REST
handler shared one thread and the VTA could use at most one CPU however
many it had. In a Nitro enclave this showed as a 2-vCPU enclave half idle at
its ceiling (47%/62% per vCPU), with storage replies waiting for that one
thread to poll them.

With more than one CPU the REST runtime is now multi-threaded, one worker
per CPU. With one CPU it stays current-thread: a multi-threaded runtime was
measurably worse there (1-vCPU enclave at 220 keys/sign per second: 463
errors against 2).

Measured alone on c6g.4xlarge with a 2-vCPU enclave, in builds with extra
timing logging and an audit-key cache not in this series: at 320/s p95
840 -> 71 ms. With this series as it stands, c6g.4xlarge saturates at about
345/s with a 2-vCPU enclave and about 380 to 400/s with a 4-vCPU enclave.

Review note: handlers that interleaved only at await points now also run in
parallel. Existing non-atomic read-modify-write sequences were already racy
across await points; this makes those races more likely.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Carlos Rincon <carlos.r@affinidi.com>
(cherry picked from commit 503900091a4ea0ce33a9be5a87671e4c65272b2a)
Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* perf(vta-enclave): serve REST on vsock directly, without the inbound socat

Inbound REST reached the VTA through `socat VSOCK-LISTEN:5100,fork` to
127.0.0.1:8100: one forked process per connection. Under load the parent's
new connections timed out while socat forked (every error at 320 keys/sign
per second on a 4-vCPU enclave was one such timeout).

With vsock-store (enclave builds), the VTA binds vsock itself when
VTA_REST_VSOCK_PORT is set, and the entrypoint sets it instead of starting
the inbound socat. Every peer is reported as 127.0.0.1, which is what the
VTA saw through socat, so rate limiting and trusted X-Forwarded-For handling
are unchanged.

Measured alone on c6g.4xlarge with a 4-vCPU enclave, in builds with extra
timing logging and an audit-key cache not in this series: errors at 320/s
7 -> 0, at 400/s 43 -> 22; the remaining errors are the parent proxy's
256-connection inbound cap. Saturation unchanged.

Review notes: the entrypoint is part of the enclave image (and its PCR0).
Before the VTA binds the port, the parent's connections are refused rather
than accepted by socat; readiness checks should be confirmed against that.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Carlos Rincon <carlos.r@affinidi.com>
(cherry picked from commit 610241f184a031f64ea6787a56afd4114fb7f2de)
Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* test(vti-common): a refresh token stays single-use under a multi-thread runtime

The REST server now runs one worker per CPU, so two presentations of one
refresh token can be claimed on two threads at once. Sixteen concurrent
claims per token, twenty rounds, on the local store: exactly one wins each
time (RFC 9700 §4.14.2). The take_session_id_by_refresh doc no longer calls
the vsock path non-atomic; #1999 made it atomic.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(vta-service): enclave REST on vsock fails closed and trusts only the parent

Reworks the direct-vsock ingress from #1951 (review findings 2, 3, 6, 7).

- Fail closed. VTA_REST_VSOCK_PORT is read once at boot, before anything
  binds. A value that is not a vsock port (1 to 2^32-2), or any value in a
  build without vsock-store, refuses the boot with an error naming it. It
  used to be ignored, and the VTA served a TCP port that nothing forwards to
  in an enclave: no reachable API and no error.
- No dead TCP port. In vsock mode no TCP listener is opened at all (it was
  bound, never served, so in-enclave connections to it hung). The REST
  thread binds vsock on its own runtime and reports the result back; the
  boot waits for it, so a bind failure fails the boot, not a thread.
- Only the parent. The vsock listener accepts CID 3 only (others are
  dropped and logged with security_alert) and reports it as
  vti_common::rate_limit::VSOCK_PARENT_PEER, 0.0.0.3: never a valid TCP
  source, so neither a TCP peer nor anything inside the enclave can present
  it. Through socat the peer was 127.0.0.1, which any in-enclave process
  could also be. Trust stays a declaration: the Nitro configs move from
  trust_xff_cidrs = ["127.0.0.1/32"] to ["0.0.0.3/32"], so parent-proxy.sh
  (a byte bridge that must not be trusted) still refuses to start, and a
  stale loopback entry fails safe (one shared bucket) with a boot warning
  naming the fix. The parent proxy reads the same list, so it stops
  trusting TCP clients on its own loopback too.
- Docs: config.toml, config.fleet-base.toml, the Nitro README, the proxy
  module docs, Dockerfile.nitro, docs/02-vta/rate-limiting.md and the
  entrypoint describe the vsock ingress. The entrypoint is part of the
  image, so this is a new PCR0: operators pinning --expect-pcr0 re-measure.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(vta-service): bind the REST vsock listener once, so a soft restart cannot end the process

/vta/restart starts a new REST thread without joining the old one. The
vsock listener used to be bound per generation, inside the REST thread, so
the new generation could race the old one for the port: EADDRINUSE, the
ready channel reported an error, and `run` returned it, ending the process.

The vsock listener is now bound once at boot with the blocking `vsock`
listener, as TCP is, and each generation gets a try_clone() of the same
socket, adopted into its runtime through tokio-vsock's FromRawFd (the only
way 0.7 adopts a socket; one documented unsafe block, on an fd this code
owns exclusively). A bind failure is now the boot's error, before any
thread starts. Tested on the listener helper: a generation's clone keeps
serving the same port after the original is dropped (TCP everywhere; vsock
too where the host can bind AF_VSOCK).

Also:
- One PARENT_CID: vti_common::store::vsock::PARENT_CID is public and the
  REST listener uses it, instead of a third private copy.
- The boot warning for an enclave whose trust_xff_cidrs omits the parent
  is a tested function, and fires only when vsock mode is on and a
  non-empty list lacks 0.0.0.3. An empty list is a deliberate "trust
  nothing" (a byte-bridging parent), and the shipped list keeps
  127.0.0.1/32 for the parent proxy (see the next commit).

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(nitro): keep the parent proxy's loopback upstream trusted alongside the vsock parent

The parent's enclave-proxy reads [server] trust_xff_cidrs as its own
trusted_upstream_cidrs. Replacing ["127.0.0.1/32"] with ["0.0.0.3/32"]
made the proxy stop trusting a loopback upstream on the parent (a local
TLS terminator) and trust an address no TCP peer has, putting every client
behind that terminator in one rate-limit bucket.

The shipped Nitro configs now list both: 0.0.0.3/32 is the VTA's (the
parent over vsock), 127.0.0.1/32 the proxy's. Neither means anything to
the other program — the enclave VTA opens no TCP port, so no VTA peer is
ever 127.0.0.1, and no TCP peer of the proxy is ever 0.0.0.3 — so one key
can carry both without overloading a meaning, and no config schema
changes. The config comments, docs/02-vta/rate-limiting.md, the Nitro
README and the stale socat→127.0.0.1:8100 comment in the proxy's
channels.rs say so.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(nitro): drop the HEALTHCHECK that polled a port the enclave no longer opens

The image's HEALTHCHECK fetched http://localhost:8100/health. The VTA now
serves REST on vsock only and opens no TCP port, so the probe could only
fail. It is removed rather than replaced: the image runs solely as a Nitro
Enclave (nitro-cli build-enclave turns it into an EIF), where no Docker
runtime executes a HEALTHCHECK, and a process-alive probe would be a signal
that never goes false. Health is checked from the parent — GET /health
through deploy/nitro/enclave-proxy, as the load balancer's target check
already does. The Dockerfile says so where the HEALTHCHECK was.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(vta-service): vsock ingress keeps legacy XFF trust, never panics, backs off and cleans up

From the final combined review of #2005.

- Upgrade keeps rate limiting. On vsock the VTA binds no TCP, so a trusted
  127.0.0.1 in its config can only ever have meant the socat hop from the
  parent: it now also trusts the parent (0.0.0.3), logged once at info with
  how to make it explicit. Without this an upgraded ["127.0.0.1/32"] put
  every client in one bucket, so one client could lock everyone out of
  /auth and /bootstrap. Safe because a non-empty trust_xff_cidrs implies the
  Rust enclave-proxy, which sets X-Forwarded-For itself: parent-proxy.sh
  refuses to start whenever it is set. The boot warning now fires only on
  vsock for a non-empty list naming neither address; an empty list (a
  byte-bridging parent) trusts nothing and is not warned. TCP mode is
  unchanged. Tested as effective_trust_xff_cidrs, including end to end
  through the key extractor.
- Adoption cannot panic. The REST listener wraps the blocking vsock
  listener in AsyncFd itself (set_nonblocking and AsyncFd::new, both
  fallible) instead of tokio-vsock's FromRawFd, which unwraps; the REST
  runtime build is fallible too. A real OS error now reaches the boot
  through the ready channel. This also removes the unsafe block.
- A failed generation shuts down cleanly. If a soft restart's REST
  generation cannot adopt its listener, the iteration signals shutdown,
  cancels messaging, joins the REST thread and persists the store (what the
  not-yet-started storage thread would do) before returning the error.
- No accept-error flood. Accept failures back off 10 ms → 1 s (reset on
  success) and are warned on the first failure, then at most one summary
  per 10 s; recovery is logged once at info.

title: feat(vtc): wallet sign-in with a trigger link (auth/oob/*); SIOPv2 kept as legacy
body:
## Summary

The VTC side of wallet sign-in with a trigger link. The VTC acts as the sign-in service over the `auth/oob/*` Trust Tasks on `POST /v1/trust-tasks`.

- **`auth/oob/*` handlers** for `request`, `claim`, `prove`, `respond`, `redeem` and `cancel`, with `identify` and `grant` carried inside `prove` and `respond`. They follow contract C5 and C9:
  - The claim is by `K_a` and carries `parentThreadId` equal to `payload.requestId`.
  - `identify` is verified against the member's `authentication` key, and `grant` against `assertionMethod`.
  - The step 1 and step 2 responses are signed by the VTC's `assertionMethod` key (new `LocalSigner::sign_attested_response`).
  - `redeem` returns `{ subject, displayName, notAfter, amr }` and sets the member session as HttpOnly cookies. It goes through the same backend, keyspace and cookie shapes as every other portal sign-in.
  - `auth/oob/*` responses are `Cache-Control: no-store`.
- **Request state.** Requests live in the member-sessions keyspace under their own `oob_req:` prefix and are swept by the storage thread. The `K_b` key is held on the request record, not on the session.
- **Member portal.** "Sign in with your wallet" (a clickable trigger-link QR) is the default and first option. `GET /v1/member/sign-in/config` gives the page the community DID, the link host and the flow. The portal HTML is served with `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`, `no-store` and the default CSP.
- **SIOPv2 is deprecated (contract C7) but kept.** It is behind "Using an older wallet?", marked deprecated in code and docs, and not removed.
- **`vtc status`** reports whether the VTC's DID document lists the `SignInPortal` and `TrustTaskHTTPS` services, and names the fix if not.
- **Audit:** new `AuditEvent::MemberWalletSignIn` (city and country only, never the address).
- **Config:** new optional `admin_ui.sign_in_link_host`, defaulting to `link.trustoverip.org`.

The VTA side is in the companion PR: https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1997.

## Backwards compatibility

What I checked, against `feat/vtc-member-portal`:

- **SIOPv2 member-portal sign-in.**
  - Its routes are unchanged: `/v1/member/wallet/auth/challenge`, `/v1/member/wallet/auth/` and `/v1/member/wallet/auth/refresh`. So are `/v1/member/session` and the cookie names, paths and session format.
  - The backend change is doc comments only.
  - The existing integration tests in `tests/it/member_portal.rs` still pass. They cover the full challenge → `id_token` → session flow, refresh, the cookie session and cookie scoping.
  - In the UI, the SIOPv2 button and install guide moved inside a closed `<details>` "Using an older wallet?". `Portal.test.tsx` pins that the SIOPv2 button is still there and that the trigger-link option comes first.
- **`POST /v1/trust-tasks` dispatch.**
  - The `auth/oob/*` arm matches only `oob_tasks::URIS`, and `oob_tasks::precheck` returns `None` for every other type.
  - Every existing type routes exactly as before, and the `dispatcher_routes_every_dispatched_uri` census still covers them.
  - The new `HttpContext` task-local is read only by the `auth/oob` handlers. Cookies are appended only when a handler set some, and `no-store` only for `auth/oob/*` bodies.
- **`AuditEvent::MemberWalletSignIn`.**
  - `AuditEvent` is `#[non_exhaustive]` and adjacently tagged (`type`/`data`), so adding a variant leaves existing records byte-for-byte readable.
  - The payload's optional fields are `#[serde(default)]`.
  - An older binary skips an envelope it cannot parse rather than failing (`audit/writer.rs`). `vti-common`'s change is additive (a new variant on a non-exhaustive enum and a new struct).
- **Sessions and cookies.**
  - `vti_common::auth::Session` is unchanged. `K_b` lives on the `oob_req:` record, not on the session.
  - `cleanup_expired_sessions` iterates only `session:` and the new sweep only `oob_req:`, so neither reads the other's rows.
  - Sessions minted by `redeem` are ordinary member sessions, so existing sessions load as before.
- **Config.** `admin_ui.sign_in_link_host` is `Option` with `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]`, so existing configs start unchanged and a default config does not write it.
- **`TrustTaskHTTPS` follows the base convention (HTTPS binding 0.2 §6).**
  - `vtc status` checks for a `TrustTaskHTTPS` entry at the Trust-Task base `<public_url>/v1`, which is what the `vtc-host` template publishes. Clients POST to `<base>/trust-tasks`.
  - The check refuses an entry at the full `/v1/trust-tasks` URL, because base-plus-append consumers would reach `/v1/trust-tasks/trust-tasks`.
  - The handler stays at `POST /v1/trust-tasks`, and the portal posts there directly.

## Dependence on the VTA PR

There is no build-time dependency. This branch compiles and its tests pass on its own base, and it does not use the `ATTESTATION_SLUGS` change: the VTC states the purpose it requires (`assertionMethod` for `grant`, `authentication` for `identify`) and verifies against it directly. The dependency is at runtime: a member's wallet can complete sign-in only against a VTA that has the VTA PR. That VTA signs `grant` for `assertionMethod` after the device's user-verification consent, and enrols the UV key. Until then the VTC refuses a grant signed for `authentication`, as it should.

## Testing

Run locally on `feat/vtc-member-portal`, with the same commands CI uses:

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo clippy -p vtc-service --features vetting-pcs --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo nextest run --profile ci -p vtc-service -p vtc-client`: 2924 passed, 1 skipped.
- `cargo test -p vtc-service -p vtc-client --doc`: passed.
- `cargo nextest run --profile ci -p vti-common --all-features`: 740 passed.
- Admin UI (`vtc-service/admin-ui`): `npm run wire:check` clean, `npx tsc -b --noEmit` clean, and `npx vitest run` 863 of 863 passed across 73 files.

New tests:
- `vtc-service/tests/it/member_portal_oob.rs`: the whole `auth/oob` flow over `POST /v1/trust-tasks`, and its refusals.
- `oob.rs` unit tests, including the `TrustTaskHTTPS` base check.
- `WalletSignIn.test.tsx`.
- `Portal.test.tsx`: the option order, and SIOPv2 behind "Using an older wallet?".
- The `trust_task_manifest` census.

The existing SIOPv2 integration tests in `tests/it/member_portal.rs` are unchanged and pass.

## Known follow-ups

- The plugin's VTA-minted holder is not an enrolled device. The VTA signs `identify` only for an enrolled device, and `register_device` overwrites the ACL entry's kind. A decision on how the plugin enrols is pending.
- The browser session key (design §12.9) is not built.
- GeoIP is stubbed to "unknown".
- Existing VTCs need `dids edit` plus `cnm did-log install` to publish the `TrustTaskHTTPS` and `SignInPortal` services. `vtc status` names the exact entries.

## Related

- Companion VTA PR: https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1997.
- https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-vti-spec/pull/58

## Backport

title: perf(storage): atomic take / insert-if-absent / swap / compare-and-move in the parent proxy
body:
Part E1 of the plan for #1951 (TEE `keys/sign` throughput). **Stacked on #1999** (enclave-side per-key locks; rebased onto its round-trip deadline, `4847c198`); merge that first.

## Design
The parent's storage proxy now serves the enclave store's claims and moves as single operations, advertised by a capability probe:

| Opcode | Replaces | Round trips (old → new) |
|---|---|---|
| `OP_TAKE` (get + delete) — `take_raw`, the refresh-token claim | GET, DELETE | 2 → 1 |
| `OP_INSERT_IF_ABSENT` — `insert_if_absent`, `insert_raw_if_absent` | GET, INSERT | 2 → 1 |
| `OP_SWAP_IF_ABSENT` — `swap` | GET, INSERT, DELETE | 3 → 1 |
| `OP_MOVE_IF_EQUAL` — `move_if_unchanged` | GET, GET, INSERT, DELETE | 4 → 2 |
| `OP_HELLO` | — | once per connect |

- **Parent:** each op runs under a per-keyspace `std::sync::Mutex` held across its fjall steps. It's a mutex, not fjall's transactional database: the critical sections are a few fjall calls with no `await`, and switching the database type would touch every operation. Plain get/insert/delete don't take it, matching the local store.
- **Off the workers:** each op's critical section (the lock plus the fjall calls under it) runs in `tokio::task::spawn_blocking`. Contended ops on one keyspace (every refresh-token claim) therefore wait on the blocking pool instead of tying up runtime workers and starving plain reads on other connections. The std mutex stays: nothing under it awaits. A dropped connection never cancels a section midway.
- **Crash-atomic moves:** swap-if-absent and move-if-equal commit their insert and delete as **one fjall write batch** (one journal record, one seqno), so a parent crash never leaves the moved-from row live beside its replacement.
- **Reply frames** up to 64 KiB go out in one write (#1951 follow-up); larger ones are written as header then payload, not copied (the enclave client's rule).
- **Never resent once possibly applied:** the enclave pool has `request` (idempotent: get/insert/delete/scans/HELLO, resent once as before) and `request_once` (the atomic ops).
  - A `request_once` is resent only if its frame was not completely written; the proxy reads a whole frame before acting.
  - The 10 s round-trip deadline from #1999 follows the same rule: expiry after the frame was fully written is outcome-unknown, and expiry before is a not-sent retry.
  - After that, any failure is `OutcomeUnknown`: returned as an error, never resent, and **no single-op fallback**, since either could apply it twice (a resent take would refuse a legitimate refresh; a resent move would report `TargetExists` for a move that happened).
  - Idle connections are checked before use with one non-blocking read poll (no-op waker). An idle connection owes nothing, so `Pending` means live; EOF, an error or stray bytes discard it before any write. A parent that closed an idle connection therefore doesn't produce an outcome-unknown error; a close that lands after the check is reported as unknown, the safe direction.
  - `OnceError` is the typed form inside the crate. Callers see `AppError::Internal("…outcome unknown…")`, because adding an `AppError` variant would be a breaking change.
- **Enclave:** the per-key locks from #1999 are still held around every operation. That gives defence in depth, and the same exactly-one guarantee on the single-op fallback.

## The parent never needs plaintext
Values are AES-256-GCM ciphertext bound to (keyspace, key). Take, insert-if-absent and swap move opaque bytes. For compare-and-move, the **enclave** reads the row, decrypts it and compares plaintext; it then asks the proxy to move only while the row still holds *the exact ciphertext it just read*. The test `the_parent_never_sees_plaintext` asserts no plaintext reaches the parent in either mode.

## Compatibility: either side may be upgraded first
- **New enclave, old proxy:** `HELLO` gets "unknown opcode", so capabilities are 0 and the enclave uses today's single operations.
- **Any other error to `HELLO` fails the probe, and the connect.** HELLO reads no storage and takes no input, so a proxy that refuses it is broken or not the proxy expected; guessing "none" would hide that on the slow path.
- **Old enclave, new proxy:** the enclave never sends the new opcodes.
- **Proxy downgraded mid-run:** the next atomic op gets "unknown opcode"; nothing was applied, so it falls back and succeeds.
- **Re-probe:** with no capabilities known, the next operation after 60 s asks again (one caller does), so a proxy upgraded again, or one that was old at boot, is used atomically without an enclave restart.
- `deploy/nitro/README.md` documents this.

## Tests
- **Proxy** (`cargo test --release --locked`, 53 passed): each op and its outcomes; 64-wide concurrency on a 4-worker runtime with exactly one winner for take / insert-if-absent / swap / move; truncated and over-long fields return errors rather than panicking. Every move commits exactly one write batch and a refused move commits none. A small frame is one write; a large one is two, with the payload not copied; a 192 KiB frame round-trips. Contention: with two workers and two contended ops holding / waiting for a 300 ms critical section, a GET on another keyspace answers within 100 ms. With the lock taken on the worker (the old placement), the same test fails at about 310 ms; five reruns of the new code pass. `cargo clippy --release --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` is clean; fmt clean.
- **Enclave** (`cargo test -p vti-common --features vsock-store,encryption --lib store::`, 144 passed):
  - every exactly-one test runs 32-wide against **both** proxy generations;
  - `atomic_opcodes_cut_round_trips` counts requests: old `[2,2,3,4]` vs new `[1,1,1,2]`;
  - an older proxy probes as no capabilities;
  - a mid-run downgrade falls back without failing;
  - every `move_if_unchanged` outcome matches in both modes;
  - no plaintext reaches the parent;
  - an `OP_TAKE` or `OP_SWAP_IF_ABSENT` that was applied and then hung up on returns an error: one frame, no resend, no fallback, state applied once;
  - pool: an atomic request is not resent after its frame was received, while an idempotent one is; a write failure before sending is retried and applied once; a stale idle connection is discarded without error;
  - pool deadline: an atomic request whose reply never comes times out as outcome-unknown (one frame, no resend, connection dropped); one whose write never completes times out and goes out once on a new connection;
  - `HELLO` refused otherwise fails the probe; a downgraded-then-upgraded proxy is re-probed and used again; there's no re-probe before it's due.
- Also passes with `vsock-store` alone (55 vsock tests). Clippy is clean with `vsock-store,encryption`, `vsock-store` alone and default features; fmt clean.

## Risks
- **Resolved: an undecryptable `OP_TAKE` no longer destroys the row** (`bae14a1d`).
  - **The problem:** `OP_TAKE` deletes in the parent before the enclave decrypts. Before this fix, a value that failed to decrypt or authenticate was gone once the error came back, so a storage-key misconfiguration would have wiped every row a claim touched.
  - **The fix:** the enclave re-inserts the exact bytes it received at the same key, while still holding the key's lock, and then returns the original decrypt error. The restore uses `OP_INSERT_IF_ABSENT` where the proxy serves it, so a legitimate value written meanwhile is never overwritten; otherwise `OP_INSERT`. If the restore itself fails, it's logged at `error` with `security_alert = true`, and the decrypt error is still returned.
  - **Tests:** with the wrong key, the row is still present and byte-identical in both proxy generations, and the right key then claims it once. With encryption on, a successful take is still one round trip; the restore path is two.
- The proxy is a separate binary, so the parent and the enclave image can roll out in either order (see Compatibility above).

Credit: #1951 (Carlos Rincon) measured the round trips this removes and proposed the one-write reply.

title: perf(storage): atomic take / insert-if-absent / swap / compare-and-move in the parent proxy (#2003)
body:
perf(storage): atomic take / insert-if-absent / swap / compare-and-move in the parent proxy (#2003)

* perf(enclave-proxy): atomic take / insert-if-absent / swap / compare-and-move

The enclave store's claims and moves were sequences of single operations
over vsock: two round trips for a take or an insert-if-absent, three for a
swap, four for a compare-and-move. The proxy now serves each as one
operation (OP_TAKE, OP_INSERT_IF_ABSENT, OP_SWAP_IF_ABSENT,
OP_MOVE_IF_EQUAL), advertised by OP_HELLO, under a per-keyspace lock held
across its fjall steps. A plain mutex rather than fjall's transactional
database: the critical sections are a few fjall calls with no await, and
switching the database type would touch every operation.

None needs plaintext. Values are ciphertext bound to (keyspace, key);
OP_MOVE_IF_EQUAL compares the stored ciphertext with bytes the enclave has
just read and compared in plaintext itself.

Each reply frame now goes out in one write (it was two packets). A DID-log
write through any of the new operations still lands on disk.

Tests: each op, its outcomes, 64-wide concurrency with exactly one winner
on a multi-thread runtime, and truncated / over-long fields as errors.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* perf(vti-common): use the proxy's atomic operations, falling back to single ones

VsockStore::connect asks the proxy which atomic operations it serves
(OP_HELLO). take_raw, insert_if_absent, insert_raw_if_absent, swap and
move_if_unchanged use them when present: 1, 1, 1, 1 and 2 round trips
instead of 2, 2, 2, 3 and 4. The enclave's per-key locks are still held
around every one, so a proxy without them, or one replaced by an older
build while the enclave runs (detected by 'unknown opcode' on the next
atomic op, which then falls back without failing), keeps the exactly-one
guarantee on single operations. Either side may be upgraded first.

move_if_unchanged compares plaintext in the enclave, then asks the proxy
to move only while the row still holds the ciphertext just read: the parent
never sees what it compares.

Tests: every exactly-one test runs against both proxy generations; round
trips per operation are counted; an older proxy probes as none; a
downgrade mid-run falls back; with encryption, no plaintext reaches the
parent. deploy/nitro/README.md states the compatibility rule.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(vti-common): an undecryptable OP_TAKE restores the row instead of losing it

OP_TAKE deletes in the parent before the enclave decrypts, so a value
that failed to decrypt or authenticate was gone by the time the error was
returned. With a storage-key misconfiguration that would silently wipe every
row a claim touches; the two-step path had always left it in place.

Now the enclave re-inserts the exact bytes it received at the same key,
still holding the key's lock, and returns the original decrypt error. The
restore uses OP_INSERT_IF_ABSENT where the proxy serves it, so a legitimate
value written meanwhile is never overwritten, else OP_INSERT. A failed
restore is logged at error with security_alert = true.

Tests (fake parent, both proxy generations): the row is still present and
byte-identical after a take with the wrong key, and the right key then
claims it once; with encryption on, a successful take is still one round
trip and the restore path is two (OP_TAKE, OP_INSERT_IF_ABSENT).

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(enclave-proxy): commit a move as one write batch; copy only small reply frames

move_locked (OP_SWAP_IF_ABSENT, OP_MOVE_IF_EQUAL) wrote the new row and
removed the old one as two fjall writes, so a parent crash between them
left both rows: the moved-from row still live beside its replacement, e.g.
an old ACL DID keeping its authority. They are now one fjall write batch,
one journal record under one sequence number, which recovery replays whole
or not at all. No other operation writes more than once. A test asserts
every move commits exactly one batch, refused moves commit none, and the
outcomes are unchanged.

write_frame copied every reply into a fresh buffer to send it in one write,
and a prefix scan can answer with up to 16 MB. Frames up to 64 KiB are
still coalesced (the enclave client's rule); larger ones are written as
header then payload. Tests: a small frame is one write, a large one two
with the payload as given, and a 192 KiB frame round-trips.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(vti-common): never resend an atomic storage op that may have been applied

ConnectionPool::request resent a frame on a fresh connection after any
failure, including a failure while reading the reply. That is harmless for
get/insert/delete and wrong for the atomic ops: an OP_TAKE applied before
the connection dropped, resent, finds nothing and refuses a legitimate
refresh with the token already gone; a resent OP_SWAP_IF_ABSENT reports
TargetExists for a move that happened.

The pool now has request (idempotent, resent as before) and request_once.
A request_once is resent only if it failed before its frame was completely
written: the proxy reads a whole frame before acting, so a partial one
cannot have been applied. Once the frame is out, any failure is
OnceError::OutcomeUnknown and is never resent; the store returns it as an
error and does not fall back to single operations, which could apply it a
second time. (OnceError is the typed form inside the crate; adding a
variant to the published AppError would be a breaking change, so callers
see an Internal error saying the outcome is unknown.)

So that a connection the parent closed while idle does not make that error
routine, idle connections are checked before use: one non-blocking poll of
the read side with a no-op waker. An idle connection owes nothing, so a live
one is Pending; Ready means EOF, an error or unsolicited bytes, and the
connection is discarded before any byte is written. A close that lands after
the check is still reported as outcome unknown, the safe direction.

The capability probe: only 'unknown opcode' to HELLO means an older proxy.
Any other error fails the probe and so the connect: HELLO reads no storage
and takes no input, so a proxy that refuses it is broken or not the proxy
expected, and guessing 'none' would hide that on the slow path. And an
'unknown opcode' on an atomic op no longer zeroes the capabilities for the
life of the enclave: with none known, the next operation after
REPROBE_AFTER (60 s) asks again (one caller; the rest stay on the single-op
path meanwhile), so a briefly downgraded proxy is used atomically again
without a restart.

Tests: pool - an atomic request whose frame was received and not answered
is not resent (one frame), an idempotent one is; a write failure before the
frame is sent is retried and applied once; a stale idle connection is
discarded without error; a live one is not stale. Store, fake parent - an
OP_TAKE or OP_SWAP_IF_ABSENT applied and then hung up on gives an error,
one frame, state applied exactly once; HELLO refused otherwise fails the
probe; a downgraded-then-upgraded proxy is re-probed and used again; no
re-probe before it is due.

The round-trip deadline (ROUND_TRIP_TIMEOUT) keeps the same rule: a
deadline that expires after the frame was completely written is outcome
unknown (never resent); one that expires before is a not-sent retry. Tests:
an atomic request whose reply never comes times out as outcome unknown,
one frame, connection dropped; one whose write never completes times out
and goes out once on a new connection.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(enclave-proxy): run atomic ops' critical sections on the blocking pool

Each atomic operation took its keyspace's std::sync::Mutex inside an async
handler and held it across synchronous fjall I/O on a tokio worker thread.
Contended ops on one keyspace (every refresh-token claim lands on the same
one) then occupy workers twice over, the holder doing blocking I/O and the
waiters blocked on the lock, and every connection task on those workers -
plain GET/INSERT on other keyspaces included - waits behind them.

The lock and the fjall calls under it now run in tokio::task::spawn_blocking
(critical_section). The mutex stays a std one: nothing under it awaits, and
blocking work under a blocking lock is what the blocking pool is for. A
dropped connection no longer cancels anything midway: the section runs to
its end. The one-write-batch move is unchanged.

Test: two workers, two contended ops on one keyspace holding / waiting for
a 300 ms critical section; once both have reached the lock, a GET on
another keyspace from a worker task must answer within 100 ms. Checked
against the old placement (lock taken inline on the worker): the read
waited 310 ms and the test failed.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

title: perf(vta-service): fewer storage reads per keys/sign without widening key custody
body:
## What and why

Part B of the rework of #1951 (Carlos Rincon's TEE `keys/sign` throughput PR). It keeps that PR's sign-path saving — **10 storage operations per `keys/sign` down to 8** — and fixes what review found in how it got there.

**Kept from #1951** (cherry-picked with `-x`, authorship and sign-off preserved):
- `fcc9f0d7` perf(vta-service): read the caller's ACL entry once per keys/sign (from 72371e53)
- `bd000667` perf(vta-service): reuse the context record for the keys/sign custody check (from 7e284648)

**Changed on top:**
- **Finding 8 — nested Option in a security gate.** `require_key_in_caller_scope` took `Option<Option<AclEntry>>` (outer `None` = not read, inner `None` = no row); a future `Some(None)` for a skipped lookup would silently pass gate 4 (#818). The row is now read once into `CallerAcl`, which has no "not read" state, and both gates take `&CallerAcl`. Same gates, same order, same audited refusals. `ensure_may_sign` keeps `Result<()>` for its other callers.
- **Finding 9 — key custody trusted a caller-supplied record.** `derive_record_key_in_context(…, Option<&ContextRecord>, …)` is gone. `key_custody::load_sign_context` does the one context read itself and returns a `CustodyContext` (private fields — only key custody constructs one), and `derive_record_key_in` takes it. The base path rule 6 checks comes only from key custody's own read in this request; a `CustodyContext` read for another context falls back to the record's own context. Key custody is again the only code that decides the base path, as CLAUDE.md requires.
- **Finding 10 — per-ancestor clone on the hot path.** `effective_context_policy_and_record` cloned every ancestor's `ContextPolicy`. It now resolves over borrowed policies; nothing is cloned and the leaf record comes back whole.

## Tests
- New: `gate_4_binds_a_protocol_defined_signature_too` — gate 0 does not run for `ProtocolDefined`, gate 4 still refuses a key outside `allowed_keys`.
- New: `the_sign_contexts_base_comes_from_custodys_own_read` — a `CustodyContext` read for another context cannot vouch for a foreign path; both refusals audited.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` — clean

- `key_custody_census` passes unchanged (no new raw seed access).

Not re-run: the enclave load test; storage-op count is unchanged from #1951's measured build (8 per sign).

title: perf(vta-service): fewer storage reads per keys/sign without widening key custody (#2001)
body:
perf(vta-service): fewer storage reads per keys/sign without widening key custody (#2001)

* perf(vta-service): read the caller's ACL entry once per keys/sign

sign_payload read the caller's ACL entry twice: once for the sign
capability (gate 0) and again for the allowed-keys filter (gate 4). The
entry from gate 0 is now passed to gate 4, which reads it itself only when
gate 0 did not run (protocol-defined signing input). Both gates still run,
in the same order, and now see the same version of the entry.

One storage round trip fewer per keys/sign.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Carlos Rincon <carlos.r@affinidi.com>
(cherry picked from commit 72371e53a019b9d6062152667fdb671df373ef51)
Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* perf(vta-service): reuse the context record for the keys/sign custody check

keys/sign read the key's context record twice: once while resolving the
context policy chain, and again in key custody for the context's base path.
effective_context_policy_and_record (vta-support) returns the leaf record
it already read, and derive_record_key_in_context (key_custody) takes it.

Custody stays the only way to derived key material and keeps its check:
the passed record is used only when its id is the key record's context,
otherwise custody reads the context itself, so a mismatched record cannot
supply the base path. derive_record_key keeps its signature and behaviour.

One storage round trip fewer per keys/sign in a top-level context.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Carlos Rincon <carlos.r@affinidi.com>
(cherry picked from commit 7e284648ea3cbc34b5de40b8eff5db2d5959153a)
Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* perf(vta-support): resolve the context chain's policy without cloning it

effective_context_policy_and_record cloned every ancestor's ContextPolicy
(key allowlists, quota maps) on each keys/sign only to keep the leaf record.
It now keeps the records and resolves over borrowed policies, so nothing is
cloned per ancestor, and the leaf comes back whole, its own policy included.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* refactor(vta-service): keys/sign reads once through types that cannot widen custody

Keeps the two reads #1951 saved per keys/sign (10 storage operations to 8)
and removes the two ways it made the gates easier to misuse.

- The caller's ACL row is read once into `CallerAcl` and both gates take it.
  `require_key_in_caller_scope` took `Option<Option<AclEntry>>`, where outer
  `None` meant "not read" and inner `None` "no row": a caller passing
  `Some(None)` for a lookup it skipped would have passed gate 4 (#818).
  `CallerAcl` has no "not read" state. Same gates, same order, same refusals;
  `ensure_may_sign` keeps its `Result<()>` for its other callers.
- `derive_record_key_in_context` trusted a caller-supplied `ContextRecord` for
  the custody base path. It is replaced by `key_custody::load_sign_context`,
  which does the one context read itself and returns a `CustodyContext` only
  key custody can construct, and `derive_record_key_in`, which takes one. The
  base path rule 6 checks therefore again comes only from key custody's own
  read in this request; a context read for another context falls back to the
  record's own.

Tests: gate 4 refuses a ProtocolDefined signature (gate 0 does not run there);
a CustodyContext read for another context cannot vouch for a foreign path.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* refactor(vta-service): one call into key custody from the sign path

derive_record_key_in now takes Option<&CustodyContext>: None, or a context
read for another record, falls back to derive_record_key inside key custody.
The sign path no longer duplicates the eight-argument derive_record_key call
in a match arm. Gates, census and audited refusals unchanged.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

title: fix(vta-enclave): bounded, visible log loss; warnings and errors never dropped
body:
## What and why

Part D of the #1951 rework. Carries Carlos Rincon's commit from #1951 (`fix(vta-enclave): log to stderr only while vsock logging is down`, cherry-picked with `-x`), which removes the per-line console write that capped throughput, and fixes the two log-loss findings from its review.

| Review finding | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|
| 4: lines queued while connected were drained and dropped during reconnect backoff, and with stderr skipped they vanished entirely | `while rx.try_recv().is_ok() {}` on every retry | The queue is left alone (bounded, so memory cannot grow) and sent after reconnect, in order, after the line whose write failed |
| 5: a full channel dropped lines silently, with no console fallback | `let _ = tx.try_send(..)` | Drops are counted; one `vsock-log: dropped N lines (queue full)` line precedes the next line that fits. WARN/ERROR lines that cannot be queued go to stderr. The level comes from event metadata (`make_writer_for`), not text |

The module docs now say exactly what can still be lost: a line handed to a write that fails on both the old and the new connection.

CI: the enclave job now compiles `vsock-log` (both its feature sets). It is in the Nitro image and was otherwise only checked by hand.

## Tested
- 9 unit tests in `vsock_log` (the drain task is generic over the stream and connector, so they run without vsock): drop counting and marker, a marker that does not fit, WARN/ERROR fallback, no double console write, level from metadata, and replay of queued lines after an outage (fails against the old drain-and-drop).
- `cargo check` / `cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings` for `vta-enclave` with `rest,didcomm,vsock-store,vsock-log` and `...,tenant-overlay` (macOS); `cargo fmt --check`; actionlint.

**Only CI / an enclave can verify:** Linux compilation of the CI feature sets, and behaviour against the real parent log receiver.

## Backport
none

title: fix(vta-enclave): bounded, visible log loss; warnings and errors never dropped (#2000)
body:
fix(vta-enclave): bounded, visible log loss; warnings and errors never dropped (#2000)

* fix(vta-enclave): log to stderr only while vsock logging is down

The enclave's log writer wrote every line synchronously to stderr before
queueing it for the asynchronous vsock forwarder. Inside the enclave stderr
is the console, and a production enclave runs without `--debug-mode`, so
nobody can read it; every write is still synchronous and serialised on the
`Stderr` lock. At INFO the VTA logs about four lines per request, and this
capped throughput: in load tests an appliance saturated at about 97
keys/sign per second, and handled at least 160 without errors once the
per-request lines were no longer written.

The drain task now records whether the vsock connection is up, and the
writer falls back to stderr only while it is not (boot before the first
connection, reconnects), so boot failures still reach the console. The
vsock stream, which is where operators read the logs, is unchanged.

Signed-off-by: Carlos Rincon <carlos.r@affinidi.com>
(cherry picked from commit 660db6fa6b1e1dce6fcd444e9b83a8a5df4227cd)
Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(vta-enclave): bounded, visible log loss; warnings and errors never dropped

Follow-up to the commit above (from #1951), addressing two findings of its
review.

- A disconnect no longer drains and drops the queue. `connect_with_backoff`
  emptied the channel on every retry, and with stderr skipped while
  connected those lines were lost entirely, usually the ones explaining the
  outage. The queue is left alone (it is bounded, so memory cannot grow) and
  sent after the reconnect, in order, after the line whose write failed.
- A full channel no longer drops silently. Lost lines are counted, and one
  `vsock-log: dropped N lines (queue full)` line precedes the next line that
  fits. A WARN or ERROR line that cannot be queued goes to stderr instead;
  the level comes from the event metadata (`make_writer_for`), not text.
- The drain task is generic over the stream and how to open it, so the
  policy is unit-tested without vsock: drop counting, the marker, the
  WARN/ERROR fallback, the level decision, and replay after an outage.
- CI's enclave job now compiles `vsock-log`, which is in the Nitro image and
  was otherwise only checked by hand.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(vta-enclave): a stalled log receiver is a disconnect, not a latched connected

Review of #2000 (R6.2, no latched status): `connected` stayed true while a
write to the parent was blocked. A receiver that stops reading but keeps the
socket open reports no error, so the drain task blocked forever, the queue
filled, INFO/DEBUG lines were only counted, and stderr stayed silent because
every writer believed the connection was up.

Every write (lines and heartbeats) is now bounded by WRITE_TIMEOUT (2 s: a
healthy write takes well under a millisecond, and 2 s is short against the
15 s heartbeat and against how fast a busy enclave fills the queue). A
timeout is treated as a disconnect: connected goes false so writers fall
back to stderr, the unsent line and the queue are kept, and the task
reconnects with backoff, replaying them in order.

Test: a sink that accepts the connection but never reads; after the timeout
connected goes false, a new line reaches stderr, and both lines are replayed
after a working reconnect.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

---------

Signed-off-by: Carlos Rincon <carlos.r@affinidi.com>
Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>
Co-authored-by: Carlos Rincon <carlos.r@affinidi.com>

title: feat(vta-sdk)!: wallet sign-in with a trigger link: sign auth/oob grants, enrol UV keys, advertise TrustTaskHTTPS and SignInPortal
body:
## Summary

The VTA side of wallet sign-in with a trigger link. The VTC is the sign-in service over the `auth/oob/*` Trust Tasks, and the member's VTA signs the two documents the wallet carries:

- **`auth/oob/grant` is an attestation (VTI-KEY-106).** It is added to `ATTESTATION_SLUGS`, so the VTA signs it for `assertionMethod`. `auth/oob/identify` stays operational and is signed for `authentication`, as the service verifies it.
- **Default policy for sign-in documents on `vault/sign-trust-task`.** `identify` and `grant` must match an exact schema. They are signed only for an enrolled, active device, as the entry's own principal, for one of the entry's targets, and within a clock-skew window. A `grant` also needs a never-reused id and the device's user-verification consent in `ext["org.openvtc.uv-consent"]`. That consent is a signed `task-consent/decision/0.2` over the digest of the unsigned grant. It can come from a hardware key or a WebAuthn ES256 passkey, verified with `vti-webauthn`. Each signature is audited, and a signature the audit trail cannot record is withheld.
- **User-verification key enrolment.** `device/register/0.2` and `device/heartbeat/0.2` accept an optional `ext["org.openvtc.uv-key"]`. It is stored on `DeviceBinding.uv_key` and summarised on the binding under `ext["org.openvtc"].uvKey`. A malformed key is refused. A disabled or wiped device cannot enrol one, and a replacement is accepted only on heartbeat.
- **`vtc-host` template.** It now advertises `TrustTaskHTTPS` (`#trust-tasks`, `{URL}{TRUST_TASKS_BASE}`, default `/v1`) and `SignInPortal` (`#sign-in-portal`, `{URL}{SIGN_IN_PORTAL_PATH}`, default `/members/`).
- **Many devices per member.** Each device (every browser install, every phone) has its own DID, its own ACL entry, and so its own binding, `consumerKind`, form factor and UV key. The gate checks the caller's own row. It checks a grant's UV decision against that row's UV key and the caller's own transport key, never another device's. Disabling or wiping one device changes one row, and the member's other devices keep signing in. A disabled or wiped device is refused with the new `oobDeviceDisabled`, distinct from `oobNotEnrolledDevice` (no binding, which the device fixes with `device/register`). No data-model change was needed; the design is in `design-docs/vta-multi-device.md` in the workspace docs.
- **Tests.** New tests pin that every built-in template and every VTA-minted document lists an `assertionMethod` key, so a persona can sign a grant.

The `vtc-service` side is in the companion PR: https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1998.

## Backwards compatibility

What I checked, against `main`:

- **`ATTESTATION_SLUGS`.** `auth/oob/grant` is appended. The three existing slugs and their purposes are unchanged, and the proof-purpose classifier test still pins them. The constant's type grows from `[&str; 3]` to `[&str; 4]`, so the commit is marked `!`. No code in this workspace or in its sibling repos names that type.
- **`vtc-host.json` services.**
  - The template renders only when a DID is minted, so existing VTC DIDs are unaffected until someone runs `dids edit`.
  - The new variables are in `optionalVars` with defaults.
  - `VTCRest` and `VTCStatusList` are byte-for-byte unchanged and keep indices 0 and 1 when there is no transport.
  - The `TrustRegistry` referral moves from index 2 to 4. I searched production code for service selection by index or position and found none. All such uses are in `#[cfg(test)]` modules, and production code matches on `type` or `id`.
- **The VTC's `TrustTaskHTTPS` follows the base convention in HTTPS binding 0.2 §6.** Its `serviceEndpoint` is the Trust-Task base (`{URL}/v1`), and clients POST to `<base>/trust-tasks`, which is `/v1/trust-tasks`. Every existing consumer composes the URL this way: `vti-common`'s push engine, `vta-service`'s outbound REST and DID-hosting transport, `vta-sdk`'s `ServiceCapabilities`, the browser plugin and DID hosting. The `did-host-http*` templates already publish `{URL}/api` as a base. An earlier draft of this branch published the full URL, which would have sent those peers to `/v1/trust-tasks/trust-tasks`. A test now pins that the rendered entry resolves, through `ServiceCapabilities`, to the base.
- **`device/register/0.2` and `device/heartbeat/0.2`.** The `org.openvtc.uv-key` extension is optional. A client that does not send it gets exactly the old behaviour: no `uv_key`, no extra audit event, and no `ext` added to the wire binding unless local capabilities already put one there.
- **`vault/sign-trust-task/0.2` and the UV-consent gate.** The gate classifies the envelope first and returns early for anything outside the `auth/oob/` family, so every other type signs exactly as before. Within the family, only `auth/oob/grant/0.1` requires `org.openvtc.uv-consent`. `identify/0.1` is policed without one. Other `auth/oob/*` types, which no VTA signed before because the family is new, are refused rather than signed unattended. The new optional `ext` member on the request body is ignored for every non-grant type.
- **Multi-device.**
  - No storage or wire-shape change.
  - `register`, `heartbeat`, `list`, `disable` and `wipe` keep their requests and responses.
  - A registration still writes only the caller's own entry, so it cannot change the kind or binding of the member's administrative entries or of another device.
  - The one behaviour change is on this PR's own unreleased gate: a disabled or wiped device now gets `oobDeviceDisabled` instead of `oobNotEnrolledDevice`.
  - `OobError` (new in this PR) is `#[non_exhaustive]`.
  - A test writes an ACL row in the pre-`uvKey`, pre-`version` shape raw. It still loads, signs `identify` and enrols a passkey on heartbeat.
- **Storage.**
  - `DeviceBinding.uv_key` is `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]`. Old ACL rows load unchanged, and a row with no UV key serialises exactly as before.
  - `AclEntry`/`DeviceBinding` are not `deny_unknown_fields`, so an older VTA reading a row that has a UV key ignores the field.
  - The new audit actions are plain strings in the existing record shape.
- **Public API.** I ran `cargo semver-checks` against `main`.
  - **`vta-sdk`:** 196 checks pass. Everything is additive.
  - **`vti-common`:** one finding, `constructible_struct_adds_field` for `DeviceBinding.uv_key`, so a struct literal outside the crate would need `uv_key: None`. Nothing outside this repo constructs `DeviceBinding`; I checked the sibling OpenVTC and Affinidi repos. The commit is marked `feat(vti-common)!` so the release tooling sizes the bump.
  - **`vta-service`:** `register_device` and `heartbeat_device` gained parameters. `OobError` and the rest of `oob_sign_in` are new in this PR. Against this branch's previous head, the only finding is the added `OobError::DeviceDisabled` variant, and the enum is now `#[non_exhaustive]` so later variants are not breaking.
- **`notAfter` on a grant.** The VTA's check accepts integer epoch seconds (contract C9) and also RFC 3339 timestamps. That is deliberately lenient as a reader, and it is left accepting both.

## Dependence with the VTC PR

There is no build-time dependency in either direction. Each PR compiles and passes on its own base, and the VTC PR does not use the `ATTESTATION_SLUGS` change, because it names the purpose it requires and verifies against it. The dependency is at runtime: wallet sign-in against a VTC with #1998 completes only when the member's VTA has this PR, which signs `grant` for `assertionMethod` after the device's user-verification consent. A VTA without it signs a grant for `authentication`, and the VTC correctly refuses it.

## Testing

Run locally after rebasing onto current `main`, with the same commands CI uses.

Re-run for the multi-device commit:
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, and `cargo clippy` for `--workspace --all-targets`, `--workspace --all-features --all-targets` and the three reduced `vta-service` feature sets: all clean.
- Every `cargo check` feature combo, including `rest,didcomm` without `webvh`: clean.
- `cargo nextest run -p vta-service -p vti-common -p vta-sdk`, the `--doc` tests, `setup::interactive`, `routes::bootstrap` and `transport_harness_tests`: all pass.
- `vta-enclave` with `vsock-store` is Linux-only and was not built locally; this commit does not touch it.

Earlier results:

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo clippy -p vta-service --no-default-features` with `rest`, with `setup,keyring,rest,tsp,cli-synthesis` and with `setup,keyring,rest,didcomm,cli-synthesis`, all `--all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Every other command in the "Feature combos (vta-service builds)" job is clean, including `rest,didcomm` without `webvh`, which the first push missed (fixed in e85538c1), and the `setup::interactive` and `routes::bootstrap` test runs. The commands are `cargo check -p vta-service --no-default-features` with `tee,rest,didcomm`, `rest,didcomm`, `aws-secrets,keyring,rest` and `azure-secrets,keyring,rest`.
- `cargo check -p vta-sdk --features client,sealed-transfer,provision-integration`: clean.
- `cargo nextest run --profile ci --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client`: 5446 passed, 23 skipped.
- `cargo test --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client --doc`: passed.
- `cargo test -p vta-sdk --all-features`: passed.
- `cargo nextest run --profile ci -p vtc-service -p vtc-client`: 2871 passed, 1 skipped. This shows the `vti-common` change does not affect the VTC.
- `cargo semver-checks --baseline-rev origin/main -p vta-sdk -p vti-common`: `vta-sdk` clean. `vti-common` has the one finding described above.

New tests:
- `vta-service/tests/it/vault_sign_in_oob.rs`: the sign-in policy end to end, covering an enrolled device, UV consent from a hardware key and from a passkey, replay, and the refusals. It also covers one member with two browsers and a phone:
  - each device signs with its own UV key, and another device's key is refused;
  - disabling or wiping one device leaves the others' rows unchanged and still signing in;
  - registration touches only the registering row;
  - an old-shape row still loads.
- Unit tests for UV key enrolment, replacement and refusal.
- The proof-purpose classifier.
- The template and minted-document `assertionMethod` pins.

## Known follow-ups

- The browser session key (design §12.9) is not built.
- GeoIP is stubbed to "unknown".
- Existing VTCs need `dids edit` plus `cnm did-log install` to publish the new `TrustTaskHTTPS` and `SignInPortal` services.

## Related

- Companion VTC PR: https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1998.
- Browser plugin, which registers each install as a device before its first sign-in: https://github.com/OpenVTC/vta-browser-plugin/pull/305. It needs this PR deployed for sign-in to complete.
- https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-vti-spec/pull/58

## Backport

none

## Checklist

- [x] Targets `main`
- [x] No `version =` edits in any `Cargo.toml`
- [x] Tests cover the change; `cargo fmt` and `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` are clean

title: feat(vta-sdk)!: wallet sign-in with a trigger link: sign auth/oob grants, enrol UV keys, advertise TrustTaskHTTPS and SignInPortal (#1997)
body:
feat(vta-sdk)!: wallet sign-in with a trigger link: sign auth/oob grants, enrol UV keys, advertise TrustTaskHTTPS and SignInPortal (#1997)

* feat(vta-sdk)!: sign auth/oob/grant for assertionMethod (VTI-KEY-106)

Adds `auth/oob/grant` to `ATTESTATION_SLUGS`, so `vault/sign-trust-task`
signs a wallet sign-in grant for `assertionMethod`: the grant ("let this
browser key act as me at this origin until notAfter") is the approving
DID's attestation, which the service relies on to open a session, and it
verifies the grant against `assertionMethod` (sign-in trigger-link
contract C5, base design §10).

`auth/oob/identify` stays operational and is signed for `authentication`,
as the service verifies it; the other `auth/oob` documents are not
attestations either. Both are pinned in the classifier tests.

BREAKING CHANGE: `ATTESTATION_SLUGS` is now `[&str; 4]`.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(vti-common)!: enrol a device's user-verification key

A device enrols a UV key on `device/register`, and replaces it on
`device/heartbeat`, under the `org.openvtc.uv-key` extension (the
registry's device schemas are closed and have no UV-key member yet). Two
kinds (sign-in trigger-link contract C6, base design §5 and §11):

- `hardwareKey`: a Secure Enclave / StrongBox key as a P-256 (or Ed25519)
  `did:key`; it must be declared biometric-gated;
- `webauthn`: the browser plugin's passkey — credential id, P-256
  Multikey (the only algorithm vti-webauthn verifies), RP id and origin.

`hardwareBacked`, `biometricGated` and any platform attestation are
recorded as the device's claims (the attestation is stored, not yet
verified, like `device/register`'s own). A malformed key is refused
rather than ignored. A replacement is accepted only on heartbeat, whose
row is the caller's own, so only the device's transport key can write
it, and never for a disabled or wiped device. Enrolment and replacement
are audited; the binding reports a summary (kind and claims, not the key)
under `ext["org.openvtc"].uvKey`.

BREAKING CHANGE: `DeviceBinding` has a new `uv_key` field, and
`register_device` / `heartbeat_device` take new arguments.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(vta-service): default policy for wallet sign-in documents

`vault/sign-trust-task` now applies the key-grant sign-in design's
default VTA policy (base design §11; contract C5, C6, C9) to
`auth/oob/identify/0.1` and `auth/oob/grant/0.1`, whatever the
operator's policy set says:

- both: the exact Type URI (any other `auth/oob` document, version or
  variant is refused, never signed unattended), framework members only,
  a strict payload, an enrolled and active device as caller, `issuer` the
  entry's principal, `recipient` a DID the entry targets, and `issuedAt`
  within 300 s;
- identify: signed without user verification, for `authentication`;
- grant: signed for `assertionMethod` only with a `task-consent/decision`
  0.2 under `ext["org.openvtc.uv-consent"].decision` whose
  `payloadDigest` and `challenge` are the SHA-256 (JCS, multibase) of the
  unsigned grant, approved by the device's UV key — the hardware key's
  own proof, or the transport key's proof plus a WebAuthn assertion with
  UV over that challenge, verified with vti-webauthn; refused if the
  persona's locally hosted DID document does not list the signing key
  under `assertionMethod` (VTI-KEY-022); and never twice for one grant
  `id` (recorded in the task-consent keyspace after every check passes).

Every identify and grant signature is audited with the device, the
persona, the `requestId` and the UV decision; a signature whose audit
row cannot be written is withheld. Refusals are audited too.

The `auth/oob` payloads are local types until the registry publishes
them. The grant follows contract C9: `decision` is approve or decline,
`notAfter` is epoch seconds (RFC 3339 is also read), and `contextDigest`
a sha2-256 multihash in multibase.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* test: pin that minted DID documents list an assertionMethod key

A persona signs `auth/oob/grant` for `assertionMethod` (VTI-KEY-106) and a
service refuses a key not listed there (VTI-KEY-022). The default webvh
document builder and every built-in DID template already list one; these
tests keep it that way.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(vta-sdk): VTC DID documents advertise TrustTaskHTTPS and SignInPortal

A wallet signing in by trigger link takes the Trust Task endpoint and the
member portal's origin only from the VTC's verified DID document
(VTI-LNK-053, 102, 105). The vtc-host template now emits both:

- TrustTaskHTTPS: the full URL documents are POSTed to
  (TRUST_TASKS_PATH, default /v1/trust-tasks), never a base a client extends.
- SignInPortal: the member portal (SIGN_IN_PORTAL_PATH, default /members/).

Existing VTCs need a VTA-side `dids edit`, then `cnm did-log install`
where the VTC serves its own did.jsonl.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(vta-sdk): VTC TrustTaskHTTPS advertises the Trust-Task base, not the request URL

HTTPS binding 0.2 §6 makes a TrustTaskHTTPS serviceEndpoint the base and
the request URL <base>/trust-tasks. Every consumer composes it that way:
vti-common's push engine, vta-service outbound send_rest, vta-sdk's
ServiceCapabilities, the browser plugin and DID hosting, and the
did-host-http* templates publish {URL}/api. Publishing the full
/v1/trust-tasks URL would have sent those peers to
/v1/trust-tasks/trust-tasks.

The VTC now publishes {URL}{TRUST_TASKS_BASE}, with /v1 as the default, so
<base>/trust-tasks is the /v1/trust-tasks vtc-service serves.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* docs(vta-service): put the vault module doc comments back on their modules

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(vta-service): build the sign-in policy without the webvh feature

`AppState::webvh_ks` exists only with `webvh`, so `OobDeps` names it
under the same gate and the persona's assertionMethod check reads it
through the deps. Without `webvh` this VTA hosts no DID logs and the check
already left the document to the service.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(vta-service): wallet sign-in from any of a member's devices

Each of a member's devices (every browser install, every phone) is its
own DID with its own ACL entry, and its device binding, consumerKind, form
factor and UV key live on that entry. The auth/oob gate already checks the
caller's own row, and a grant's UV decision against that row's UV key and
the caller's own transport key. So multi-device needs no new data model:
disabling or wiping one device changes one row.

What changes:

- A disabled or wiped device is refused as oobDeviceDisabled, which is
  distinct from oobNotEnrolledDevice (no binding at all). A client can fix
  the second itself with device/register and must not try to fix the first.
  oobNotEnrolledDevice now names device/register in its message.
- OobError is #[non_exhaustive].
- The module doc says what "entry" and "principal" mean (the vault entry
  and its persona DID) and states the device model; register_device states
  that it writes only the caller's own row.

New tests cover one member with two browsers and a phone, each its own
context-scoped entry:

- each device signs with its own UV key, and another device's passkey,
  transport-key decision or hardware key is refused;
- disabling or wiping one device leaves the others' rows byte-identical
  and signing in;
- registration touches only the registering row;
- a pre-uvKey, pre-version ACL row written raw still loads, signs
  identify and enrols a passkey on heartbeat under its original deviceId.

No storage or wire-shape change. device/register/0.2 and heartbeat/0.2
behave exactly as before.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

---------

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

title: fix(vti-common): pooled enclave storage with atomic multi-step operations
body:
Part A of the plan for #1951 (TEE `keys/sign` throughput), reworked so the VTA's security improves rather than regresses.

## Kept from #1951 (Carlos Rincon, cherry-picked with `-x`)
- **Connection pool** for the enclave's vsock storage (up to 8), including the fix for a cancelled request leaving its response for the next caller.
- **One write per request frame.**

## Added
- **Atomic multi-step operations in the enclave store.** `take_raw` (the refresh-token claim), `insert_if_absent`, `insert_raw_if_absent`, `swap` and `move_if_unchanged` now hold per-key striped locks across their round trips, shared by every handle from one `VsockStore`. On `main` these were non-atomic and only safe because I/O was serial; #1951's pool and multi-thread REST would have made double-claims easy (review finding 1). Now they're atomic regardless — **stronger than `main`**.
- The "single-replica TEE deployments are unaffected in practice" warnings and caveats are gone, because the gap is.

## Tests
- `store::vsock::atomicity_tests`: each operation 32-wide on a 4-worker multi-thread runtime against a fake parent speaking the real wire protocol (3 ms per request) — exactly one winner each. A control test proves the harness catches the old unlocked read-then-delete (>1 winner).
- `store::key_locks::tests`: exclusion, no self-deadlock on a shared stripe, no deadlock for crossed two-key operations.
- `cargo test -p vti-common --features vsock-store,encryption --lib store::` → 123 passed. Clippy clean with and without `vsock-store`.
- CI: new step in the Enclave job runs these (nothing else compiles `vsock-store`).

## Follow-ups (same plan)
C (multi-thread REST + direct vsock inbound) builds on this. E1 adds native `TAKE` / `INSERT_IF_ABSENT` / `CAS` opcodes to the parent proxy to cut these to one round trip each.

## Backport
none

title: fix(vti-common): pooled enclave storage with atomic multi-step operations (#1999)
body:
fix(vti-common): pooled enclave storage with atomic multi-step operations (#1999)

* fix(vti-common): pool the enclave's vsock storage connections

Inside a Nitro enclave every storage operation went through one vsock
connection behind one mutex held for the whole round trip, so all storage
I/O in the VTA ran strictly one operation at a time. Throughput of anything
that touches storage was capped by the round-trip time, whatever the
enclave's vCPU count: a keys/sign costs about ten round trips, and load
tests saw the same ceiling (about 85 signs/s) with one and with two enclave
vCPUs, with neither the enclave nor the parent CPU saturated.

VsockStore now keeps a bounded pool of connections (up to 8). A request
owns a connection for one complete round trip and returns it only after a
full response; the parent's storage proxy already serves each connection in
its own task, so independent operations now run in parallel. Each
operation is still a single request, and the multi-step operations (swap,
take_raw, move_if_unchanged) are no less atomic than before: the old lock
was released between their steps too.

This also fixes a latent correctness bug. The old code kept the shared
connection after a cancelled request: if a request future was dropped
after writing its request but before reading the response (a request
timeout, a client disconnect), the next caller read the previous caller's
response. A pooled connection that fails or is cancelled mid-round-trip is
dropped instead of reused.

The pool is transport-agnostic and compiled under `test` as well as
`vsock-store`, so its tests run on every platform, not only Linux.

Signed-off-by: Carlos Rincon <carlos.r@affinidi.com>
(cherry picked from commit e24a09c841913f6d0981668860012b13002739df)
Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* perf(vti-common): send each vsock storage request in one write

A storage request was written as two writes, the 4-byte length and then the
payload. On an unbuffered vsock stream each write is its own packet across
the enclave boundary, so every request cost two. The frame is now built in
one buffer and written once.

Measured alone on c6g.4xlarge with a 2-vCPU enclave, in builds with extra
timing logging: saturation about 245 -> 255 keys/sign per second, p95 at
235/s 600 -> 66 ms.
Replies from the parent are still written in two parts; changing that is a
change to the parent's proxy.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Carlos Rincon <carlos.r@affinidi.com>
(cherry picked from commit bace8cec27a01fa905aaaa463ccffc9699b1d98a)
Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(vti-common): make the enclave store's multi-step operations atomic

The parent's storage proxy serves single operations, so the vsock store
ran take_raw, insert_if_absent, swap and move_if_unchanged as sequences of
round trips with nothing excluding a second caller. Two presenters of one
refresh token could both read it before either deleted it and both rotate,
defeating reuse detection (RFC 9700 §4.14.2). The gap was documented as
"single-replica TEE deployments are unaffected in practice", which held
only while one mutex-guarded connection and a single REST thread kept the
steps from overlapping; a connection pool and a multi-thread REST runtime
remove both.

Per-key striped locks (store::key_locks), shared by every handle a
VsockStore hands out, are held across each multi-step operation; two-key
operations take both in stripe order, so crossed swaps cannot deadlock.
This is the local store's guarantee (two multi-step operations on one key
never interleave), per key rather than per keyspace because a vsock round
trip is long. It does not depend on the parent: the enclave is the only
writer to its store.

Tests run each operation 32-wide on a multi-thread runtime against a fake
parent that serves the wire protocol with a delay per request, and assert
exactly one winner; a control test shows the same harness catching the old
unlocked read-then-delete. CI runs them in the Enclave job (they are
behind vsock-store, which no other job compiles).

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* perf(vti-common): coalesce only small storage frames

One write per frame keeps a small request to one vsock packet, but copying
a frame near the 16 MB limit just to prepend its length doubles peak memory
for a saving that does not exist: a frame that size spans many packets
anyway. Coalesce up to 64 KiB; above that, write the header and the payload
separately.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(vti-common): bound every enclave storage round trip

A parent that accepts a frame and never answers held that request's pool
permit, and for a multi-step operation its key lock, with no end: eight
such requests and every storage operation in the enclave blocks. Each
round trip now has a 10 s deadline (the parent answers in tens of
microseconds); on expiry the request fails and the connection is dropped,
never reused, since its next bytes could be the late answer.

This is also what keeps key_locks within the intent of R1.3 (no lock
across an await): the locks are held across awaits by design, and every
such await is now bounded.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

---------

Signed-off-by: Carlos Rincon <carlos.r@affinidi.com>
Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>
Co-authored-by: Carlos Rincon <carlos.r@affinidi.com>
Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
